530073|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39% YoY to Rs 380 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 35% (from 40% in Q4 FY26) on credit provisions and one-time items.
530073|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 380 crore (+39% YoY, +Rs 29 crore QoQ), with EBITDA of Rs 139 crore (+30% YoY) at a 35% margin versus 40% in Q4 FY26. Core crane rental EBITDA margin fell to 47% from 53% in FY26; management attributed about 6 points to ECL provisions on aged receivables (~Rs 6.2 crore), FX mark-to-market (Rs 1.4 crore), a one-time employee incentive, and revenue-mix shifts to ancillary equipment and cross-rental. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 1,400-1,500 crore revenue and Rs 525-575 crore EBITDA, with the bulk of the Rs 652 crore capex pool deploying in H2.

financial_highlights.change: +39% YoY; +Rs 29 crore vs Q4 FY26 (Rs 350 crore)
+30% YoY vs Rs 107 crore; down from Rs 143 crore in Q4 FY26
+30% YoY vs Rs 50 crore; Rs 69 crore in Q4 FY26
vs 53% in FY26; ~49% underlying excluding FX and incentive
Crane rental 124 days, renewable E&C 98 days, GCC 201 days

segments.name: Crane rental (India + Botswana)
segments.commentary: Utilisation ~86% at a 2.29% yield; contributes ~60% of revenue from operations. Fleet of 492 cranes, gross block ~Rs 3,300 crore.

segments.name: GCC (Saudi Arabia, Qatar)
segments.commentary: Utilisation ~86% at a 4.10% yield; total income Rs 19 crore at 23% EBITDA margin; Saudi operation cumulatively EBITDA positive. Management cites ~47% EBITDA margin for KSA crane rental. DSO 201 days.

segments.name: Renewable E&C (Sangreen Future Renewable)
segments.commentary: Contributes ~37% of revenue, ahead of full-year mix on execution phasing. Wind E&C EBITDA margin 18% before unallocated costs (10-12% after). Order book ~Rs 680-686 crore.

segments.name: Project EPC
segments.commentary: Balance ~3% of revenue from operations.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 1,400-1,500 crore, EBITDA Rs 525-575 crore (unchanged); blended return on capital 16.25-16.5%.
FY27 EBITDA growth of 20-30% on FY26 EBITDA of Rs 429 crore; blended margin expected to be lower.
FY28 guidance: revenue growth 30-40% and EBITDA growth 20-30% (EBITDA Rs 650-700 crore).
Credit provision expected to normalise over FY27 as aged receivables are recovered; management expects ~15% revenue uplift in FY27 from the capex.
Debt-to-equity guided at 0.72x on a gross consolidated basis; management cites treasury surplus of over Rs 300 crore, implying net 0.3-0.7x.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex pool of Rs 652 crore approved by the board; Rs 92 crore capitalised in Q1, balance in H2 FY27.
Of the capex, ~Rs 324 crore is for the Middle East (Rs 316 crore revenue-generating), with orders placed with OEMs; revenue contribution expected between Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Fleet 492 cranes; management declined to disclose incremental lifting capacity.
Cross-rental and ancillary equipment used in Q1 to meet demand without fresh capex (lower margin, no capital consumed).
Plans to add a depot in KSA and/or Qatar; location and timing not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Order book ~Rs 1,250 crore for the group, stated as fully executable within FY27; inquiry pipeline ~Rs 5,600 crore (Rs 4,656 crore for E&C).
Renewable E&C order book ~Rs 686 crore, already above FY26 renewable revenue; management expects ~15% of that book may slip into FY28.
KSA 0-12 month executable inquiry pipeline ~$22 million; zero-to-24-month Middle East pipeline ~$38 million.
Management says yields in India have improved over the last quarter and are not being capped by competition; no material change in client tenure or rate-reset behaviour.
Wind industry: 6 GW added last year, ~29 GW under construction; thermal 62 GW under bid or award.

qa_highlights.question: Where would an incremental crane go, India or KSA, and what drives the decision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said allocation depends on inquiry pipeline, order visibility and duration, market-share needs and internal IRR hurdle, with group ROCE as the anchor.

qa_highlights.question: Will the blended margin fall as renewables reach one-third of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sangreen is asset-light with lower margin; blended margin will be lower but absolute EBITDA is up, with FY27 EBITDA guided at Rs 525-575 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 0.72x debt-to-equity imply debt of Rs 1,000-1,100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 0.72x a gross consolidated ceiling, said it is comfortable, and noted a treasury surplus of over Rs 300 crore; net D/E estimated at 0.3-0.7x.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ECL provision one-time and is it India-only?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly India, nothing from KSA; management expects normalisation over FY27 as aged debtors are recovered, with a Rs 3-4 crore reversal from Q4 to Q1 cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the E&C margin outlook, and is 18% wind E&C margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: The 18% is before unallocated costs (10-12% after); management guides E&C to settle at 12-15%, with slippage risk from client-side delays and POCM revenue recognition.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GCC DSO 201 days, and when will it fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to West Asia disruption; management said significant collections occurred in July, with improvement visible in Q2 results, and zero working-capital draw in KSA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for GCC capex and is supply delayed by West Asia conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply chain disruption is temporary, orders are placed with OEMs, and Rs 316 crore of revenue-generating capex should come online between Q3 and Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost and currency terms of new borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: India INR debt at around 8% (plus or minus 0.25%); overseas USD debt at SOFR plus 5.5-6%. Blended cost to be disclosed at half-year.

risks_watch: Credit provisions: ECL charge of ~Rs 6.2 crore on aged receivables (mostly India) is expected to normalise over FY27; track whether provisions actually fall and collections recover in Q2.
GCC/KSA working capital: DSO of 201 days with West Asia disruption cited; management says significant July collections and DSO improvement will show in Q2 results, so verify.

Capex execution: Rs 652 crore pool with bulk deploying in H2 FY27; Rs 316 crore Middle East revenue-generating capex expected Q3-Q4 FY27 despite supply-chain disruption; watch OEM delivery and commissioning dates.

Renewable E&C margins and execution: wind E&C margin 18% before unallocated costs (10-12% after); guided to 12-15%; ~15% of Rs 686 crore order book may slip into FY28 on client delays and POCM revenue recognition.

Blended margin dilution as Sangreen grows toward one-third of revenue; FY27 EBITDA guided Rs 525-575 crore, and debt-to-equity of 0.72x gross ceiling (management says net 0.3-0.7x) with cost of debt and blended borrowing cost not disclosed until half-year.
key_quotes: So, overall, we grew the top line and gave back margin and that is the real outcome.
So, Saudi is not a response to India and India is not a response to Saudi Arabia.
So, the ECL provision is expected to normalize in the course of the financial year as we recover debtors which has basically aged.
And we believe that the entirety of this CAPEX should come offline in terms of revenue generation between the third and fourth quarter of this financial year.
530073|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on demand, KSA, and the Rs 1,250 crore order book, but candid and somewhat defensive on margin, explaining the 6-point core crane margin drop as ECL, FX, a one-time incentive and mix. Management was evasive on lifting capacity, the blended cost of borrowing, and the specifics of E&C margin sustainability, deflecting several questions.

rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at Rs 1,400-1,500 cr (~20% growth at midpoint), backed by a Rs 1,250 cr executable group order book and a KSA 0-12 month pipeline of ~$22 mn, with crane utilisation at ~86%.

530075|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 EBITDA rose to Rs.90 crore (about 71% margin, Rs.83 crore or 69% ex one-off) on flat volumes; exit guidance 2,500 BOEPD, 5,000 BOPD by FY29.
530075|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs.121.7 crore and net profit of Rs.57.3 crore, with volumes flat QoQ and realised oil down to $88.2/bbl from $95.3/bbl. Management reiterated a 2,500 BOEPD exit for FY27 and 3,500 BOEPD next year, with 5,000 BOPD targeted by FY29 on onshore assets only. The company signed two KG Onshore and Cambay Basin revenue sharing contracts (DSF IV) on 22 October 2026. Bakrol's 10-well campaign is complete, Karjisan's seven-well campaign is under way, and October production was about 2,000 BOEPD. Balance sheet is debt-free with about Rs.100 crore cash and liquid investments and Rs.780 crore equity.

segments.name: Cambay Basin (Bakrol, Karjisan, Lohar, Cambay)
segments.commentary: Bakrol average about 950 BOE/d in October after the 10-well drilling and fracking campaign; Karjisan (PSC, royalty and cess under 5% of top line) has seven wells planned this fiscal, two drilled but not yet on production. Cambay field (50% JV with Synergia) has one to two optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027.

segments.name: KG Onshore
segments.commentary: Seven new discoveries added, about nine fields in total, of which only Mukkamala is producing; management says resource base may be larger than the offshore portfolio. Single-rig, multi-well appraisal planned; a resource estimate to follow after third-party reserve work. Wells expected to cost about $10 million more than Cambay's roughly $1.5 million.

segments.name: Duarmara (Assam, JV)
segments.commentary: Duarmara-4Z found oil in the TIPAM-1 zone rather than the expected gas; oil recirculated to surface twice. Well cost about Rs.60-70 crore, and a plan covering wells 1, 2 and 4 is due over the next five to six months. Gas monetisation is constrained by Assam's lack of National Grid connection.

segments.name: Offshore
segments.commentary: Treated as optionality; excluded from the 5,000 BOPD guidance, with management focus shifting to it in FY28-29.

guidance_outlook: Exit FY27 at about 2,500 BOEPD, with Karjisan's seven wells and the Cambay optionality wells as the main drivers; October production was about 2,000 BOEPD (one answer cited about 1,950).
Exit FY28 at about 3,500 BOEPD and FY29 at about 5,000 BOEPD, onshore only; minimal contribution assumed from KG and Duarmara.
EBITDA margin expected to stay above 65% for the year; management says its endeavour is to keep margins in line.
Capex guided at Rs.250 crore for FY27 (against Rs.220 crore in FY26), with funding via internal accruals for now; no commitment on debt or equity raises.
KG Onshore development plan and capex guidance to come after field development plans are filed with regulators; Duarmara oil plan in five to six months.
capex_capacity: Bakrol 10-well campaign complete (drilling and fracking); production response showing Bakrol as a multi-year growth field.
Karjisan: seven wells planned for FY27; two drilled, first perforation expected within about a week, rig back on site.
Cambay field: one to two optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027; field area about 160 sq km.
Duarmara: well cost Rs.60-70 crore; TIPAM-1 oil zone; partner alignment needed.
Historical capex: Rs.51 crore (FY23), Rs.160 crore (FY24), Rs.87 crore (FY25), Rs.220 crore (FY26), Rs.250 crore (FY27 target).
demand_pricing: Pricing is linked to international crude benchmarks; Cambay crude sells at about a 10% discount to dated Brent on average, with most volumes to Indian Oil and about 20% to private buyers at a slightly higher discount.
Realised oil ran about $76 in July, $84 in August and above $100 in September.
Royalty and cess are about 30% of top line in Bakrol and Cambay versus under 5% in Karjisan, averaging about 15-16% of revenue.
Variable handling cost is about $1-1.5 per barrel on ONGC tolling; fixed costs are about 70-75% of the cost base.
Management's investment hurdle: double-digit returns at $65-70/bbl, cash back within one to one-and-a-half years, and no loss at $50/bbl.
Assam gas is sold at a discount to APM prices because Assam is not connected to the National Grid; oil is easier to truck out.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins above 65% be sustained for the full year as costs stay flat while volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed costs are 70-75% of the cost base and incremental barrels are cheaper in Cambay; KG will add establishment costs, but margins should hold. Management's stated aim is to keep margins in line, not a firm guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental revenue will Karjisan and Bakrol add, and does the 2,500 exit depend on Cambay?
qa_highlights.answer: Bakrol is at about 950 BOE/d. Karjisan's seven wells are already in the 2,500 exit figure, which management said has no ambiguity; Cambay optionality wells sit outside it and could take production beyond 5,000.

qa_highlights.question: How will KG Onshore be funded and ramped up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to decide between internal accruals, debt or equity; it will start with one rig, drill a couple of wells and then decide on a bigger campaign. Wells cost about $10 million more than Cambay wells.

qa_highlights.question: What pricing formula and price range should be used for sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is set by a crude-yield-based discount to dated Brent (about 10%), and investments are screened at $50-70/bbl. Management gave no explicit bear-to-bull range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Duarmara oil potential, capex per well and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Well cost Rs.60-70 crore with 3.5 km wells. Oil is light, and flow and frac options are being studied. A concrete estimate is expected next fiscal, not this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CWIP high and why are deferred tax liabilities rising?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs.100 crore of the Rs.190 crore CWIP is Duarmara, to be capitalised on production. Deferred tax is rising because drilling capex is fully expensed for tax; it may partly reverse if drilling slows.

risks_watch: Duarmara gas evacuation and oil development path are unresolved, with the TIPAM-1 oil zone yet to be tested and the JV partner to be aligned.
KG Onshore high-pressure, high-temperature wells cost about $10 million more each; no resource or reserve estimate yet.
Karjisan's seven wells and the Cambay optionality wells (with Synergia) need to deliver to reach 2,500 BOEPD exit and 5,000 BOPD by FY29.
Realisations are sensitive to crude; September's above-$100 prices lifted the average, and private buyers' purchasing has been limited at higher prices.
Growing deferred tax liability and the chance of a funding decision (debt or equity) once KG ramps up.
Management's first investor call; one-off Rs.6.5 crore refund included in other income.
530075|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on the Cambay ramp-up, with a clear 2,500 BOEPD exit and 5,000 BOPD FY29 target. Cautious and deliberately vague on KG Onshore, Duarmara and offshore, explicitly declining to give capex, reserve or funding numbers beyond the onshore guidance.
key_quotes: So, at $65-$70, if a project gives me double-digit return and gets me back my cash within year to year and a half, that is a go project for me.
Karjisan has the best fiscals in our portfolio as of today, because it has concessional Cess and royalty rates to it, because it is still in its primary term as a production-sharing contract.
So, the 5000 barrel plant that you have has a very subdued KG or the Cambay optionality in it.
Oil does not need pipeline infrastructure. Oil I can just put into a truck to haul across 300 kilometers and sell to refiner somewhere, right?

financial_highlights.change: flat volumes QoQ; Q1 not stated

financial_highlights.value: Rs.90 crore (71% margin); Rs.83 crore (about 69%) excluding Rs.6.5 crore one-off refund

rose as new Bakrol wells came into production
nearly 5x vs Rs.11.8 crore in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.value: about 1,700 BOEPD production, revenue about Rs.254.8 crore, EBITDA about Rs.180 crore, net profit about Rs.112 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Cash, bank balances and liquid investments

financial_highlights.value: about Rs.190 crore, of which about Rs.100 crore is Duarmara

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin above 65% for FY27 (Q2 at 71%, or 69% ex Rs.6.5 crore one-off), with fixed costs at 70-75% of the cost base and incremental Cambay barrels cheaper, though it is an aim, not a firm guarantee and KG will add establishment costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Exit FY27 at about 2,500 BOEPD from October run-rate of about 2,000 BOEPD, driven by Karjisan's seven wells (two drilled, first perforation within about a week) and Cambay optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027; the 2,500 exit already includes Karjisan but not Cambay optionality.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volumes rose from about 1,700 BOEPD H1 average toward the 2,000 BOEPD October run-rate and a 2,500 BOEPD FY27 exit, but Q2 volumes were flat QoQ and the ramp depends on wells not yet producing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is already guided at Rs.250 crore (up from Rs.220 crore), and KG Onshore development capex and a Duarmara oil plan (Rs.60-70 crore per well) will follow in five to six months or after field development plans are filed, but no figures are committed yet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was held (2,500 BOEPD FY27 exit, 5,000 BOPD FY29), and October production of about 2,000 BOEPD plus Bakrol's 950 BOE/d and Karjisan's wells leave room, but realisations fell to $88.2/bbl from $95.3/bbl and September's above-$100 price lifted the average.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Exit and FY29 targets depend on Karjisan wells and Cambay optionality wells being delivered, and realisations are crude-sensitive (July about $76, August $84, September above $100), with private buyers limiting purchases at higher prices.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: KG Onshore (seven new discoveries, about nine fields, only Mukkamala producing) and Duarmara oil (TIPAM-1 zone) could add new production, but KG resource estimates and Duarmara plans are not due for several months and minimal KG/Duarmara contribution is assumed for FY28-29.

rows.label: Two KG Onshore and Cambay DSF IV revenue sharing contracts signed
rows.why: Two revenue sharing contracts (KG Onshore and Cambay Basin, DSF IV) were signed on 22 October 2026, adding acreage that supports the onshore growth story.

rows.label: Debt-free balance sheet with cash buffer for capex
rows.why: No borrowings and about Rs.100 crore cash and liquid investments against Rs.250 crore FY27 capex funded from internal accruals for now, though a debt or equity decision is possible once KG ramps up.

rows.label: Assam gas monetisation constrained by no National Grid link
rows.why: Assam gas sells at a discount to APM prices because Assam is not connected to the National Grid, so Duarmara's gas contribution is unlikely to add near-term revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Cambay and Karjisan ramp to a 2,500 BOEPD exit and held FY29 5,000 BOPD, but was cautious and vague on KG Onshore, Duarmara and offshore funding and capex; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, KG funding, and the crude sensitivity of realisations.

530117|2026-03.headline: Privi FY26 revenue rose 21.7% to INR2,582.9 crore and PAT 75% to INR327.5 crore, with a 25.76% EBITDA margin.
530117|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR725.70 crore (up 15.29% YoY), EBITDA INR184.41 crore (up 25.09%) at a 25.41% margin, and PAT INR95.66 crore versus INR63.57 crore a year earlier. For FY26, income grew 21.73% to INR2,582.92 crore, driven by about 6.5% volume growth, roughly 8% price increases and product mix. Management reiterated a 20%+ growth target and 20%+ EBITDA margins, with the first capex phase due by 30 June 2026 taking installed capacity to 54,000 MTPA. The PRIGIV JV turned profitable for the first time in Q4, and the merger with PFSPL and PBPL awaits NCLT approval.

segments.name: Standalone aroma chemicals (core)
segments.commentary: Management said demand for core aroma chemicals is steady, with about 70% of revenue from exports, mostly under contracts. Realisations rose from about INR450/kg to about INR600/kg over five years, per management.

segments.name: PRIGIV JV (with Givaudan, 51:49)
segments.commentary: Turned profitable in Q4 FY26 for the first time. Revenue is expected at about INR130 crore in FY27 versus INR55 crore last year, with an additional INR50 crore capex. It manufactures high-end specialty chemicals exclusively for Givaudan.

segments.name: Downstream / new specialty molecules
segments.commentary: Silver Amber, Amber Silk, Privilege and Privitolide are in commissioning, with one already commissioned. Ethyl maltol, maltol and cyclopentanone projects target mechanical completion by June 2027, with revenue expected over the next 18 months. Furfural backward integration is about 2 years away, and the vertical is said to reach about INR1,000 crore revenue.

guidance_outlook: Targets 20%+ revenue growth for the coming year on a standalone basis; the 20% excludes merged entities until the scheme is effective.
Expects to sustain 20%+ EBITDA margins going forward; one answer referenced a 24% margin and another 25%.
Long-term target of about INR5,000 crore revenue and INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA in 3 to 4 years, roughly 2x.
Post all three capex phases, standalone capacity is expected at about 72,000 MT, around mid-to-late 2028.
Expects the NCLT approval for the merger of PFSPL and PBPL into the parent during FY27, internally targeted for Q3 FY27.
Expects state incentives of about INR13 crore a year, based on 50% of the GST on in-state sales in Gujarat and Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: First capex phase to complete by 30 June 2026, taking installed capacity to 54,000 MTPA, with a calibrated ramp-up over the coming quarters.
Phase 2 of the multi-specialty aroma chemicals project is progressing as planned.

The three new-molecule projects (ethyl maltol, maltol, cyclopentanone) are in detailed engineering with procurement started; the 12 to 15 month build targets mechanical completion by June 2027, followed by about one month of trials.
A biomass-to-value-added-products demonstration plant with capex of about INR70-75 crore is in basic and detailed engineering, expected in about 12 months.
Furfural backward integration is expected around FY28-29, after first establishing the finished goods and sourcing furfural from outside in the meantime.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil attributed it to the timing overlap of annual raw-material and finished-goods contracts, which fall into Q4 and Q1, and said the business should be judged on an annual basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth guidance inclusive of the proposed merged entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said the 20% is standalone as it stands today; the merged entities will be consolidated once the scheme takes effect.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital days rise amid the current situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Babani said any increase would be no more than 3-5%, because price rises tend to lengthen customer payment times.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the FY26 forex gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said forex gains of about INR14 crore were recorded in other income, as the company is a net exporter.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net-capacity and commissioning timelines after all three phases?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said about 72,000 MT standalone after the first three phases, with completion around June to September 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Can standalone EBITDA margins of 27-28% be reached at the consolidated level?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said consolidated margins should improve now that PRIGIV has turned profitable, but gave no level.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross margin improve next year given crude-linked input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil said the company will assume gross margin stays at a similar level, and that any upside will come from internal efficiency gains.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in other expenses and power costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil credited the ProMax residual steam and power-saving programme and better freight and logistics contract pricing, per Narayan Iyer.

risks_watch: Crude-linked and West Asia disruption could raise freight, fuel and raw-material costs. Management said shipping may be delayed by a week or two, but stock cover is in place.
Q4 gross margin dip, which management attributed to contract timing; watch whether it reverses in Q1 FY27.
Execution risk on the 54,000 MT capacity ramp-up after 30 June 2026 and on the 2028 target of about 72,000 MT.
The NCLT approval timing for the merger (internally targeted for Q3 FY27) and its effect on consolidated numbers.
Demand for the new molecules at lower price points (for example about $45/kg); management is still testing market elasticity.
Biotech demonstration plant economics and capex, which management called complex and still at engineering stage.
530117|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term 5k story and margin sustainability, but cautious on biotech economics and on new-molecule pricing. Management deflected several questions on customer names and pipeline partners, citing confidentiality.
key_quotes: We have delivered 25% plus margins consistently across all quarters and for the FY 26 on the EBITDA numbers.
So we are covered for almost a quarter for regular raw material, which are contracted.
We are definitely likely to get there, because as I said, one of the key parameters there is what kind of products you are making.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR63.57 crore in Q4 FY25

demand_pricing: Management said demand for fragrance and flavour ingredients keeps growing, and that customers want reliable, compliant, non-China suppliers.
FY26 growth split: about 6.5% from volume, about 8% from price, and the balance from product mix.
Management said it expects to pass on raw-material-driven price increases, citing customer trust and a 1-2% price premium for supplier reliability.

Raw-material cover: renewable inputs under annual contracts have about 1 to 1.5 months of inventory plus about 1 month in transit. Other inputs have about 3 months in stock and 2 to 3 months in pipeline.
Management said about 70% of raw materials are imported, which partly offsets rupee-driven realisation gains.
Management said it is in discussions with other MNC partners but is too early to disclose.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY26 EBITDA margin rose to 25.76% from 22.35%, PRIGIV turned profitable in Q4 and the ProMax steam and power savings and freight contract pricing are cutting costs, yet management only commits to sustaining 20%+ and assumes gross margin stays flat.

530117|2026-06.headline: Privi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.22% YoY to Rs 666 crore; consolidated EBITDA Rs 167.47 crore at 24.58% margin, PAT Rs 83.2 crore.
530117|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 consolidated total income of Rs 681.42 crore (+20.01% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 167.47 crore (+18.73% YoY) at about 24.58% margin, and PAT of about Rs 83.2 crore versus Rs 61.46 crore a year earlier. Growth was attributed to volume, price and product mix. Phase-1 capacity expansion (48,000 to 54,000 MT) is slated to commercialise within about 15 days, while the Phase-2 completion timeline has slipped to September 2027 for the final 12,000 MT. Gross margin compression (about 650 bps YoY per an analyst) was explained as a base effect from low-cost raw materials in CY25 and a normalising RM/sales ratio of 52-55%.

segments.name: Camphor
segments.commentary: Management says camphor is about 4-6% of revenue (figures given as 5-6% and 4-5%), made via CST route; not treated as a strategic product.

guidance_outlook: Rs 5,000 crore revenue and Rs 1,000 crore+ EBITDA target reiterated, over three to four years (about 2x); management said no change in guidance.
Chairman: targeting ~20% CAGR with similar EBITDA margins, benchmarked off prior-year numbers.
EBITDA margin expected around 24.6% to nearer 25% going forward; RM/sales guided at 52-54%.
New specialty and furfural-based (Maltol, Ethyl Maltol, Cyclopentanone, Musk T) plants mechanically complete by about mid-FY28 with contributions from H2 FY28.
Privi Speciality / Privi Fine Sciences / Privi Biotechnologies merger: scheme filed with NCLT; completion expected this financial year (by FY27 year-end).
capex_capacity: Phase-1: capacity from 48,000 to 54,000 MT of existing products, expected to commercialise in about 15 days from the call; earlier 6,000 MT tranche slipped from June 2026 to September 2026.
Phase-2: additional 12,000 MT (54,000 to 66,000 MT) to be completed by September 2027; Phase-2 has commenced.
Phase-3 (multi-specialty aroma) expected to start around end-2026 or early 2027; funding mainly internal accruals with bank borrowing as needed.
Capex outlook for FY27 and next two years: Rs 850-900 crore, covering Phase-2 and Phase-3.
Post-merger, about 6,000 MT of Privi Fine Sciences capacity to be added to Privi portfolio. Utilisation at around 90% of installed capacity.
Demonstration plant in Navi Mumbai for 2 TPD biomass processing; 12-15 months to build, then about a year of operation before a large-scale plant (outside the 5K/1K plan).
demand_pricing: Demand described as healthy across fragrance and flavour value chain despite global headwinds; customers diversifying supply chains.
Growth attributed to volume, price increases and product mix; no quarterly volume/realisation split given (to be disclosed annually).
Crude-based raw materials ~15-18% of purchases; alpha-pinene from GTO at historic highs, but CST purchases are back-to-back with customers.
Management claims Iran war and Hormuz freight impact limited; Red Sea freight impact seen as ongoing for years with no margin concern.
Maltol and Ethyl Maltol >95% manufactured in China; Privi targets about one-quarter of global opportunity, with Ethyl Maltol demand from Indian pharma importers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall ~650 bps YoY to ~44.2% and what recovers in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited low-cost RM and high CY25 selling prices in the prior-year base; RM/sales guided at 52-55% on average. Management expects EBITDA margin near 24.6-25% via scale benefits and lower depreciation and interest.

qa_highlights.question: Phase-2 capacity date: June or September 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Clarified: the 6,000 MT Phase-1 tranche moved from June 2026 to September 2026; the 12,000 MT Phase-2 balance completes by September 2027. Guidance unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue from PRIGIV and its EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: PRIGIV revenue about Rs 18 crore in Q1 with EBITDA margin of about 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Alpha-pinene price rise impact?
qa_highlights.answer: CST purchases are back-to-back with customers; balance GTO-based alpha-pinene is at historic highs and costs are being passed on. Future direction not predicted.

qa_highlights.question: Phase-2/3 funding and debt levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily internal accruals, with bank borrowing as needed; debt/EBITDA and debt/equity to stay well below typical thresholds.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for this year and next two years, and new 5K/1K plan products?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex Rs 850-900 crore over this year and the next two. Furfural-based chemistry (about Rs 1,000 crore+ revenue), Musk T and about 10-11 specialty molecules; plants mechanically complete by mid-FY28.

risks_watch: Phase-1 and Phase-2 timelines have already slipped; Phase-2 completion now September 2027 versus earlier June 2027 reference in annual report.
Gross margin compression (~650 bps YoY) and raw material mix volatility, with management attributing to base effects.

Merger completion (NCLT approval) and strategic alliances not yet disclosed in detail.
Management declined to disclose product-level split and quarterly volume/price breakdown.

530117|2026-09.headline: Privi Q2 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% to INR773.16 crore and EBITDA 16.7% to INR212.49 crore, with a 27.48% EBITDA margin and first-ever interim dividend of INR5 per share.
530117|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly total income of INR773.16 crore (up 13.9% YoY), EBITDA of INR212.49 crore (up 16.66%) and PAT of INR117.03 crore (up 24.61%). H1 PAT was INR201 crore, up about 29%. Phase 1 capacity expansion (48,000 to 54,000 MTPA) was completed as of 30 September 2026, with Phase 2 and Phase 3 capex still in progress. Management reiterated 20% annual growth and a path to INR5,000 crore revenue by 2030, but H1 volume growth was only about 7-7.5% and Q2 volume growth about 4%.

segments.name: PRIGIV (JV with Jeevadan)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 sales about INR28 crore with PBT close to INR2 crore; H1 sales about INR47 crore with negligible loss of about INR0.02 lakh. Management guided JV revenue of about INR225 crore for FY27-28 from two expansion phases; a third phase is in pilot.

segments.name: Privi Fine Sciences / Privi Biotechnology (merger pending)
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR68 crore with loss of about INR34 crore. Capacity of about 6,000 MTPA is in place but utilisation is held back by pending regulatory and pollution board approvals; management sees potential revenue of INR300-350 crore at full utilisation.

guidance_outlook: Management maintains 20% growth guidance for FY27 on an annual basis, despite H1 growth of about 15%; it expects H2 to be stronger than H1.
FY27-28 revenue expected close to INR3,750-4,000 crore with 20% growth maintained or exceeded; EBITDA margin to be held at current levels.

Phase 2 (furfural-based derivatives: maltol, ethyl maltol, cyclopentanone and specialty molecules, about 12,000 MTPA) to be completed June-September 2027, with revenue from October 2027; target about INR1,000 crore revenue at full capacity.

Q4 volume growth expected as annual contracts start, with 85-90% utilisation on expanded capacity.

PRIGIV capacity expansion underway in two phases; a third phase is being evaluated through pilot studies with guidance to follow in 3-6 months.
demand_pricing: Management says aroma chemical usage is rising, citing new applications for pinene and African market growth through customers, but gave no segment-level growth guidance.
Freight: contracts now include quarterly freight pricing pass-through mechanism; management says freight disruption has been less severe for Privi than peers.

Raw materials: about 70% of revenue from non-petroleum feedstock; management sees no significant impact from West Asia conflict. Procurement of CST/GTO imports reported as diversified with no supply constraints.
RMC (raw material cost) at about 52% of sales in Q2 FY27, vs 54% in Q1 FY27 and 51% in Q2 FY26; expenses at 9.72% of sales.
Customer response to next-year contracts described as positive; first customer indications point to higher purchases, but no specifics were disclosed.
Q2 volume growth about 4% YoY; H1 volume growth about 7-7.5% YoY, with the balance of revenue growth from price/mix.

qa_highlights.question: Has the debottlenecking capacity commissioned by September 2026 started ramping, and what is utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil said expansion is complete, with part of volumes in Q3 and most in Q4 when annual contracts start; utilisation on expanded capacity is expected at 85-90%.

qa_highlights.question: Does management still hold 20% growth guidance when H1 grew about 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer confirmed 20% annual growth guidance, saying H1 is normally lower than H2 and investors should look at yearly numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin look flat ex-other income, and when were incentives received?
qa_highlights.answer: Iyer said incentives were INR1.62 crore in H1 FY27 vs INR9 crore last year, with INR12-15 crore expected in the next two quarters; margin held because fixed costs were spread over a larger base and RMC was about 52%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income high in Q1 and Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Iyer said it is mainly forex gains, as Privi is a net exporter and the dollar has favoured it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital trending down, and what is the long-term level?
qa_highlights.answer: Iyer said customers pay on time or early; cycle is below 100 days now and the long-term annual range is 105-110 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Privi Fine Sciences merger and its utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil said regulatory approvals are nearing completion; management expects the merger before FY-end. Utilisation is about 85%, but the expansion awaits pollution board permissions, and management expects revenue to rise from about INR100 crore toward INR250-300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue will the Phase 1-3 capex generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Iyer said Phase 2 could deliver about INR1,000 crore at full 12,000 MTPA capacity, Phase 3 (INR400-425 crore capex) about INR450-500 crore, with total about INR1,900 crore by 2030.

risks_watch: H1 volume growth of about 7-7.5% and Q2 volume growth of about 4% sit well below the 20% annual guidance; H2 must deliver a sharp acceleration.
Phase 2 and 3 timelines (June-September 2027 completion, about INR1,000 crore spend) depend on execution; capex is still largely ahead.
Privi Fine Sciences / Privi Biotechnology (merger, 6,000 MTPA plant) remains loss-making at about INR34 crore loss in FY26 and depends on pending pollution board and regulatory permissions.
PRIGIV deleveraging (debt conversion to advance with multinational partners) is in process but has no timeline.
Q2 margin benefited from the prior-year INR9 crore incentive base and forex gains in other income; underlying margin gains are harder to isolate.
Two strategic JV agreements remain unsigned; management gave no timeline.
Freight and geopolitical exposure; management says limited impact, but freight is passed through on a quarterly basis with a lag.

rows.why: Management expects the merger before FY-end and revenue to rise from about INR68 crore (FY26) toward INR250-300 crore, but the plant is loss-making (INR34 crore FY26 loss) and expansion awaits pollution board permissions.

530305|2026-03.headline: Piccadily Agro FY26 standalone revenue rose 28% to INR1,143 crore and PAT 33% to INR140 crore; management guides 60-70% Alco-Bev growth in FY27.
530305|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first year Piccadily crossed INR1,000 crore revenue, with standalone PBT up 33% to INR190 crore and PAT up 33% to INR140 crore. Q4 standalone revenue rose 33% YoY to INR364 crore, with PBT of INR63 crore and PAT of INR46 crore, while Q4 standalone EBITDA margin fell about 300 bps on a weaker sugar quarter and a higher distillery mix. Management announced a scheme of demerger of the sugar business into a separate listed entity, targeted for completion in FY27, and a change of statutory auditor (partner-level continuity). FY27 is guided as an exceptional year, with Alco-Bev growth of 60-70% in value terms, driven by capacity additions at Indri and the new Mahasamund (Chhattisgarh) plant.

financial_highlights.change: PBT +17% YoY from INR54 crore; PAT +14% YoY from INR40 crore

segments.name: IMFL (brands, Alco-Bev)
segments.commentary: Q4 IMFL growth about 63% YoY; FY26 IMFL growth about 31% on annualised basis per management. Indri grew about 16% in FY26 per analyst question, not confirmed by management; IMFL EBITDA margin stated at 45-50%.

segments.commentary: FY26 Alco-Bev revenue INR908 crore (+42%), PBT INR209 crore (+37%), EBITDA margin about 31.5%. Non-IMFL portion is mainly ethanol and country liquor; no bulk malt sales.

segments.commentary: Sugar EBITDA margin fell to about 2% in Q4 FY26 from 11% in Q4 FY25, driving most of the standalone margin decline; sugar business is proposed to be demerged.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of IMFL volume growth by brand (Indri, Cashmir, Camikara, Whistler) and channel split between CSD, HORECA, export and domestic.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined category or brand-wise breakup, citing internal confidentiality, and reiterated 60-70% Alco-Bev growth. Channel mix given: CSD and paramilitary about 30%, exports about 25%, with domestic the balance; HORECA focus being increased.

qa_highlights.question: Why Indri grew only about 16% in FY26 against expectations of 25-30%, and whether there is brand fatigue.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said increased competition is not the main reason; supply was constrained during the expansion. Supply constraints are expected to ease from this year, allowing stronger growth.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 EBITDA margin decline: was it mix-driven, and what margin range is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sugar margin fell to about 2% in Q4 FY26 from 11% a year earlier, with a higher distillery sale mix also contributing. Management guided FY27 Alco-Bev absolute EBITDA growth of 60-70% with margin flat to about 50 bps higher.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR300-350 crore incremental IMFL revenue in FY27 on a base of about INR500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to use of new Indri and Chhattisgarh capacity, previously constrained by supply, plus a new product pipeline expected to start from around Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for FY27 and the Scotland facility.
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex not more than INR25-30 crore, mainly barrels (85,000 to 1,00,000) with some warehouse and bottling expansion. Scotland distillery construction is starting, with completion over the next couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: what drove the 132% jump in short-term borrowings and the normalisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings funded higher receivables from IMFL sales and about INR100 crore of added malt inventory. Management expects to bring borrowings back to FY26 levels as sales grow 60-70% and malt inventory is monetised.

530365|2026-03.headline: Orient Bell Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 66% YoY to INR16.4 crores, with margin up 270 bps, after ~20% cumulative price hikes in March-April.

530365|2026-06.headline: Orient Bell Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42.8% YoY to INR203 crores, with EBITDA margin at 8.7% and a record 39.7% gross margin.
530365|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 42.8% YoY to INR203 crores on 22.9% volume growth and about 15.9% higher ASP, with EBITDA up to INR17.6 crores from INR5.6 crores. Management attributed the quarter to Morbi shutdowns (late March to mid-May) that opened a supply gap, plus its own demand-generation push and dealer sell-out support. The company remains debt-free, reports a working capital cycle of 18 days, and is weighing deployment of its cash. Management declined to give any revenue or margin guidance.

segments.name: Projects

segments.name: GVT (glazed vitrified tiles)
segments.commentary: GVT was about 47% of Q1 sales by value; about 15-20% of GVT came from Dora plant, bulk from SKD, and a low single-digit share from Morbi.

segments.name: Tile adhesives (Masterbond)
segments.commentary: Early-stage, cash-and-carry business with INR2.5 crores of sales in Q1, currently scaling in North and part of East India.

qa_highlights.answer: Adhesives generated INR2.5 crores in Q1 on a cash-and-carry basis, expanding from North to East; no bathware plans.

530367|2026-03.headline: NRB Bearings Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to INR372 crores, EBITDA margin 19.5%, and FY26 PAT up 77% to INR146 crores.
530367|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR372 crores, with EBITDA up 17% to INR74 crores (19.5% margin) and PAT of INR42 crores. For FY26, revenue rose 11% to INR1,335 crores, EBITDA rose 19% to INR267 crores, and margin expanded to 19.5% from 18.3%. Management attributed margin gains to solar power, automation, yield improvement and renegotiated vendor costs, and flagged a quarter-end forex anomaly that pulled down Q4 gross margin. Management leaned on an FY-level lens, declined to disclose standalone export, aftermarket, and segment splits, and guided to brownfield capacity commissioning from June-July 2026.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Management says NRB is in transmission, driveline, chassis and steering, with limited engine exposure beyond two- and three-wheelers and little wheel-end content. Replacement market grew about 4%, and the company said it shifted focus toward OEMs in Q4.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Industrial business is about 14-15% of revenue per management, including tractors and farm equipment. Target is 20-25% of revenue over time; named focus areas are construction equipment, off-highway, gearboxes, switchgear, power generation and electric grid.

segments.name: Aerospace (Mahant Toolroom, acquired subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mahant Toolroom order book is close to INR50 crores, up from INR25 crores at announcement, with all orders from HAL across divisions. Management expects full operational control between mid-April and May 2026 and a business plan in about six months.

guidance_outlook: International business expected to grow 10-14% in FY27 per current business plan, with management saying maybe up to 15%.

FY27 capex guided at about INR120 crores (including land), against a total announced INR200 crore capex over 18 months plus up to INR40 crores for land; split is 90% machines and 10% infrastructure and building.
Brownfield capacity enhancements to commission from June-July 2026 through FY27 and up to Q1 2028, with partial benefits from the current quarter.
Management aims to sustain EBITDA margins of 18-21% over time; industrial products expected to be as profitable as the core, with individual products ranging from 14% to 30%.
Five-year aspirational revenue target of about INR2,500 crores, which management said is increasingly becoming a concrete goal.
Mahant Toolroom business plan to be shared in about six months; AS9100-linked aerospace certification expected in about six months.
capex_capacity: Reported capacity utilisation about 85%; management says effective utilisation at several plants is much closer to full after adjusting for demand variation, maintenance, shifts and changeovers.
Bottlenecks identified at specific plants; machinery orders placed and first machines arrived, with major enhancement commissioning from June-July 2026.
Capex split: about 90% machines and 10% infrastructure/building/plant; maintenance, quality, new product and small balancing capex is part of normal capex at about 10% of turnover.
Joint venture declaration allows up to 20% of JV capacity to be used for automotive; about 20-25% of current automotive capacity is being used for industrial products.
Mahant Toolroom acquisition gives people, design and certification capability; the company had INR100 crores of aerospace RFQs but lacked an AS9100 plan.
demand_pricing: Management says growth came from volume, market share gains, capacity utilisation, product mix and efficiency, not one-offs.
Export demand was affected by geopolitics and logistics; India faced gas shortages, and customers changed product mix during Q4, which reduced the quarter's original plan.
Management says it prices to maintain margin profile; EV-specific bearings priced to keep existing margins and bearing content per vehicle is largely value neutral.
Company does not give export, aftermarket or standalone splits; it says the replacement market grew about 4% and that it deprioritised replacement given discount structures.
New wins include Siemens (details withheld under confidentiality), and aerospace platforms for HAL and NAL.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reports consolidated international business (all overseas-supplied customers, including subsidiaries) at about 4% growth and declined to give standalone export or aftermarket figures; replacement market grew about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex, and what is the split between standalone and subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex for FY27 is closer to INR120 crores, including land; management declined to split standalone versus subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin dip, the first sub-60% quarter in a long time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it primarily to forex, combining product mix with high-import-content products and quarter-end rupee conversion of COGS; it said this is an accounting anomaly that should normalise.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Mahant's INR50 crore order book will convert in FY27, and is HAL 100% of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY27 revenue and said the order book pace depends on rollout rates; HAL is the sole customer but across multiple divisions.

qa_highlights.question: Will industrial be margin accretive, and when will industrial reach 20% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial products are expected to match the company's 18-20% EBITDA requirement, averaging out over five years; industrial is 14-15% of revenue today and the aim is 20-25%, with no firm timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of the INR120 crore capex and maintenance capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the INR200 crore 18-month plan plus INR40 crore land; maintenance capex sits within normal capex at about 10% of turnover.

530367|2026-06.headline: NRB Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19.2% to INR370 crore and PAT 15% to INR38 crore; standalone PAT up 31.7%.
530367|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR370 crore (vs INR310 crore) and PAT of INR38 crore (vs INR33 crore). Standalone sales grew 14.7% YoY, PAT 31.7% and EBITDA 21.7%. The call focused on the diversification push into aerospace (via the MTR/Mahant Tool acquisition), electrification, off-highway, and robotics, plus a revised FY31 revenue outlook. Management projects INR300 crore revenue and INR90 crore profit contribution by 2031, though the timing was not committed.

segments.commentary: 14% of total revenue, up from 11%, with industrial growth of 34%.

segments.name: Heavy mobility / off-highway
segments.commentary: Accredited US defence supplier for heavy vehicles; supplies French and US defence programmes. JCB UK named as a customer at the AGM.

segments.name: Electrification / EV
segments.commentary: Management says about 70% of its applications are EV-agnostic (common to ICE, hybrid and EV). A BMW i steering product launches in 2027. Electrification vertical formed; more announcements promised in 3-6 months.

segments.name: Unitec JV (industrial cylindrical roller bearings)
segments.commentary: INR110 crore investment for INR130 crore capacity; plant to be commissioned by April 2027 at Aurangabad (Shendra) after relocating from Hyderabad. Land and a partly ready building already bought.

segments.name: NRB USA
segments.commentary: First win at Columbia, South Carolina facility: high-precision planet pins for a GM Corvette programme via a tier-1 transmission customer, about 300,000 peak volume.

qa_highlights.answer: Data-centre bearings are NRB's own product in development, not part of the JV, with no announcement yet. For the CAGR, management pointed to the trailing 12-month average of 14.28% and said the INR2,500 crore target was too low.

qa_highlights.answer: Power, logistics and petroleum-linked cost escalation. Management said it is offsetting this through value engineering (VAVE), plant cost reduction and price increases.

qa_highlights.answer: Total programme INR270 crore, of which INR60 crore is spent and about INR100 crore is ordered or in process. Management said INR100 crore of capex yields about INR130 crore of sales.

rows.label: NRB USA Make-in-USA facility receiving Corvette orders

530475|2026-03.headline: Tinna Rubber Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to over 18% on revenue of INR157 crores, up 22% YoY, with FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25%.
530475|2026-03.overview: Management reported record tire processing volumes in FY26 and a standalone EBITDA margin of 17.2%, up 286 bps. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 22% YoY and 13% QoQ to INR157 crores, with EBITDA up 63% YoY to INR29 crores. Subsidiaries and new projects (Oman, South Africa, Saudi, TP Buildtech, PCMB, pyrolysis and rCB) carried start-up costs and geopolitical drag that management expects to normalise through FY27. Infra segment softened on bitumen shortages, which management expects to be temporary.

financial_highlights.value: revenue INR75 crores, EBITDA INR6 crores

financial_highlights.metric: Combined loss, Mbodla, South Africa and Tinna Rubber Arabia (FY26)

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20% YoY in FY26, driven by MRP and reclaim rubber demand and exports, which grew 30% in volume. Management sees strong FY27 growth on higher virgin polymer prices and rubber blending in bitumen.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Revenue declined from INR222 crores to INR205 crores in FY26 as the company prioritised value-added products. Bitumen shortage is expected to hit Q1-Q2 FY27 volumes, with management expecting normalisation later in the year.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23% in FY26 despite a marginal volume decline, reflecting price correction. Management expects a modest improvement in FY27.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Revenue stable YoY while volumes rose 8%. Appointed exclusive distributor in India for Zibo TAA Metal Technology (China) steel abrasives, with 30% volume growth targeted in FY27.

segments.name: PCMB (polymer compounding and masterbatch)
segments.commentary: About 4% of FY26 turnover, operating at 40% utilisation, with QoQ growth of about 75%. Budgeted FY27 revenue of about INR75 crores, rising to 8-10% of revenue. Haryana polymer compounding capacity to reach 18,000 tpa by end Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Pyrolysis (TPO) and rCB
segments.commentary: Pyrolysis plant has started and the rCB plant is under commissioning. FY27 revenue from both is projected at INR50-55 crores, with EBITDA margins of 15-19%. Full operation is expected by Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 20-25% over FY26.
Vision 2029 target: revenue of INR1,000 crores with EBITDA margin above 18%; management says 18% is its guidance comfort level, and the FY29 target is organic only.
Maintain about 18% EBITDA margin in FY27; consolidated EBITDA projected to cross INR100 crores in FY27.
Tire-crush capacity to rise from 185,000 tpa to 235,000 tpa by FY27, with about INR100 crores capex over FY27-28, mostly from internal accruals and up to about INR20 crores debt if needed.
Oman normalisation expected within Q1 FY27; South Africa breakeven from Q2 FY27; Saudi tire recycling plant (24,000 tpa) capex of INR20-25 crores, with work starting end Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Working capital days expected to stay at current levels, since PCMB carries higher credit terms.
capex_capacity: Tire-crush capacity in India expanded 9% to 185,000 tons in FY26; target of 235,000 tpa by FY27. Tire-crush volume rose 13% to 155,000 tons in FY26.
Capacity utilisation was 90% in India and 85% in Oman in FY26. Varale plant at 80% utilisation.
Solar capacity rose from 1.23 MW to 4.48 MW in FY26; about 50% of power needs expected from renewables from FY27.
Pyrolysis plant (100 TPD feed) and rCB plant: about INR40 crores capex, largely complete. TPO stabilisation expected by end Q1 FY27 and rCB trial production in Q2 FY27.
TP Buildtech Kolkata plant commissioned, running under 25% utilisation, with three new construction system product lines launched.
Micronized rubber powder capacity being increased at at least two plants. PCMB capacity moving from a 6,000 tpa pilot to an 18,000 tpa polymer compounding facility in Haryana.
demand_pricing: Raw material economics: virgin rubber about INR240-260/kg vs recycled rubber about INR50/kg, roughly one-fifth the cost.

Bitumen prices have almost doubled, driving stronger crumb-rubber-modified bitumen (CRMB) demand, though India's bitumen supply constraint (imports of 3-3.5 million tons) hit road-work volumes in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Realisations on reclaim rubber and MRP improved on demand; management said realisation volatility currently favours the company.
Freight rates and elevated polymer prices from the Middle East crisis raised import costs; management says the company offset these by sourcing from multiple geographies and feedstock types.
Competition from new CRMB and rCB entrants: management cites a moat from raw material, product, customer and geographic diversity, plus 2-5 year approval cycles with tire majors.

qa_highlights.question: Vision FY29 revenue breakup by segment, and EPR outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PCMB rises toward 8-10% of revenue from about 4%. Infra is expected to be about 30%, Industrial about 35%, Consumer about 10%, with the balance from rCB and pyrolysis. EPR revenue stays around INR29-30 crores a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the infra slowdown hit blended margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects better realisations on reclaim rubber and MRP to offset any infra softness, and says the bitumen-driven slowdown is temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA expected from RCB and pyrolysis plants in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined FY27 revenue of about INR50-55 crores. EBITDA margins of 15-19% are expected once the plants are fully running, with payback in line with the existing business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise from 42 to 55?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase is mainly due to PCMB, where industry practice carries longer credit days. Core rubber-products credit days have not changed materially, and working capital days are expected to stay at current levels.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR100 crore capex be funded, and what is the debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of it from internal accruals, with FY27 EBITDA projected above INR100 crores. Management may take up to about INR20 crores of debt if needed.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling bitumen supply and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The company holds no bitumen and does not trade it. It supplies modifier to IOC and to contractors who source their own bitumen, which the company says is assured business for the next couple of years.

risks_watch: Bitumen availability (India imports 3-3.5 million tons, with Iran a key supplier) may keep infra volumes soft in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Middle East tensions delay the Saudi plant capital works (now expected end Q2 or Q3 FY27) and disrupt Oman exports; Oman normalisation is expected within Q1 FY27.
Start-up losses at South Africa and new plants; South Africa breakeven targeted from Q2 FY27, and TP Buildtech margins remain under pressure from crude, polymer and currency movements.
Receivable days rose to about 55 from 42 due to PCMB credit terms; watch whether working capital intensity persists.
Competition from new CRMB and rCB entrants; management cites strong moats but no quantified pricing impact.
Consolidated PAT growth (9%) lagged EBITDA growth; FY26 revenue growth was only 8% and infra revenue fell, so FY27 20-25% growth needs execution.
key_quotes: FY26 was another year of strong execution for Tinna Rubber, despite geopolitical uncertainties and a dynamic operating environment, we achieved record tire processing volumes and delivered robust EBITDA margins of over 17%.
But we expect that to normalize immediately because India has a very aggressive program for road construction.
Our comfort level to give a guidance to market is at 18%.

I don't see us doing any inorganic acquisition related to our business, but some adjacency business, if it comes across, where we have something new to learn or a new product line to add or new geography to add, those are the ideas we remain open to and we will look at those opportunities.
530475|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 execution, Vision 2029 and the Industrial/PCMB growth story, but cautious and deflecting on infra near-term volumes, bitumen supply, and per-ton realisation metrics. Management repeatedly stressed temporary disruption and declined to disclose new expansion locations or quantify pricing impact from competition.

rows.why: Management guides 20-25% FY27 revenue growth with tire-crush volume at 155,000 tons in FY26 (+13%) and Industrial exports already up 30% in volume in FY26, while Infra volumes are soft in Q1-Q2 FY27.

rows.why: Bitumen shortage (India imports 3-3.5 million tons) is expected to hit Infra volumes in Q1-Q2 FY27, Infra revenue already fell from INR222 crores to INR205 crores in FY26, and Middle East tensions could delay the Saudi plant and disrupt Oman exports.

rows.why: rCB trial production in Q2 FY27, TP Buildtech launched three new construction system product lines, and the Zibo TAA steel abrasives distribution targets 30% volume growth in FY27 with PCMB budgeted at about INR75 crores.

rows.when: Oman in Q1 FY27; South Africa from Q2 FY27
rows.why: Combined loss at Mbodla, South Africa and Tinna Rubber Arabia was INR1.58 crores in FY26 from start-up costs, and management expects Oman to normalise within Q1 FY27 and South Africa to break even from Q2 FY27.

rows.why: Receivable days rose 13 days, mainly from PCMB where industry credit terms are longer, and management expects working capital days to stay at current levels rather than improve.

rows.label: Net debt-to-equity down to 0.39 and debt-funded capex
rows.why: Total debt fell 10% to INR121 crores and net debt-to-equity fell from 0.73 to 0.39 in FY26, but the INR100 crores capex plan could add up to about INR20 crores of debt.

530475|2026-06.headline: Tinna Rubber Q1 FY27 posted record EBITDA above INR50 crores (21%+ margin) and PAT above INR20 crores, with EPR credits adding a one-off monetisation lift.
530475|2026-06.overview: Management reported record Q1 FY27 profitability, with standalone and consolidated EBITDA margins above 21% and PAT margins above 13%. Standalone revenue rose 18% YoY and consolidated revenue rose 20%, with EBITDA margin up 638 bps standalone and 575 bps consolidated. Management attributed the margin gain mainly to gross margin expansion from cheaper feedstock and a higher mix of value-added products such as MRP and reclaimed rubber. Growth engines (PCMB, TPO/rCB, Oman, South Africa) are still ramping, and management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR670-700 crores and a sustainable 18-20% EBITDA margin.

financial_highlights.value: Above INR50 crores (EBITDA margin above 21%, cited as ~22%)
financial_highlights.change: Standalone EBITDA margin +638 bps YoY; consolidated +575 bps YoY

financial_highlights.value: Above INR20 crores (PAT margin above 13%; INR21 crores cited)
financial_highlights.change: Standalone PAT margin +471 bps YoY; consolidated +416 bps YoY

financial_highlights.value: ~INR9 crores; EBITDA margin 8.53%; PAT INR0.34 crores
INR19 crores revenue; INR3 crores EBITDA

financial_highlights.change: Threefold vs INR4 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR30.58 crores (company figure); analyst read INR27.19 crores for Q4 FY26 vs company figure INR29.85 crores
financial_highlights.change: Increase of ~INR5.4 crores QoQ per analyst; company to clarify by email

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 58% YoY; MRP volumes +28% and reclaimed rubber volumes +37% YoY; run-rate cited at INR45-46 crores per quarter. Exports volume +46% YoY.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Revenue +7% YoY; volumes +33% YoY on rubberized bitumen demand amid bitumen shortage. Secured a 15,000 tonne rubberized bitumen processing order for FY27. Bitumen emulsion hit by supply constraints.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Volumes declined (analyst cited ~20%); binder and synthetic grass prices rose up to threefold, delaying turfing projects. Management says consumer is ~8-10% of business.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Revenue steady with marginal volume decline, supported by price corrections. Exclusive India distributorship for Zibo TAA Metal Technology steel abrasives; ~50% volume growth targeted in FY27.

segments.name: Tire recycling (India and Oman)
segments.commentary: India capacity utilisation 88%, volumes +35% YoY but down 10% QoQ on softer consumer demand. Oman utilisation 78%, hit by West Asia conflict.

segments.name: PCMB / PP Buildtech
segments.commentary: PCMB at 82% utilisation of initial 6,000 tpa; total capacity 18,000 tpa after Haryana expansion; targeted ~10% of FY27 revenue. Kolkata plant commissioned Q4 FY26; targeting >30% growth and INR100 crores revenue in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reiterated at INR670-700 crores (INR675-700 crores cited in later reply).
EBITDA margin guidance of 18-20% for FY27, described as sustainable despite Q1 at ~22%; management declined to confirm either 18% or 22%.
Vision 2029: INR1,000 crores revenue by FY29, 25%+ revenue CAGR, 33%+ profitability CAGR, EBITDA margin above 18%, ROCE above 30%, presence in 10 locations.
Capex of ~INR100 crores across FY27-FY28; INR27 crores spent in Q1 FY27; ~INR60 crores to be capitalised in FY27. Capex could rise if demand stays strong.
TPO/rCB (pyrolysis oil and recovered carbon black) contribution of 7-10% of FY27 revenue (~INR50-60 crores). TPO sales from Q2 FY27; rCB production from Q3 FY27.

South Africa breakeven expected Q2 FY27; Phase 2 tyre crumb production expected Q2 or Q3 FY27. Saudi Arabia (24,000 tpa) construction targeted toward end of calendar 2026, subject to Middle East normalisation.
Expansion of India tyre crushing capacity to 235,000 tpa (+27%) by FY27; MRP capacity 3,500 tpa addition by Q3 FY27 to 20,000 tpa total.
capex_capacity: India tyre crushing capacity 185,000 tpa, rising to 235,000 tpa by FY27 (+27%).
MRP capacity: 3,500 tpa expansion commissioning by Q3 FY27, taking total to 20,000 tpa.
TPO plant at Varle: trials began Q1 FY27; commercial sales Q2 FY27; stabilisation by Q3 FY27. rCB production Q3 FY27, commercial sales by Q4 FY27.
Rooftop solar: Gummidipoondi 999 kW (June 2026) and Varle 2,218 kW (July 2026). Renewable capacity raised from 1.23 MW to 4.48 MW; renewables were 51% of power in Q1 FY27.
Management is exploring de-bottlenecking and possibly a greenfield India plant; India utilisation cited at 80-85% by analyst. Blended utilisation target 75-80% by year-end across geographies.
demand_pricing: Industrial demand supported by rising raw material costs and ESG-driven tyre-maker demand; MRP and reclaimed rubber volumes growing fast.
Rubberized bitumen demand rose as bitumen supply tightened and prices rose due to the West Asia conflict; government push to reduce import dependence.
Consumer turfing demand hit by binder and synthetic grass price spikes; management says the market is intact and will recover once prices stabilise.
EPR credits: ~100,000 units monetised in Q1 at a floor price of ~INR2,500 per unit (~INR25 crores cash). Management says EPR contributes ~INR25-30 crores a year at PBT level.
Margin gain attributed to raw material optionality and value-added product mix. Management said inventory gains were very marginal.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin rise is due to inventory gains, and is there margin normalisation ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gains were very marginal. Management said the changes are systemic (raw material optionality, value-added mix), and expects some front-ended costs from new projects, so 18-20% is the sustainable range.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the 400-500 bps margin expansion; material plus inventory cost fell to 46% of sales.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main contribution came at gross margin, from cheaper raw material and higher realisation from value-added products, plus scale efficiencies. Overall EBITDA margin expanded about 4 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: How is EPR monetisation accounted for, and what is its contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said accrued EPR credits from prior years were monetised against unbilled revenue. Q1 P&L impact was already booked in FY26. Annual EPR contribution is about INR25-30 crores at PBT level. Analysts' questions on clean PAT were not fully resolved on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Chile and Saudi Arabia, and will overseas investment scale up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Oman's limited scope and similar operating parameters for Saudi Arabia, and end-of-life tyre sourcing and hedging for South Africa and Chile. India remains the core investment focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for infrastructure given the West Asia situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bitumen shortages hit some projects, but rubberized asphalt demand rose as contractors sought cheaper alternatives. Infrastructure revenue grew 7% in Q1, and Q1 is the peak road-work season.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue guidance of INR670-700 crores was reiterated; margin should sustain at 18-20% even though Q1 was 22%.

risks_watch: Earnings quality: the INR21 crore EPR monetisation and its treatment in the P&L were unclear on the call; analysts could not get a clean recurring PAT.
Other expenses rose ~INR5.4 crores QoQ per analyst; company promised an email clarification.
Geopolitical risk (West Asia conflict) affecting bitumen and binder supply, Oman utilisation (78%), and the Saudi project timeline.
Consumer segment volumes declined; recovery depends on binder and synthetic grass prices.
Q2 FY27 monsoon-related seasonality in infrastructure; capacity ramp-ups of TPO, rCB and PCMB must deliver to hit INR670-700 crores.
Management's margin guidance (18-20%) is well below the Q1 print (22%); watch for Q2 and Q3 margin normalisation.
530475|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the strategy, but guarded on forward numbers: management declined to confirm either 18% or 22% margin, and deflected several EPR accounting questions to email follow-ups.
key_quotes: We are delighted to share that we have commenced FY27 on a very strong note, delivering our best ever quarterly profitability.
I will neither confirm that we will achieve 18% nor will I confirm we will achieve 22%.
Our focus -- our core investment will remain India for the foreseeable future.
Our hedge comes from the fact that we cater to consumer business, industrial business, infra business, steel now PCMB and also TPO and rCB.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin ~22% (up 638 bps standalone) came from cheaper feedstock and value-added mix, but management guides 18-20% as sustainable and expects front-ended costs from new projects, so margins are more likely to normalise than expand.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: India tyre crushing capacity rising from 185,000 to 235,000 tpa (+27%) by FY27 with MRP addition of 3,500 tpa by Q3 FY27, and India utilisation already at 88%, so new capacity is firmly committed and coming live in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Industrial volumes growing fast (MRP +28%, reclaimed rubber +37% YoY), Infrastructure volumes +33% on a 15,000 tonne rubberized bitumen order, and steel abrasive volume growth of ~50% targeted in FY27, offset by consumer volumes down ~20%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: India utilisation at 88% and management is exploring de-bottlenecking and possibly a greenfield India plant, with ~INR100 crores capex across FY27-FY28 and capex that could rise if demand stays strong.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated INR670-700 crore revenue and 18-20% margin rather than raising them, and declined to confirm either 18% or 22% margin, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 margin guide of 18-20% sits well below the Q1 print of ~22%, but management reiterated it; risk is from West Asia bitumen/binder disruption, consumer volumes down ~20%, and the Saudi timeline, with the INR670-700 crore revenue guide dependent on TPO/rCB and PCMB ramp-ups.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TPO commercial sales from Q2 FY27, rCB production from Q3 FY27 (commercial sales by Q4 FY27) and TPO/rCB guided at 7-10% of FY27 revenue (~INR50-60 crores).

rows.label: 15,000 tonne rubberized bitumen processing order for FY27
rows.why: Secured order for 15,000 tonnes of rubberized bitumen processing, with infrastructure volumes +33% YoY amid bitumen shortage.

rows.label: South Africa breakeven and Saudi Arabia 24,000 tpa plant
rows.when: Q2 FY27 breakeven; Saudi construction toward end CY2026
rows.why: South Africa breakeven guided for Q2 FY27 with Phase 2 tyre crumb in Q2/Q3 FY27, but Saudi construction is subject to Middle East normalisation and Mbodla plus Saudi start-up loss was ~INR53 lakhs.

rows.label: EPR credit monetisation and earnings quality
rows.why: About 100,000 EPR units monetised at ~INR2,500 (~INR25 crores cash) and management puts annual EPR at INR25-30 crores PBT, but clean recurring PAT was not resolved and other expenses rose ~INR5.4 crores QoQ per analyst.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q1 print, capacity ramp and the INR670-700 crore revenue guide, but guarded on margins (declined to confirm 18% or 22%) and deflected EPR accounting questions to email; analysts pushed on clean PAT, the one-off EPR lift and the ~INR5.4 crore QoQ rise in other expenses

530475|2026-09.headline: Tinna Rubber Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31% to INR157 crores and PAT 45% to INR17 crores; H1 PAT up 60% to INR38 crores.
530475|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue reached INR157 crores (up from INR120 crores), with EBITDA of INR29 crores (18.8% margin) and PAT of INR17 crores (10.9% margin). H1 revenue rose 25% to INR313 crores, EBITDA 50% to INR63 crores (20.4% margin) and PAT 60% to INR38 crores (12.2% margin). Management said profitability moderated from Q1 due to start-up costs, geopolitical uncertainty and subsidiary performance, and reiterated FY27 guidance of about INR700 crores revenue, INR126 crores EBITDA and INR70 crores PAT. Expansion moved forward with a 40-acre Andhra Pradesh site (INR250 crores over 3 years), while the Saudi Arabia tyre recycling plant has been delayed by the West Asia conflict.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 38% to INR112 crores despite bitumen supply constraints; management cites it as a main growth driver with Industrial, and notes monsoon and cold-weather seasonality in Q2 and Q4.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 37% to INR85 crores; exports were about 6% of total revenue with export volume growth of about 15%.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: H1 revenue rose to INR21 crores from INR19 crores, driven by price correction with stable volumes.

segments.name: Steel (by-product)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to INR57 crores from INR53 crores, mainly on price correction with stable volumes; management describes it as a by-product of tyre recycling.

segments.name: PCMB (Polymer Composites & Masterbatch)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue more than tripled to INR27 crores after 12,000 tpa added at Gannaur; capacity now 18,000 tpa, targeted at 8-10% of FY27 revenue and about INR70 crores top line. Management said this business runs at lower EBITDA margin than the core.

segments.name: TP Buildtech (associate)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR41 crores with EBITDA INR4.7 crores, contributing INR1 crore at consolidated level; best-case target of INR100 crores revenue by FY27.

segments.name: Oman subsidiary
segments.commentary: Ran at 90% utilisation in H1; EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% from 6.4% in FY26; PAT of INR1.3 crores in H1.

segments.name: South Africa and Saudi Arabia (start-up)
segments.commentary: Combined start-up loss of about INR94 lakhs in H1; South Africa Phase 1 complete with semi-processed exports begun, and 9,000 tpa crumb line delayed 3-4 months.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA up 37% YoY; margin vs 18.0% a year ago
down from INR121 crores at end FY26
vs about INR6.7 crores in Q1 FY27

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 EBITDA margin (about 16% per analyst) come off versus prior quarters, and what about PCMB mix and steel price trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin was 18%-plus in Q2 (reported 18.8%), Q1 was an aberration with raw material and inventory benefits, and PCMB runs at lower margin than core as a new business still stabilising with R&D spend.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company's sourcing and margin stability differentiated versus peers hit by geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited diversity of geography, raw material base and customer base, pan-India presence, and multiple tyre origins, without commenting on competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Where is India capacity being added to reach 235,000 tpa, and by when?

530517|2026-03.headline: Relaxo Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8.1% YoY to INR 751 crore, with EBITDA margin at 16.5%, aided partly by GST cut-driven channel restocking.
530517|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 751 crore (+8.1% YoY), EBITDA INR 124 crore (+10.6%) and PAT INR 68 crore (+20.4%), with PAT margin at 9.0%. Management attributed the volume recovery to GST cut from 12% to 5%, channel restocking by distributors and better consumer demand, and said the underlying growth is closer to 5-6% over the last two quarters. FY26 revenue fell to INR 2,702 crore from INR 2,790 crore, while PAT rose 5.3% to INR 179 crore. Management has taken 2-3 price increases of roughly 15-18% at consumer level to offset input cost and wage inflation linked to West Asia tensions and Haryana labour costs.
