Management said the company cut trade discounts and lifted contribution on higher volumes, with some benefit from back-end cost work; there was a small price increase in Q4.
Management stated the industry (footwear) is seeing price hikes across players, not only Relaxo; Bata, Red Tape and Metro were cited by analysts as not yet having raised prices.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 growth was a one-off channel restock after the GST cut, and what is underlying growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full impact started after December and underlying growth was about 5-6% over the last two quarters, as distributors' stock was liquidated in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: By how much have input costs risen and how much price has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended consumer price increase of about 15-18%; cost increase estimated at 15-20% including labour, with margins expected to be protected.

qa_highlights.question: Why take price hikes early when competitors have not, and what is the volume risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the April raw material spike and a more than 30% wage increase in Haryana; said the price hike cannot be taken back and gave no volume guidance beyond the 4-5% target.

qa_highlights.question: Does FY27 capex of INR 180-200 crore include the EBO rollout, and will 100 EBOs dilute margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the EBO capex (INR 30-35 lakh per store, about INR 30-35 crore for 100) is part of the INR 200 crore; management said EBO margins are already accretive and company-level margin is expected to rise about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the high Q4 margin, and is there any inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited back-end plant cost reduction, higher volume against fixed costs, lower trade discounts and a small Q4 price increase; denied any inventory gain.

530521|2026-06.headline: Virat plans Rs 95 crore primary investment in Brahm Lifestyle for 70.2% stake, pivoting toward lifestyle brands; socks contract sales ~6 million pairs.
530521|2026-06.overview: The investor call, hosted by the Brahm Group (promoter, ~75% owner), centred on a strategic pivot rather than Q1 FY27 operating results. Management said Virat will be renamed Brahm Virat Industries Corporation Limited (pending ROC approval) and will invest Rs 95 crore via preferential allotment for a 70.2% controlling stake in Brahm Lifestyle Products Private Limited. Virat's core business is contract manufacturing of socks (9 million pairs capacity, 145 machines), with a nascent branded push (Lord Walker). No audited Q1 FY27 financials, margins or segment numbers were presented; forward figures were management projections and were explicitly labelled forward-looking.

segments.commentary: Management cited ~6-6.5 million pairs contract volume at ~Rs 60 per pair (~Rs 36 crore revenue, 10-12% operating margin); branded target of 2 million pairs in two years at Rs 200-250 per pair.

segments.commentary: About 600 bags sold this year at ~$1,200 retail; target of 2,000 bags at ~$2,000 in two years (~$2 million sales).

segments.commentary: Run-rate ~Rs 1 crore per month; management targets ~Rs 100 million FY-end sales at ~10% EBITDA margin; app launch mid-September.

segments.commentary: Targeting Rs 5 crore sales in first year via memberships; online launch planned November in Pune.

Lord Walker: target of ~1 million pairs in calendar 2027, with 5-year plan toward a global lifestyle brand.
Management aims for a 50-60% CAGR on deployed capital; this was described as a personal track record, not a guarantee.
Inorganic acquisitions: 5-6 LOIs under NDA, to be brought to the Virat board when appropriate; no specifics disclosed.
capex_capacity: Capacity: 9 million pairs per year from 145 machines (up from 33 machines and 2 million pairs in 1995); current output ~6 million pairs.
Spare capacity cited as the rationale for branded and DTC expansion, with contract manufacturers in the Gujarat ecosystem available for support.
Brahm Fresh app launch mid-September; Skill by Brahm online in Pune in November.
Handbag production: leather sourced from Indonesia, assembly in India; apparel tie-ups in Kolkata, Coimbatore and Bengaluru.
No explicit Virat capex figure or commissioning timeline was disclosed.
demand_pricing: Virat exports to UK and Switzerland; UK FTA operational from 15 July 2026 removes 11% import duty on Indian socks, per management.
Customers include John Lewis, Waitrose, Barbour, FootAsylum, Umbro, Castore, Sudu, Kukri, Migros (~300 stores) and Galaxus (Switzerland).
Lord Walker launched domestically on Amazon, Myntra, Nykaa, Instamart and Blinkit; first year is focused on brand awareness.
Management said it has zero sales so far in North America, Far East and Middle East, and named these as future targets.
Competition: management referenced China and Turkey sock production and cotton prices, without quantification.

qa_highlights.question: How mature is each business and how will management bandwidth be handled across multiple businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the socks business is mature and cash generative. Other businesses were described as self-sufficient, with funding and teams in place and shared Brahm platform services for technology, HR and admin.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the Rs 95 crore be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no major need for money in socks or handbags. Funds are earmarked for Skill by Brahm, possible acquisitions (5-6 LOIs under NDA), international distribution and marketing, with no specific allocation given.

qa_highlights.question: Can management provide revenue, EBITDA or ROCE guidance for 12-24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave two-year socks projections (Rs 100 crore revenue, Rs 20-40 crore EBITDA) and a handbag target (~$2 million sales), and said a Rs 3,000 crore market cap was achievable. Caveated as forward-looking.

qa_highlights.question: Will Virat expand into products beyond socks, such as gloves or knitwear?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said apparel for men, women and kids is planned under Lord Walker, including undergarments, t-shirts and kidswear (Little Walker), with knitwear for kids a future option. Emphasis remains on getting socks right first.

risks_watch: Related-party style transaction: Rs 95 crore primary raise into a promoter-linked entity, with ambiguity on valuation, pricing and minority-shareholder protection (management said near book value).
Heavy reliance on promoter's unaudited forward projections across socks, handbags, fresh seafood and wellness; no historical audited financials for the new verticals were presented.
Management bandwidth across many new businesses, with the group management focus on the lifestyle platform.
Execution milestones to track: ROC approval of name change, Brahm Fresh app launch in mid-September, Skill by Brahm launch in November, Lord Walker volumes against 1 million pairs in CY2027.
Regulatory check on the NSE trading permission; the company clarified it is not yet listed on NSE, only permitted to trade.

530549|2026-03.headline: Shilpa Medicare Q4 FY26 revenue hit record INR439 crore (+30% YoY) with EBITDA INR121 crore (28% margin); FY26 revenue INR1,549 crore (+18%).
530549|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR439 crore, up 30% YoY, with EBITDA of INR121 crore (+40% YoY, 28% margin). Full-year FY26 revenue was INR1,549 crore (+18%) and EBITDA INR445 crore (+30%, 29% margin), with gross margin at 70%. Adjusted PAT before exceptionals was INR87 crore for Q4 and INR232 crore for FY26 (about +135%). Q4 also included a INR30 crore exceptional gain from selling 31% of Sravathi Advance (JV now an associate, 34% held) and an INR18 crore associate share of profit tied to Maaia. Management gave no formal FY27 guidance, and most FY27 commentary was qualitative.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR985 crore, up 16%; Q4 revenue INR259 crore, up 16% YoY, driven by newly expanded capacity uptake and captive demand from formulations.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR205 crore, up 54% YoY; FY26 INR618 crore, up 30%. Excluding licensing income, base business grew 64% in Q4 and 75% for FY26. European formulation revenue exceeded INR200 crore, up over 100%.

segments.name: Biologics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR150 crore, up roughly 100% YoY, driven by CDMO deal momentum; includes a prior-year-type milestone component (Orion albumin milestone referenced by analyst, not quantified).

530555|2026-03.headline: Paramount Communications Q4 FY26 revenue rose 24.5% QoQ to INR 573 crore, but FY26 EBITDA fell to INR 117.5 crore (6% margin) on US tariff disruption.
530555|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sequential recovery: revenue INR 573 crore (+13.6% YoY, +24.5% QoQ), EBITDA incl. other income INR 38.8 crore at 6.7% margin, and PAT INR 20.5 crore. FY26 revenue rose about 23% to INR 1,912 crore, but absolute EBITDA and PAT declined YoY due to US tariffs escalating from 10% to 50% during 2025. Management redirected volumes to domestic demand, which grew about 27%, and retained a US presence at sub-economic margins. The Narmadapuram greenfield plant (INR 300 crore, Phase 1) is the main growth lever, with a stated INR 5,000 crore revenue ambition by FY31.

segments.name: Domestic B2B industrial
segments.commentary: Grew 37.3% to INR 1,001 crore in FY26, led by power cables; domestic order book at INR 508 crore (87% of order book).

segments.name: Domestic B2C and distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 10.6% to INR 179 crore in FY26.

segments.name: Domestic B2G (government/PSU)
segments.commentary: Stable at about INR 182 crore in FY26, so its share of revenue fell.

segments.name: Exports (USA-led)
segments.commentary: Grew 13.9% to INR 550 crore in FY26 despite tariffs; eight active US distributors versus two in FY22.

guidance_outlook: FY27 (informal, assuming current metal prices hold): top-line growth of 15-20% and at least 10% volume growth; no formal guidance given.
Margins expected to return to FY25 levels as a first milestone, with pre-tariff margin levels targeted by end of FY27.

Narmadapuram Phase 1: investment about INR 300 crore by FY28; partial operations from Q1 FY28; sales target about INR 500 crore in FY28 and INR 1,200 crore in FY29; expected 9-10% margin and 3-4 year payback.

Long-term aspiration: INR 5,000 crore revenue by FY31, implying doubling every 3-4 years; Phase 1 capacity alone seen at INR 3,600-4,000 crore, with Phase 2 (INR 200-300 crore capex) to exceed INR 5,000 crore.
Working capital expected to normalise within Q1 FY27 after receivables rose on Q4 back-ended dispatches.
capex_capacity: Two existing plants at Dharuhera (Haryana) and Kushkhera (Rajasthan) described as running at optimal utilisation for three to four years; physical space constraint reached.
Existing-plant capex of about INR 50-55 crore a year, over INR 160 crore across the past three years.

Narmadapuram (Madhya Pradesh): about 31 acres allotted by MPIDC and possession taken; civil works underway; long-lead machinery ordered; building construction to start shortly; commissioning from FY28.

Narmadapuram products: EHV cables up to 132 kV (starting with 33 kV, then 66 kV and 132 kV), transmission conductors, elastomeric EBeam and EPR cables, lead-sheathed rubber cables; EHV approvals expected by FY28.

Funding: about INR 122 crore of equity raised (about INR 92 crore from investors, about INR 30 crore from promoters), plus internal accruals and modest debt; current debt only about INR 110 crore of working capital limits.
demand_pricing: Management cites six demand drivers: India T&D capex of INR 3.35 lakh crore (FY26-30), renewables (210-220 GW solar and 50-60 GW wind by FY30), data centres (about 70% higher cable density for AI facilities), US grid capex above USD 1 trillion, construction capex of INR 18-19 lakh crore, and railways (FY27 budget INR 3 lakh crore).

US tariffs: 10% reciprocal tariff from 2 Apr 2025, raised to 25% in August and 50% by end-August 2025; IEEPA tariffs invalidated by US Supreme Court (Feb-Apr 2026), which management says restored India's competitiveness.
Management says it kept US presence at sub-economic margins at lower volumes; competitors from Vietnam, South Korea, Cambodia, Ecuador and Egypt had a tariff advantage in FY26.
Pricing policy: no firm-price orders with delivery beyond 3-4 months; metal is bought the next working day after order receipt; price-variation formulas increasingly accepted by customers.
Management expects Q2 FY27 onwards to see stronger US demand pull, with one or two new products to be launched in the US next quarter.
Middle East, Europe, Australia and Africa flagged as opportunistic markets, with the Middle East a focus area in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new plant reach optimum utilisation, and what is the payback and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 (INR 300 crore) targets INR 1,200 crore revenue by FY29; payback 3-4 years; margin 9-10%. No formal guidance, but 15-20% top-line growth and at least 10% volume growth assumed if metal prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the domestic market not scaled up the top line or bottom line over the past year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the constraint is capacity, not demand; the plants have run at full utilisation for four years, and the company diverted US volume to domestic. FY24 precedent: US sales fell from INR 400 crore to INR 280 crore while domestic doubled from INR 400 crore to INR 800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables roughly double, and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 65% of Q4 sales were dispatched in the second half of the quarter; over three-quarters had been realised by 15 May 2026. Working capital cycle moved only from 99 to 101 days; CFO said most dispatches are against LCs.

qa_highlights.question: Can Paramount return to FY25 margins, and what drives margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 EBITDA margin is the first milestone. Drivers: new products, US tariff normalisation, power, renewable and data-centre demand, and operating leverage on volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will EHV lead times exceed 5-6 months, and how is raw material risk handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids long-delivery firm-price orders and prefers 3-4 month horizons or price-variation clauses; EHV would follow the same policy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the longer-term aspirational revenue and margin view?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crore by FY31; Phase 1 capacity can reach about INR 3,600-4,000 crore, and Phase 2 to exceed INR 5,000 crore. Margins expected to move towards peer range as scale grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when the balance sheet has low leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity was about INR 122 crore of the INR 300 crore project; management said it diversifies the funding mix, with working capital needs still to be bank-funded and current debt about INR 110 crore.

risks_watch: Receivables: working capital cycle at 101 days; management says receivables normalise in Q1 FY27 with over three-quarters of Q4 receivables already collected. Watch the Q1 FY27 receivable run-rate.
US tariff regime and recovery: margins in the US remain below pre-tariff levels; watch whether volumes and margins improve each quarter from Q2 FY27.
Narmadapuram execution: commissioning slated for Q1 FY28 with EHV approvals expected by FY28; the 9-10% margin and INR 1,200 crore FY29 target depend on it.
Raw material (copper and aluminium) pass-through: policy is to avoid long firm-price orders, but EHV and longer-cycle orders may test this.
Management's FY31 INR 5,000 crore target and the FY27 guidance are informal and conditional on metal prices holding.

530555|2026-06.headline: Paramount Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore; operating margin (ex other income) expanded 320 bps YoY to 6.6%.
530555|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore but fell 7.7% QoQ, which management attributed to the seasonal Q4-to-Q1 pattern. Operating profit excluding other income rose 129.2% YoY to INR 34.7 crore, with margin up 320 bps YoY and 136 bps QoQ to 6.6%. The US export recovery after the IEEPA tariff invalidation drove exports to INR 155 crore (29%+ of revenue, up about 77% QoQ), while domestic revenue reached INR 374 crore. Order book rose to INR 615 crore from INR 583 crore, and a fresh equity raise of about INR 122 crore lifted net worth to INR 894 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins return to pre-tariff levels near 8%, and what drove the 320 bps YoY margin improvement and can it be sustained?

Drivers cited: normalisation of US exports after the IEEPA duties were struck down (expected to add 300+ bps), and a higher-margin domestic power cable mix (~57% of Q1 revenue). Exports were 29%+ of revenue vs 15% in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Narmadapuram, and are there cost or time overruns?
qa_highlights.answer: Most critical machinery is ordered, with delivery lead times long but expected on time. Civil construction has started and major works are expected to take 6-7 months. Management does not expect major overruns. About INR 30 crore+ has been spent, plus more than INR 155 crore over three to four years on existing plants.

qa_highlights.question: How is Narmadapuram capex funded, and what utilisation supports the INR 1,200 crore revenue?

INR 1,200 crore is at 75% utilisation (the CFO-level comment referred to FY29). Approvals up to 66 kV are in place; 132 kV approvals are expected to start within about a year of manufacturing, with some possibly in 6-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the export order book only INR 97 crore despite strong export revenue?

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation, and what growth is possible in FY27 versus FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing plants run at practically 100% utilisation, and the constraint is manufacturing capacity rather than demand. FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%. FY28 growth is expected to be much faster once Narmadapuram starts. The INR 5,000 crore FY31 target is seen as a floor to beat.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin progress at risk if H2 export mix falls, and how do export margins compare with domestic?

It said the company can pivot quickly between domestic and export, citing FY23 and FY25 shifts, and expects export margins to keep improving each quarter.

530555|2026-09.headline: Paramount Communications Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31.1% YoY to INR 560.4 crores, with operating margin at 7.3% versus 6.6% in Q1.
530555|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was INR 560.4 crores, up 31.1% YoY and 5.9% QoQ, with operating profit of INR 40.9 crores at a 7.3% margin. PAT was INR 24.2 crores (4.3% margin) and EPS INR 0.74. H1 FY27 revenue was INR 1,089.8 crores (up 24.1% YoY) with PAT of INR 43.9 crores. Management reiterated it expects to return to FY25 operating margins by Q4 FY27 and to reach roughly 8% operating margin around then, and it kept the Narmadapuram plant on schedule for partial commissioning in Q1 FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs 6.6% in Q1 FY27 and 1.3% in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q2 exports were INR 158.1 crores (28.2% of revenue) and H1 exports INR 313.1 crores. Management expects US exports at 25-30% of FY27 revenue, with one analyst cited figure of INR 700 crores on this basis.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Q2 domestic revenue was INR 402.3 crores (71.8% of revenue). Power cables were 55.9% of revenue; B2B institutional INR 296.7 crores, B2C retail and distribution INR 53.7 crores, B2C government and PSU INR 51.9 crores.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: Order book at 30 Sep 2026 was INR 731 crores (domestic INR 632 crores, export INR 99 crores), including INR 575 crores of power cable and specialized conductor orders. HTLS order book was above INR 200 crores as of the call date.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY (CFO-level range given as 15-18% for existing plants in one answer); H1 run rate described as indicative.

Operating margin to return to FY25 levels by Q4 FY27; about 8% operating margin targeted around Q4, excluding customer claw-backs, which are expected to show in Q3 results. Management said 'we are hopeful' on the 8% figure.

Narmadapuram plant: partial commissioning in Q1 FY28; revenue of about INR 500 crores in FY28 and INR 1,200 crores in FY29; capacity to double to about 60,000 MT over 3-4 years, with about 30,000 MT planned in that period.
Working capital: medium-term target 90-100 days, expected to normalize in H2 FY27.
Five-year target of INR 5,000 crores revenue by FY31, described as a guidance that will not be revised; management hopes to beat it.
Debt-equity expected to stay below 0.6-0.7 at most, and around 0.3 once the plant is operational. Long-term loans to be tied up in coming quarters for a INR 300 crore capex plan.
capex_capacity: Narmadapuram (Madhya Pradesh) greenfield plant, third facility: foundation and civil works under way; critical machinery ordered; partial commissioning expected Q1 FY28.

Narmadapuram scope: 220 kV AC power cable line, HTLS (carbon-core and gap-type), e-beam and rubber cables. Approvals take about 1-1.5 years for 220 kV, about 12 months for 132 kV, and 3-6 months for full 66 kV range after the plant is operational.
Existing Dharuhera and Khushkhera plants running at optimal utilization; some further capex planned at both to lift revenue.
Current capacity is about 30,000 MT; management plans to double it with the new plant.
demand_pricing: Management cites T&D investment, renewables, railways and metro, and data centers as multiyear demand drivers; the National Electricity Plan projects about INR 5 lakh crore of EHV transmission investment in 2027-2032.
Management sizes HTLS reconductoring at about INR 50,000 crore over 5 years; the company says it is among the top 5 HTLS players in India and offers up to 765 kV conductors.

Copper hit record highs in the quarter; aluminium (over 75% of metal value consumed) softened. Policy is to book metal the next working day after a firm-price order, and to avoid firm-price orders beyond 3-4 months.

US tariffs: IEEPA tariffs struck down by the US Supreme Court in February 2026; Indian cables now at par with Asian and European competitors. Most customers now carry tariff changes on their accounts.
Management says it is not chasing volume at the expense of margin; it is seeking approvals in Middle East, Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia, with results expected within 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin glide path, given export claw-backs and the tariff effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating margin went from 1.3% in Q2 FY26 to 3.3% in Q3 and 5.2% in Q4, then 6.6% in Q1 FY27 and 7.3% in Q2 FY27. Management expects domestic margins to matter more, with US exposure kept at about 30% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 8% margin target before or after claw-backs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 8% target is ex of claw-backs and that net claw-backs would be shown separately, visible in Q3. It was also said to be hopeful, not yet achieved, for Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is firm, and what is the cancellation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 731 crore order book comprises firm orders only, with very rare cancellations, and that even in the worst US period there were no major cancellations. It also said FY27 revenue visibility is comfortable given the H1 run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR 5,000 crore FY31 target be achieved sooner, and what margin goes with it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY31 is a conservative guidance it will not revise, but it hopes to beat it. It gave no EBITDA margin target for that revenue level.

qa_highlights.question: What are the approval timelines for the new plant's product ranges, and what revenue will come before 220 kV approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant will run on 11/33/66 kV orders from day one, with 132 kV approvals in about 12 months and 220 kV taking longer. It said the INR 500 crore FY28 and INR 1,200 crore FY29 targets will not be driven mainly by 220 kV in the first two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter B2C or face new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has no plans to enter the high-cost B2C segment. B2C house wire is about INR 100 crore of roughly INR 2,000 crore revenue, and it expects B2B to be unaffected by new entrants given its footprint.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 300 crore capex be funded, and what will leverage be?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said debt-equity is 0.14x now, with long-term loans to be tied up in coming quarters. Management expects debt-equity to stay around 0.3 after the plant is operational, and below 0.6-0.7 at most.

risks_watch: Metal price volatility, particularly copper and aluminium, and the company's ability to pass it through in 3-4 month order cycles.
Working capital at 108 days versus the 90-100 day target; management attributes this to early supplier payments and expects normalization in H2.
Narmadapuram execution: 220 kV approvals take 1-1.5 years, and FY28/FY29 revenue targets depend on ramp-up and product qualification.
Claw-back amounts and their timing, which could affect reported margins versus the 8% operating margin target.
Management's shift toward non-US export markets is at an early stage, with results expected in 1-2 years and substantial contribution in 2-3 years.
Management said the new plant's approvals and ramp-up could push the HTLS margin benefit later.

We are not chasing volume at the cost of margin and most of our customers now carry tariff changes to their account.
We do not accept firm-price orders with long delivery periods beyond 3 to 4 months because that is how we protect ourselves from metal volatility.

530655|2026-03.headline: Goodluck India Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin above 10% and PAT up 34% YoY to over INR56 crore, while FY27 growth guidance was trimmed to 14-15%.
530655|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR1,097 crore, with management citing EBITDA margins above 10% and PAT up 34% YoY to over INR56 crore. Standalone Q4 sales fell to INR1,061.46 crore from INR1,104.62 crore, while standalone Q4 EBITDA rose 11.7% to INR104.19 crore. FY26 revenue growth of about 4% to 5% fell well short of the earlier 15-20% guidance, which management blamed on lower HRC prices and the West Asia conflict disrupting dispatches. Defence (artillery shells) began production in Jan-Feb 2026 after licensing in October 2025 and contributed about INR46 crore revenue and INR29 crore EBITDA in FY26, a margin inflated by start-up depreciation and interest per management.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1,104.62 crore in Q4 FY25 (down about 4%)

financial_highlights.value: about INR1,000 crore (working capital loans INR800 crore, term loan INR200 crore), cash and bank about INR50 crore
INR340 crore per analyst; management said capex/WIP about INR232 crore

segments.name: Defence (artillery shells, Goodluck Defence)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR46 crore and EBITDA about INR29 crore; capacity 150,000 shells with 75-80% execution targeted in FY27 (INR250-300 crore revenue indicated). Capacity expansion to 400,000 shells is planned at about INR400 crore capex, not yet started.

segments.name: Steel / legacy businesses
segments.commentary: Management cited FY26 production growth of about 11% against sales growth of about 5%, and 94% overall capacity utilisation. Standalone capacity is about 5 lakh tonnes, with a target of 6 lakh tonnes within 9-12 months.

segments.commentary: Utilisation was about 50% in FY26, targeted at 65-70% in FY27 with the ramp-up in progress.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 14-15% (earlier 15-20%), with management hopeful but conditional on West Asia conflict easing.
Defence EBITDA margin guided at 30-35% once volumes are sufficient, though management said FY26's margin was not sustainable.
Gross margin said to be sustainable (analyst cited about 27-28% to about 33% YoY improvement).
FY27 steel volume growth guided at 13-15%, with the West Asia crisis expected to be resolved.
Capacity addition of about 40,000-45,000 tonnes in FY27 (GI conduit and front fork tubes), with total capacity of 6 lakh tonnes targeted this financial year.
Term-loan repayments of INR54 crore in FY26 and INR51 crore in FY28. FY27 capex guidance deferred to next quarter.

Standalone steel capacity about 5 lakh tonnes, aiming for 6 lakh tonnes via GI conduit pipe and front fork tube lines (9-12 months).
Hydraulic tube utilisation about 50% in FY26, targeted at 65-70% in FY27.

demand_pricing: Management said defence demand is very strong and supply-constrained, citing ReArm Europe, ReArm Gulf and Replenish US, with market demand estimated at 8-9 million shells against 2-3 million new supply.
A recent order of about 20,000 shells was reported in the press at about INR26,100 per shell; management declined to confirm or guide on pricing.
Steel prices fell from April 2025 to April 2026 per management, though an analyst noted HRC rose from about INR48,000 to INR58,000 per tonne between December 2025 and May 2026.
West Asia conflict raised consumable costs; management said pass-through takes 1-2 quarters. Exports slowed by about 5-10% due to longer transit times.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 defence revenue and EBITDA, and why is the margin so high?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue was INR46 crore and EBITDA INR29 crore. Management attributed the high margin to start-up depreciation and interest being booked over only 2-3 months of production, with material stuck at port. It said 30-35% margins are the sustainable guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 steel business grow, given utilisation near 95%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is being added via GI conduit pipe and front fork tube lines, taking capacity to 6 lakh tonnes in 9-12 months, so volume growth of 13-15% is expected in steel.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 revenue grow only 4-5% against the 15-20% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lower steel prices from April 2025 to April 2026 hurt realisation, and the West Asia conflict disrupted dispatches in March. FY27 guidance was trimmed to 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex and debt rise above guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the INR340 crore capex figure, citing WIP of about INR232 crore. Debt rose because working capital increased from slower realisations and inventory build-up in the domestic glut.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and repayment schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR1,000 crore at March 2026 (INR800 crore working capital, INR200 crore term loan) against about INR50 crore cash. Term-loan repayments are INR54 crore in FY26 and INR51 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said conduit pipe margins are normally 15-25% and planning should use 15-20%. Front fork tube margins were put at 15-16%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is premature to call Q1. It expects margins to hold through product and market reshuffling, with a possible 5-10% export impact that could resolve within weeks.

Defence margin sustainability: FY26 margin was flattered by start-up costs, and the guided 30-35% has not yet been demonstrated.
Timing of the 400,000-shell expansion (about INR400 crore) and of the 6 lakh tonne steel capacity.

531162|2026-06.headline: Emami Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR1,039 crores, but PAT fell 16% to INR137 crores on tax normalisation and input-cost pressure.

EBITDA rose 6% to INR226 crores and PBT rose 4% to INR195 crores, while PAT fell 16% to INR137 crores due to a higher effective tax rate. Input costs rose 360 bps (about 200 bps from West Asia conflict and 160 bps from business mix), compressing gross margin. International business declined 12% due to West Asia disruption, mainly in OTC pain management, which cannot yet move out of India. Management moved reporting from brand-wise to category-wise.

531201|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR192.61 crore, up 43% QoQ and 12% YoY, as deferred Q1 export dispatches landed and domestic demand stayed strong. EBITDA excluding other income was INR40.06 crore (20.8% margin, up from 16.4% in Q1) and PAT was INR32.98 crore (16.5% margin). Management reiterated the FY27 revenue target of INR750 crore, with H1 sales of about INR330 crore and an order book of over INR550 crore. Margins remain below the roughly 28-30% levels of FY24-FY26, and management shifted guidance to absolute EBITDA (INR200-250 crore) rather than percentage margin.

financial_highlights.metric: Net working capital increase in H1
financial_highlights.change: includes financial assets up to about INR29 crore, per analyst

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Export mix was about 40% in Q2 and the order book is about 60:40 domestic:export. Middle East shipments were still below normal, offset partly by North America, where US tariffs were withdrawn in February. Management said export margins are higher than domestic, but did not quantify.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic demand was described as very strong throughout. Mix is mainly renewable-related transformers, with distribution transformers made in very small quantities.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR750 crore reiterated; management said it will be more than that, and analysts were told quarterly run-rate of INR225-230 crore is needed.
FY27 EBITDA target is more than INR200 crore (INR225-250 crore in absolute terms) with percentage margin unspecified; management would not give a margin number and said it is difficult to guess.
Margins expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 with about 100% capacity utilisation and more export orders.
FY28 revenue target about INR1,000 crore; FY29 target INR1,250-1,500 crore, with maximum INR1,500 crore at 100% utilisation of 14,000 MVA capacity.
Management said margins may fall as capacity grows, but targets absolute EBITDA growth; the same or higher EBITDA margin is targeted in the long term.
capex_capacity: Expansion Phase 3 adds 6,500 MVA, taking total capacity to 14,000 MVA; commissioning expected April 2027.
Civil foundation, PEB erection and utility work are in progress; all major production equipment has been ordered.
Current utilisation is about 80% of installed capacity in Q2; management expects about 100% in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Approvals for 220 kV class transformers expected 3-6 months after the new plant starts; existing customers have given verbal commitments for orders.
Management said breakeven utilisation on the new capacity is about 35-40%.
demand_pricing: Lead times: about 3-6 months for lower kV classes; more than 1 year for higher kV classes.
Raw material prices have stabilised but remain above pre-crisis levels; new orders are priced on current raw material costs. Management said the price rise was partly passed on, but not fully.
Working capital: no bank working-capital borrowing; receivables are mainly LC-backed (for example, 180-day LCs with interest borne by the customer).
Demand drivers cited: data centres, renewables, BESS, transmission and distribution. Management said capacity additions should not pressure margins for at least a couple of years.
Analyst cited raw material cost at about 71-72% of sales versus about 60% earlier; management did not dispute this.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 revenue jump came from deferred Q1 revenue, and what is the FY27 path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of Q2 came from Q1 deferrals and part from new orders. It said H2 quarterly sales should be INR225-230 crore to reach the INR750 crore target.

qa_highlights.question: How much did higher freight cut EBITDA, and can margins return to about 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: No quantification of freight impact was given. Management said margins will fall as volumes rise, but absolute EBITDA is targeted at INR225-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Are approvals in place for 220 kV transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: No approvals yet; applications follow plant commissioning, expected to take 3-6 months. Margins on 220 kV are expected to match current classes.

qa_highlights.question: Are there sustained margin outlooks (for example 23-25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a percentage. It said it is focused on absolute EBITDA; one analyst's implied 23-24% margin was framed as 'we will be trying for that'.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakeven utilisation on the new capacity, and what is the demand risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 35-40% utilisation is breakeven and that demand is supported by power demand growth. It acknowledged a trade-off between growth and margin.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any acquisition or diversification plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is exploring options but is bound by an NDA and will disclose once progressed.

FY27 EBITDA target of INR200 crore needs about 30% margin in H2 on the management's own assumptions, while Q2 margin was 20.8%.
Heavy capacity additions industry-wide and competition from new entrants, including Waaree, may pressure pricing.
Watch for 220 kV approvals after April 2027 commissioning, Q3 revenue run-rate of INR225 crore, and the export mix improving from 40%.
Working capital rose sharply in H1, with receivables and financial assets up; management attributes this to LC-backed terms.

rows.why: US tariffs were withdrawn in February and North America is offsetting weak Middle East shipments, but export mix is about 40% and management did not quantify export margin uplift.

531209|2026-03.headline: Nucleus Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue INR 224.77 crore, flat YoY, while order book rose to INR 1,044.31 crore from INR 656.68 crore in December 2025.
531209|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 224.77 crore, up 2% QoQ but down 1.8% YoY, and full-year revenue rose 5.3% to INR 876.03 crore. EBITDA fell sharply to INR 34.62 crore from INR 74.33 crore a year earlier, as cost of delivery rose to 70.1% of revenue from 57.3%. Net profit was INR 34.55 crore for the quarter versus INR 64.77 crore YoY, with full-year net profit down to INR 116.74 crore from INR 163 crore. The order book closed at INR 1,044.31 crore, up sharply QoQ, though management said most of it would convert to revenue over several quarters. Management flagged the loss of Bajaj Finance to a competitor it said Bajaj had invested in, and some Middle East orders were postponed due to the war situation.

qa_highlights.answer: Japan discussions with top banks are active and results may come in upcoming quarters. Sales headcount grew by about 40 to 50 executives over two years, across hunting, account management and partnerships.

qa_highlights.answer: Most orders are from India and the US. Revenue lags signing due to implementation cycles, so the impact is expected over one or two quarters and beyond.

531266|2026-03.headline: VST Tillers FY26 revenue rose 25% to INR1,240 crore; Q4 revenue up 9% to INR328 crore, operational EBITDA margin 14.2%.
531266|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 25% year on year to about INR1,240 crore (transcript also cites INR1,248 crore), led by power tillers, which grew 35% to 50,332 units. Q4 revenue rose 9% to INR328 crore, with operational EBITDA margin of 14.2% versus 13.4% a year earlier, and operational PAT (excluding fair value gains/losses) up 36% to about INR39 crore. Management declined to guide FY27 growth, citing fuel and commodity inflation, a monsoon forecast at 92% of LPA, and fertiliser availability concerns; it said April and May demand was good and expects Q1 growth over the prior year. Price hikes were taken across tillers and tractors at the end of April.

segments.name: Power tillers
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 50,332 units incl. exports, up 35% from 37,297; Q4 volume 12,958 vs 13,278 a year earlier (down year on year). Management called it the highest-ever annual volume.

segments.commentary: FY26 domestic volume 4,596 units, up 18.6%; Q4 domestic volume 1,244 units, up about 20%. Q4 tractor exports rose to 430 units from 260.

segments.commentary: FY26 volume 11,346 units vs 7,458 (about 52% growth); Q4 volume 2,947 units, up 27%. Front and rear rotary weeders launched in Q4.

segments.name: Power reapers
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 3,464 units, up 44%; seasonal, so minimal Q4 volume.

segments.name: Zetor / higher-HP tractors
segments.commentary: Single 8+2 variant (3.5 litre engine) currently; FY26 target is about 1,000 units; target 5,000-6,000 units by FY30. Sold through a few dealerships with month-on-month volume increases.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give a specific FY27 growth number; aspiration is 25% growth, with Q1 FY27 expected to grow over the prior year and Q2 dependent on how events unfold.
Operational EBITDA margin expected in a 12% to 14% range, versus the earlier 11% to 13% guidance.
Earlier stated path of 23% to 26% CAGR through FY30 toward INR3,000 crore revenue was reiterated as the goal, but management said current realities make this uncertain.
Zetor 4WD variant and additional variants planned this year; Netherlands-based European operation to launch in June/July 2026.
US market re-entry (electric tractor drivetrains): trials from 2026, product launch by end-2027.
All-India launch of electric weeders and electric tillers planned for early Q2 FY27.
Retail finance penetration to rise from about 10% in FY26 to a target of 20% in FY27.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Project Chatrapati: village-level workers appointed and many new retail counters opened to extend small and marginal farmer reach.
Supply chain: TOC-based model; SRM module being rolled out to give suppliers visibility of GRN and payments.
demand_pricing: April 2026 grew in both tractors and tillers; May demand described as good so far.
Price increases taken across power tillers and tractors towards end of April 2026; management said only part of the inflation had been passed through so far.
Cost pressure from fuel and commodity price rises; operational efficiencies are buffering margins for now.
Industry commentary: management agreed high base and flat agri income mean high growth is unlikely to continue; exact FY27 industry outcome hard to predict.
Fertiliser availability described as a likely problem, with no specific data; monsoon forecast at 92% of LPA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY27 and the FY30 growth trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; it is tracking month by month and quarter by quarter, expects Q1 growth over the prior year, and targets 25% but said specifics are difficult to call given uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins be maintained with growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance moved to a 12% to 14% operational EBITDA margin range, up from 11% to 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp-up plan for the Zetor brand and volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about 1,000 Zetor units in FY27 and 5,000 to 6,000 by FY30, with more variants and a 4WD variant to come.

qa_highlights.question: How are exports and the European business shaping up?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 export momentum was better; Netherlands-based operation to launch in June/July 2026 as planned, and management is confident of export growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory held at about 36 days; receivables cut from about 75 days to 51 days, with further reduction targeted over the next 2 to 3 years via the TOC supply chain model and SRM digitisation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large investment balance be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Three areas: technology and products, global expansion (US re-entry with launch by end-2027), and inorganic opportunities in adjacencies; no specific deal announced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the electric tractor investment in Zimeno Inc (US)?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment already provisioned for; US subsidy removal and tariffs halted drivetrain exports. Expertise gained is being used to launch electric weeders and tillers first, with an all-India launch planned for early Q2 FY27.

risks_watch: Fuel and commodity inflation may not be fully passed on to customers if it persists.
Monsoon distribution and timing (IMD forecast 92% of LPA) could affect farm incomes and machinery demand.
Fertiliser shortages reported anecdotally.
Fair value losses on investments continue to affect reported PAT; Q4 loss was heavier than in Q3.
Q4 tillers volume declined year on year (12,958 vs 13,278); watch whether this recurs.
Zetor volumes depend on a limited dealer footprint and are at an early stage.
Land sale: no update given.

531266|2026-06.headline: VST Tillers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% to INR313.4 crores, but operational EBITDA margin fell about 45 bps to 12.85% on raw material inflation.
531266|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 11% YoY to INR313.4 crores from INR282.4 crores, and PAT rose to INR48.7 crores from INR44.6 crores. Operational EBITDA margin (excluding other income and fair value gains) was 12.85%, versus 13.3% a year earlier, with management attributing the drop to commodity and raw material inflation. Power tillers grew about 18% and power weeders about 56% in volume, while domestic tractors grew 4.5% and tractor exports were 275 units. Management declined to give a full-year FY27 outlook, saying it would be clearer in about a month, and said the July volume softness reflected a high base.

financial_highlights.metric: Operational EBITDA (excl. other income and fair value gain)

segments.name: Power tillers
segments.commentary: Volume grew about 18% in Q1; management cites 16-20% tiller growth over recent quarters and expects 15-20% to continue. Bajaj Finance retail financing volume roughly doubled to about 1,000 units from about 400 a year earlier, but still only 8-9% of retail sales versus a 15-20% target.

segments.name: Power weeders (SFM)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 56% in Q1 and management has been clocking 50-60% growth for several quarters. Retail counters added more than 500 in three months, taking the network toward a target of about 2,000 counters by year-end, on top of 750-800 SFM dealers.

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 4.5% in Q1 but supply lagged demand during ramp-up of the new variant, per management. Management expects Q2 growth, with substantial volume increases in Q3 and Q4; 40-50 HP is described as a crowded segment.

segments.name: Tractors (exports)
segments.commentary: 275 tractors sold in Q1. Europe: about 1,400-1,500 tractors per management, with entry into Turkey and the Nordics planned. Africa: 75 HP tractor shipments started. US expansion described as unclear.

segments.name: Reapers
segments.commentary: Seasonal product; volumes expected to pick up in Q2 with the harvest season. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 outlook given; management said it is too early and will comment in about a month, since H2 depends on monsoon and rabi sowing.
Management said demand outlook is positive through September, with the next 15-20 days critical for kharif crop survival.
Long-term target of about 20,000 tractors by FY30 (including 5,000-6,000 international units); revenue vision of INR3,000 crores by 2030.
More than 30 tractor variants planned over the next three years; three global platforms (A, B, C) to launch over 12-36 months.
Tractor dealer additions targeted at 50-60 in FY27, versus 40-50 last year.
capex_capacity: A new production facility will need investment in roughly the next two years, per the CEO.
Tiller-tractor hybrid product (geared, with differential) to roll out from the factory starting this month, with substantial volume in Q3 and Q4.
International distributor logistics infrastructure delayed from Q1 but expected operational in Q3.
Hydrostatic transmission tractor being seeded for export markets, not sold in India.
Bangalore land of about 19 acres; manufacturing already moved out, only administrative office remains; no monetisation decision yet.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no demand issue in tillers; July volumes declined YoY against a very high base.
Tractor 40-50 HP segment is crowded and highly competitive; company is acquiring market share through product breadth.
Commodity inflation (steel, forgings, castings, aluminium, copper), elevated and volatile natural rubber prices, and high crude and freight costs weighed on margins.

Emission norm: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026, which management says will not create a big cost increase for end customers. Stage 5 for all tractors in 2032 could add 25-30% to tractor technology cost today, though this may fall over time.
Possible 100% US tariff under a bill in Congress is a risk to US expansion plans.

qa_highlights.question: Why is tractor growth lagging the industry despite new launches, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 supply did not fully meet demand during the new-variant ramp-up; management expects Q2 growth and substantial increases in Q3-Q4. Strategy includes more than 30 variants over three years and state-by-state rollout of the FENTM series, starting with Gujarat, then Maharashtra.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the Bajaj Finance tie-up and other financing partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail financing reached about 1,000 units versus about 400 a year earlier, but only 8-9% of retail, against a 15-20% target. Other partners include Chola, TVS and nationalised banks.

qa_highlights.question: Is tiller export viable, and what new products are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were about 300 units last year. A geared tiller with differential for Europe and India and an electric tiller/weeder are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any moderation in demand given July volume decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed July to a high base in tillers. It sees growth continuing at least through September, with tillers at 16-20% growth and weeders at 50-60%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capital allocation policy and non-core asset plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the policy is to maximise shareholder value and it expects to deploy capital over the next 18-24 months. No development on non-core assets yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are the implications of upcoming emission norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026 is already ready. TREM 3A from April 2028 is covered. Full Stage 5 for tractors in 2032 may add 25-30% to technology cost at current prices.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression from raw material inflation; Q1 margin down about 45 bps YoY.
Tractor market share: domestic tractor growth of 4.5% trails the industry; July volumes were lower YoY.
Monsoon uncertainty over the next 15-20 days affects kharif output and rabi sowing.
Tariff risk to US expansion, and the possible 100% tariff bill in Congress.
Possible capex for a new facility in about two years; capital deployment plans to be disclosed in 18-24 months.
Management has not given a FY27 outlook; next update expected in about one month.

531279|2026-03.headline: Trishakti FY26 revenue rose ~90% to INR 32.44 crore, but EBITDA includes INR 4.58 crore subvention income and receivables sit near 200 days.
531279|2026-03.overview: Trishakti reported FY26 revenue of about INR 32.44 crore (up ~90% YoY), EBITDA of INR 20.21 crore (62% margin) and PAT of INR 7.66 crore (25% margin), with Q4 revenue above three times YoY. Reported EBITDA includes INR 4.58 crore of subvention income booked under other income, which management calls operating in nature. Fresh capex was INR 210 crore against ~INR 100 crore guidance, taking the fleet to over 140 machines. Management said FY27 order book is INR 60-62 crore, but trade receivables (~200 days) and debt-to-equity (near 2:1) remain the key open items.

segments.name: Crane / heavy equipment rental (sole business)
segments.commentary: Management describes the company as a pure-play rental platform with 140+ machines and near-full utilisation, serving L&T, Reliance, Tata, RVNL and NCC. Gross yield is ~3% per month and targeted ROC is 22-25%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 crane hiring revenue projection of INR 62.5 crore and INR 95 crore in FY28 is shown in the investor presentation; management says INR 33 crore of FY26 is an actual and FY27 billing run-rate is ~INR 5 crore per month.
FY27 order book stated at INR 60-62 crore, excluding variable overtime; contracts run to 31 December on paper and management expects extensions.
Target ROC 22-25%; management says ROC guidance is conservative because the INR 400 crore capex will not be full-year.
Management expects receivables to normalise in FY27 after a family settlement is cleared; expects debt-to-equity to settle around 1.5 over time.
Fleet target for next phase is 50-250 ton machines for the first ~INR 400 crore of capex, to keep utilisation above 95%.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of INR 210 crore against INR 100 crore guidance; roughly INR 150 crore of machines bought in H2 alone.
Fleet grew from eight machines (FY24) to over 140 machines; plan is to reach north of 200 machines.
About INR 27-28 crore of machines moved out of CWIP recently; management says CWIP is now zero.
Revenue lags capex by 1-1.5 months (compliance, transport, TPI); management says FY28 will show a 12-month run-rate.
Repays ~2.5% of loans monthly; expects to add ~INR 100 crore of borrowing as repayments of INR 40-45 crore accrue.
demand_pricing: Management says it receives new RFQs daily for 250-750 ton machines and sees no demand slowdown.
Cited Reliance's Kutch renewable expansion (civil work done, cranes expected in next 2-3 months) as an example.
Yields of ~3% monthly are said to apply to machines below 100 tons; higher-tonnage machines have lower yield but higher margin.
Management says the company works with tier-1 clients only; tier-2/3 EPC payment cycles can exceed five months.
Management says it is not working with government bodies and is focusing on private capex.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for crane and rental demand over 2-3 years, and any signs of slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no slowdown and expects demand to rise; availability of 500+ ton machines may constrain growth, so near-term focus is 50-250 ton machines.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days still ~200 with tier-1 clients, and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it to a small family settlement from 2023 and a INR 1 crore written-off inter-company receivable; says it will normalise in FY27. Under-six-month receivables are said to be about 45 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did unbilled revenue rise from ~INR 2 crore to ~INR 4.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says fleet doubled H1 to H2 (from ~INR 125 crore to ~INR 250 crore), and bill submission takes 20-22 days due to client compliance; management says unbilled will always be present and there is no bad-debt risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is subvention income and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management describes it as a financing arrangement between OEM banks and the NBFC, passed to the company as interest waivers; it is booked in Q4 because Q1-Q3 were unaudited. Management calls it part of core hiring business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall below the 60% benchmark in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says other income is part of core hiring; margins are stable on an adjusted basis. An analyst computed ~58% including subvention in revenue, versus a September quarter level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it bought INR 60-65 crore of machines in Q4, paying 20-25 days of advance labour and 3-7 days for gate passes; other expenses rose from spares for FY24 machines as free-of-cost service periods ended.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY26 leverage and debt-to-equity capped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-to-equity will remain around 1.5 to 2 times equity and that it intends to stay below 2 times; cost of borrowing is ~5% flat.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are ~3% monthly yields as competition rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says yields are sustainable, with the 3% mark applying mainly to sub-100 ton machines and blended yields holding up.

risks_watch: Trade receivables of ~200 days; management promises FY27 normalisation tied to a family settlement.
Debt-to-equity near 2:1, with ~INR 159 crore of payables/other liabilities expected to shift to borrowings; the timing and amount are not quantified.
Subvention income of INR 4.58 crore (about 23% of FY26 EBITDA) is complex and was booked in Q4; management offered to explain it off-call.
Margin sensitivity to capex-driven costs (labour pre-deployment, spares) and revenue lag of 1-1.5 months.
Contract tenure on paper only to 31 December; management expects extensions but has not confirmed them.
Machine availability for 500+ ton machines and operational downtime risk.

531279|2026-06.headline: Trishakti Q1 FY27 total income up ~310% YoY to INR 1,680 lakh, EBITDA ~INR 1,087 lakh at ~65% margin, PAT INR 430 lakh.
531279|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR 1,680 lakh (up nearly 310% YoY), EBITDA of INR 1,087 lakh (about four times YoY, ~65% margin), PBT of INR 538 lakh and PAT of INR 430 lakh, described as the strongest quarter in company history. Fleet utilisation was stated at 100% with fleet of roughly 155-158 machines. Management announced entry into wind energy equipment rental (900-ton cranes) and intent to expand into UAE and KSA, both subject to approvals. 531279|2026-09.headline: Trishakti Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 133% YoY to INR 1,551 lakhs, with EBITDA margin of 60.89%.
531279|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR 1,551 lakhs (up 133% YoY), EBITDA of INR 944 lakhs (up about 141%) and PAT of INR 519 lakhs (up 223%). H1 FY27 revenue was INR 2,989 lakhs, EBITDA INR 1,790 lakhs and PAT INR 949 lakhs. Management said about INR 370 crore of the INR 400 crore FY25-FY27 capex programme (incl. GST) is deployed, and announced "Mission 2030" targeting cumulative gross block above INR 1,000 crore by FY30. Receivable days rose over the past two years; management attributed this to a family settlement and said the cycle will normalise to about 60-65 days by year end.

financial_highlights.metric: Total H1 revenue incl. other income (per Q&A)
Gross block deployed vs FY25-27 programme (per Q&A)
financial_highlights.value: Approx INR 370 crore of INR 400 crore

segments.name: Crane and equipment rental (only segment discussed)
segments.commentary: Fleet includes rough terrain, all terrain, crawler, truck-mounted cranes, AWPs and 70-80m man lifts; management says fleet utilisation has been about 100% for three years. Management claims current ARR is about INR 78 crore after INR 40 crore of machines added in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 60-65 crore retained; management said it expects to surpass this, with an executable order book of about INR 78 crore and core revenue from operations above INR 75 crore.
Mission 2030: cumulative gross block above INR 1,000 crore by FY30, possibly by FY29 if demand holds; peak revenue of around INR 300 crore cited.
Net debt expected at INR 400-500 crore until FY30; debt-to-equity to stay under 2 for the next 1-1.5 years; deleveraging expected after FY28.
Gross block expected to exceed INR 400 crore by FY27 year end, with INR 90-95 crore (ex-GST) in CWIP to be deployed in Q3 and about INR 125 crore of wind energy capex to arrive from early November.
ARR expected to reach about INR 120 crore from December 2026 to FY28 Q3 as CWIP machines deploy.
UAE and KSA expansion deferred until balance sheet deleverages; paperwork said to be 60-70% complete.
capex_capacity: INR 400 crore FY25-FY27 capex programme: about INR 370 crore deployed (incl. GST), more than 90% complete and ahead of schedule by about six months.
CWIP of about INR 77-78 crore ex-GST (INR 95 crore incl. GST) yet to be deployed in Q3 FY27; contracts reportedly already won for these machines.

Wind energy fleet expansion of about INR 125 crore; machines to arrive from early November; OEMs can supply only 4-5 machines per month in India; management targets replacing 250-300 machines as wind turbines shift from 3.3 to 5.2 MW.

Mission 2030 implies about INR 600-700 crore of incremental capex over three years (about 2.5% of net debt repaid monthly per management); 80-ton tower cranes for data centre work in transit, expected October-November.
Two 70-80m man lifts in fleet; management says about 20-22 such machines exist in India.
demand_pricing: Management says it receives RFQs daily as a central vendor to L&T, Reliance, Tata Steel and others; capex is concentrated in Gujarat and Odisha.
Management says crawler cranes above 150 tonnes are in strong demand; lower-tonnage truck-mounted cranes (80-100 t) are also in demand.
Fleet utilisation about 100% versus an industry figure of about 80% cited in the presentation; management attributes this to 11-12 month contracts versus competitors' 3-4 month contracts.

Management said rental yields are stable and not expected to rise; machine pricing in India is fixed by rental yields. Double-shift operation on 15-20% of machines is said to add about 50% revenue on those machines.
Management said a data centre tower crane generates much higher yield, and specialised 70-80m man lifts earn more than two times current fleet monthly revenue per machine.

qa_highlights.question: Why have debtor days risen over two years, and what is the plan to fix it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a family settlement from three years ago that extended the cycle; about INR 75 lakh of provision was created this quarter and the cycle should return to about 60-65 days by year end. Management also said about INR 3 crore is over one year old, linked to the family settlement.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects net debt of INR 400-500 crore until FY30, funded by bank debt and internal accruals; most FY24-FY25 machines to be free of bank financing by FY28. Only fixed-rate loans apart from the CC limit, which was unused since January; 25 bps rate increase expected on new funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on equity dilution and UAE/KSA expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is the first priority and equity dilution is a final option; it could double the fleet by next year if debt is hard to raise. UAE and KSA expansion depends on internal accruals or equity; KSA local-stake rules reportedly changed after 1 May, allowing 100% ownership.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance INR 60-65 crore or INR 70-80 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance has always been INR 60-65 crore, and that INR 72 crore is only the current ARR; H1 revenue from operations was about INR 30 crore and it expects to beat guidance given the order book and H2 seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why are yields not improving with the new fleet, and is sustainability at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields are fixed and not expected to rise, but are sustainable; it cited three years of OEM free-of-cost servicing that defers opex, and buying power giving 5-10% machine discount versus competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the receivable cycle elevated, and what caused the move in other current liabilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said month-end revenue is not billed for 10-12 days because overtime is computed, so trade receivables run high; the move to monthly GST filing shifted about INR 2.5-3 crore of billing, and cash flow should improve from this quarter. Other current liabilities relate to machine funding timing.

risks_watch: Receivable days remain elevated; management promises normalisation to about 60-65 days by Q4 FY27, with the annual report providing clarity.
Mission 2030 assumes fleet utilisation above 90% through FY30; management acknowledged this may be bold.
Debt-to-equity to remain under 2 for 1-1.5 years; net debt of INR 450-500 crore at peak, and possible equity dilution if debt funding is constrained.
Customer concentration in Gujarat and Odisha capex cycle; no soft commitments from customers for expansion, per management.
Machine import dependence above 250 tonnes and rising global machine costs; yields not expected to rise.
Gross block and revenue timing depend on delivery of wind energy and tower crane machines, now in transit.

Our guiding principle is simple. We want to grow with India, build for the long-term, and turn our ambition into measurable execution.

rows.why: Net debt is guided at INR 400-500 crore until FY30 and debt-to-equity under 2 for 1-1.5 years, with most FY24-25 machines free of bank financing by FY28, but Mission 2030 capex of about INR 600-700 crore keeps leverage high.

531335|2026-03.headline: Zydus Wellness Q4 FY26 net sales grew 62.1% on Comfort Click, but net profit fell 5.8% as seasonal brands dropped 9.8% in the domestic business.
531335|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales rose 62.1% YoY, driven by the Comfort Click acquisition, with international like-to-like growth of 31.4% and domestic growth of only 1.7%. Domestic seasonal brands fell 9.8% as a delayed summer and rain in March and mid-April left retail and wholesale pipelines unfilled, while skin and hair care rose 39.7% and food and nutrition rose 9.4%. EBITDA grew 42.2% to INR 2,701 million, but net profit fell 5.8% due to higher finance costs from the acquisition debt, higher amortization of acquired brands and exceptional items. Management said operating leverage and the 17-18% EBITDA margin goal remain intact, while the seasonal recovery is expected from May onwards.

financial_highlights.metric: International incl. Comfort Click like-to-like growth (Q4)

financial_highlights.change: Seasonal -9.8%, skin and hair care +39.7%, food and nutrition +9.4%

Excluding exceptional items and amortization of acquired brands: +2.3%

segments.name: Seasonal brands (domestic)

segments.name: Skin and hair care (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 39.7% and FY26 grew 21.9%. Everyuth grew at strong double digits in FY26 and Cuticolor has been in the portfolio for about six months, sold in organized trade, modern trade and e-commerce.

segments.commentary: Q4 grew 9.4% and FY26 grew 15.5%. RiteBite Max Protein grew at roughly 50% in FY26 (about INR 244 crore per analyst), and management said actual branded growth is higher than reported due to contract manufacturing optimization.

Complan NutriGro was relaunched and moved to direct supply in the kids segment; VieMax by Complan launched in adult nutrition.

Management said no divestments are planned, and capital allocation across brands is considered appropriate.

Quick commerce is about 7-8% of total domestic business; e-commerce is about 44-45% of organized trade.
Sugar Free Green reported its 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth; sweetener market share rose 24 bps (MAT March 2026); Nutralite grew at double digits despite gas supply headwinds.
Management said supply disruption from the Middle East conflict has been limited, affecting only a very small part of the business.
Gross margins were in line with plan; management cited brand-level margin improvements and exits from low-margin products.

qa_highlights.question: What weighed on seasonal growth and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed weak North and East markets, March/April rains, and a missing retailer pipeline build ahead of summer. It expects a recovery from May onwards but declined to forecast the season.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be expected to move toward the 17-18% aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins are in line with plan and the miss was driven by mix from weak seasonal sales. Umesh Parikh said operating leverage will play out across the business excluding Comfort Click.

qa_highlights.question: Is quick commerce changing the innovation and channel approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sharvil Patel said the portfolio is designed for quick commerce consumers while keeping the traditional channel SKUs. Quick commerce is about 7-8% of domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Comfort Click margin trajectory and is it EPS accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Umesh Parikh said Comfort Click is in line with or slightly ahead of expectations, and it became EPS accretive in Q4. The currency tailwind is about 3%, the gap between reported and constant-currency growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company divest slow-growing categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sharvil Patel said there are no plans to divest any category and no major change in capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is Cuticolor gaining traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Cuticolor is positioned as a derma-backed, Korean-origin safe hair colour sold in organized trade, modern trade and e-commerce, with repeat buying and early traction, after about six months in the portfolio.

531344|2026-03.headline: CONCOR posted record FY26 throughput of 5.58 million TEUs (+9.6%), but PAT fell 4.5% and Q4 domestic EBIT margin collapsed to 0.2%.

531431|2026-06.headline: Shakti Pumps Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37.9% YoY to INR859 crores, but EBITDA margin stayed near 9.6% on raw material and realisation pressure.
531431|2026-06.overview: Management reported a record quarterly revenue of INR859 crores (up 37.9% YoY from INR623 crores) and PAT of INR52 crores, up 35% QoQ, with PAT margin at 6% versus 4.5% in Q4 FY26. EBITDA margin was about 9.6%, which management said was broadly stable sequentially, while YoY EBITDA fell from INR144 crores to INR83 crores due to raw material inflation (about INR36 crores) and lower sales realisation (about INR25 crores). Solar pump installations rose 57.6% YoY to 27,678 units, and the order book was about INR1,000 crores as of 22 July 2026. Management reiterated a target of INR5,000 crores revenue by FY29 and tied margin recovery to PM-KUSUM 2.0 launch and easing raw material prices.

vs INR144 crores a year ago

segments.name: Solar pumps (core)
segments.commentary: Installations up 57.6% YoY to 27,678 pumps; order book about INR1,000 crores (B2G, mostly government), management says executable within two quarters. Recent INR350 crore Maharashtra order cited.

segments.name: Solar rooftop
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8 crores vs INR2 crores a year ago. Company registered as brand owner under PM Surya Ghar; 0.5 GW panel plant expected to support integrated offering. Rooftop order book described as negligible.

segments.name: Cash and retail sales
segments.commentary: Sales of INR24 crores in Q1 FY27, described as strong growth, supported by dealer network expansion.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Described as steady; about INR100 crores of export orders received every quarter. Management said the Middle East conflict had not materially affected the business.

segments.name: EV motors
segments.commentary: In trial and validation phase; management expects 6-9 months more before revenue ramp, with meaningful contribution from FY28.

guidance_outlook: Target of becoming an INR5,000 crore company by FY29 (within three years), with no split by business given.
Management expects EBITDA margins to improve gradually QoQ as raw material prices ease and PM-KUSUM 2.0 orders arrive.
Post 2.2 GW integrated cell and module capacity, management expects about 3% EBITDA margin expansion; rooftop plus module integrated target around 15% EBITDA margin.
No EBITDA target given for three years out; company says it will update quarterly.

Order book of INR1,000 crores expected to be executed over the next two quarters, plus new orders from pipeline; management said run rate of last two quarters to be maintained, subject to rain and flood conditions.
Capex of INR1,500-1,700 crores to be completed by September 2027, with about INR800 crores in FY27 and the balance in FY28.
capex_capacity: 0.5 GW DCR solar module plant expected to be completed in September 2026; management said it would run at 40-50% in the first month, 60-70% in the second, then about 85%.
2.2 GW integrated DCR cell and module project targeted for September 2027.
Pump plant capacity expansion slated for November 2026, per management.
Company currently buys about 50-60 MW of solar pump modules externally each month; in-house capacity to replace this over time.

Working capital limits of about INR1,800 crores from about 10 Indian banks and one Qatar bank; term loan of about INR800 crores for the 2.2 GW project. Two QIPs funded equity, including INR200 crores with no bank loan.
demand_pricing: PM-KUSUM 2.0 described as ready for launch and with the PMO; management said it could be announced within weeks. Management expects orders under it to begin by end of the current quarter.
Other states' schemes (MP, Rajasthan) have not yet launched and are expected alongside KUSUM 2.0.
Receivables: about INR760 crores not yet due, about INR560 crores over 180 days, and INR477 crores retention amount. Maharashtra payments have started coming in.
Raw material cost rose about 6% YoY (stainless steel, copper, aluminium, mild steel); management said some inputs softened by INR1-1.5 recently.
Realisation impact of about 4% YoY attributed partly to sales mix across PM-KUSUM and Magel Tyala orders.
Management said no El Nino-driven demand uptick so far; higher-HP pump demand emerging in Haryana and Punjab.
No hedging of raw material prices, as management views the pressure as temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of raw material and realisation on margins, and when will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said YoY EBITDA margin impact was about 10%: about INR36 crores (6%) from raw materials and INR25 crores (4%) from lower realisation. It expects gradual QoQ margin improvement as raw material prices ease and KUSUM 2.0 orders arrive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the business split of the INR5,000 crore FY29 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split revenue by business, saying only that all segments are expected to contribute and that updates will be given quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,500-1,700 crores to be completed by September 2027, with about INR800 crores in FY27 and the rest in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company expect to win PM Surya Ghar orders without margin hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not take a margin hit; the segment is B2B with lower margins, and integrated inverters, structures and panels are expected to help it become a leader.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV motors timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The product is in validation and testing for another 6-9 months, with meaningful revenue expected from FY28 onwards.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin remains near 10% versus 24-25% in FY24-25; management has not given a multi-year margin target.
Receivables: INR560 crores over 180 days and INR477 crores retention outstanding; collection timing depends on state nodal agencies.
PM-KUSUM 2.0 launch timing has slipped in messaging, and other state schemes depend on it.
Order book of about INR1,000 crores; management declined to give quarter-wise execution split, and monsoon conditions may affect execution.
Capacity commissioning timelines (0.5 GW in September 2026; 2.2 GW in September 2027) and ramp-up at 40-85% utilisation.
Competitive intensity in tenders and rising raw material prices across the industry; EV revenue timeline remains uncertain.
531431|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, volumes and capacity timelines, but cautious and non-committal on margins, EBITDA targets, and segment-wise revenue splits. Management repeatedly framed margin pressure as temporary and external without providing a numerical recovery path.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA margin remained broadly stable on a sequential basis at 9.6%.
we view these margin pressures as temporary and largely external in nature, rather than reflective of any structural issue in the business.
We cannot give an EBITDA target for three years right now. We update it every quarter.

Going forward, with KUSUM 2.0 expected to come in and raw material prices likely to ease as the geopolitical situation stabilizes, we expect margins to improve gradually on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
we are making these investments with the goal of becoming a INR5,000 crores company over the next three years.
