531431|2026-09.headline: Shakti Pumps Q2 FY27: solar EPC revenue ~INR543 crores on 23,865 pumps installed (+7% YoY), with PM-KUSUM 2.0 approval still pending.
531431|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 solar pump installations of 23,865 units, up about 7% YoY, and cited roughly 70% growth across rooftop, solar domestic and industrial businesses. Q2 solar EPC revenue was about INR543 crores and exports about INR95 crores, with H1 solar EPC at about INR1,230 crores and H1 exports at INR177 crores. Margins were squeezed: raw material costs rose about 3% QoQ, offset by about 2% cost reduction, leaving EBITDA down about 1% QoQ. Working capital worsened, with about INR400 crores of collections slipping from Q2 into October, lifting debt to about INR830 crores before falling below INR500 crores. The call centred on the delayed PM-KUSUM 2.0 approval and the start of 500 MW solar panel trial production.

segments.name: Solar pumps (government and EPC)
segments.commentary: Q2 solar EPC revenue of approx. INR543 crores on 23,865 installations; H1 solar EPC approx. INR1,230 crores. Magel Tyala orders executed in Q2, with a 100,000-pump tender expected next quarter; 25,000-pump allocation in the latest market-mode tender was capped at 25% by an ADB condition.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q2 exports approx. INR95 crores; H1 exports INR177 crores including Uganda project. Middle East exposure is being offset by new markets; logistics handled by air freight where needed.

segments.name: Rooftop and solar domestic/industrial
segments.commentary: Management cited approx. 58% YoY rooftop revenue growth and approx. 70% growth across rooftop, domestic and industrial businesses. Rooftop volumes are constrained until Shakti-branded panels from the 500 MW plant are available.

segments.name: Solar cells and modules (500 MW panel plant, 2.2 GW cell plant)
segments.commentary: 500 MW panel facility has started trial production, with commercial production expected in 1 to 1.5 months. The 2.2 GW cell plant is about INR200 crores spent and due for completion in FY28, with strong revenue after March 2028.

guidance_outlook: PM-KUSUM 2.0 approval is expected in Q3 FY27, with execution results anticipated in Q4 FY27; management declined to give a firm launch date.
Management said the order book can cover Q3 FY27, with KUSUM 2.0 and Magel Tyala orders to add from next quarter; the company stated an order book of INR750 crores to be executed within 90 days.
Total FY27 capex plan is INR1,700 crores; approx. INR400 crores is expected in H2 FY27.
Debt is expected to decline further by March 2027, and collections to improve by year-end.
EBITDA guidance withheld until KUSUM 2.0 price list and tender rates are clear; margin benefit from the 500 MW panel plant expected to be visible next quarter but not yet quantified.
capex_capacity: Pump and motor facility under QIP 1 capex is underway; VFD and structure facilities are complete.
500 MW solar panel plant has started trial production; commercial production expected within 1 to 1.5 months.
2.2 GW solar cell plant: approx. INR200 crores spent to date; completion scheduled for FY28.
Pumps and motors capacity utilisation approx. 68% in H1 FY27.
Management said pump installation capacity will be expanded to speed up execution of new orders.
demand_pricing: Pricing flexibility is limited in solar, which is the majority of sales; only one active tender, concentrated in one state under Magel Tyala, and competitors chase the same opportunity.
Management said rates did not decline in the latest tender and expects rates to improve as bidders recognise that low quotes offer no advantage in market-mode tenders.
Raw material prices (MS, steel, copper) rose on the Strait of Hormuz conflict; management expects stabilisation.
Karnataka: approx. 12,000 pumps installed; management claims approx. 40% market share after late entry.
Export growth depends on geopolitical developments over the next six months; Uganda phase two funding is being requested from India Exim Bank.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins improve steadily, and can EBITDA be strong next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to guide EBITDA until KUSUM 2.0 price lists and tender rates are known; raw material costs rose about 3% QoQ, offset by about 2% savings.

qa_highlights.question: Can the revenue break-up for Q2 and H1 be provided?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2: solar EPC approx. INR543 crores, exports approx. INR95 crores, domestic/industrial/others approx. INR40 crores. H1: solar EPC approx. INR1,230 crores, exports INR177 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt and receivables rise, and where will debt end the year?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores of collections were received in October, not Q2. Debt was approx. INR830 crores, now below INR500 crores, expected to fall further by March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the solar cell and panel capex, and total FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: 500 MW panel line in trial production; 2.2 GW cell plant has approx. INR200 crores spent, due in FY28. Total FY27 capex is INR1,700 crores, with approx. INR400 crores in H2.

qa_highlights.question: If KUSUM 2.0 is delayed, what will utilise capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to Magel Tyala orders in hand for next quarter, a 100,000-pump tender, and open-market cash sales of solar pumps.

qa_highlights.question: Why was realisation flat, and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation was roughly flat, with about 1% impact from sales mix. Management expects improvement but would quantify it only after the next tender price is derived; the ADB condition capped the company at 25,000 pumps in the latest tender.

risks_watch: PM-KUSUM 2.0 approval timing: management has repeatedly moved expectations, and it has been awaited for about six months.
Working capital: receivables of approx. INR1,750 crores and delayed ADB-linked payments; watch whether debt stays below INR500 crores by March 2027.
Raw material inflation (MS, steel, copper) linked to the Strait of Hormuz conflict, with pricing flexibility limited in solar tenders.
Execution of the 500 MW panel plant (approvals, licences, testing) and whether rooftop revenue scales as management expects.
Geopolitical impact on export markets, especially the Middle East, and dependence on the Uganda project.
531431|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operations, volumes and the solar panel and cell roadmap, but cautious and often non-committal on KUSUM 2.0 timing, EBITDA and realisation, repeatedly deferring numbers to the next tender.
key_quotes: Despite challenging international conditions and logistics constraints in certain markets, we honoured our commitments to dealers and customers, using air freight wherever necessary.
Our margins depend on selling prices and raw material costs, which increased by approximately 3% quarter on quarter.
The order book we have needs to be completed within 90 days, and we are confident of executing it within that timeframe.

We established the 500 MW solar plant with the objective of expanding margins, but the benefits will not be immediate as approvals, licences, testing, and operational stabilisation are still underway.

531508|2026-03.headline: Eveready FY26 revenue grew 8.2% and EBITDA margin held at 11.5%; Jammu alkaline plant (INR200 crore, 360 mn units peak) inaugurated 22 April 2026.
531508|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 8.2% and EBITDA grew 8.9%, with full-year EBITDA margin at 11.5% despite steep zinc cost increases in H2. Batteries grew 9.3%, flashlights 3% and lighting about 8.1%, with calibrated price hikes in carbon zinc and alkaline. The Jammu alkaline battery plant was inaugurated on 22 April 2026 and commercial production is expected within weeks. Management guided to holding margins near 11.5% in FY27, and debt was reduced by over INR100 crore in FY26 with further reduction targeted, helped by Noida leasehold sales.

financial_highlights.value: about INR116 crore (leasehold transfer completed 30 March 2026)
about INR136 crore (INR44 crore advance received)

segments.name: Batteries
segments.commentary: Grew 9.3% in FY26 and make up about two-thirds of business. Alkaline is nearly 10% of battery business (about 15% of category saliency per management) with volume growth over 20% CAGR; company alkaline share about 16%, up from under 10% a year ago.

segments.name: Flashlights
segments.commentary: Grew 3% in FY26 on a mature battery-operated base; rechargeables and new power bank and charger launches are the focus. BIS mandate fully implemented by end-January 2026 is seen favouring branded players.

segments.name: Lighting and electrical accessories
segments.commentary: Grew about 8.1% in FY26; management called the recent double-digit quarter-on-quarter growth sustainable. Flashlights and lighting with adjacencies make up about one-third of business.

segments.name: Mosquito racquets and mobile accessories
segments.commentary: Mosquito racquets, launched about 1.5 years ago, now hold a leadership position in urban markets; mobile accessories launched in FY26 via e-commerce.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be held around the FY26 level of 11.5%, with headwinds stronger than last year.
Zinc prices expected to keep rising into subsequent quarters; a further price increase may be needed in Q2 if cost volatility persists.
Jammu plant: commercial production in a few weeks, more than 100 million units in year one, phased ramp-up; operational breakeven from year one per CFO, payback 5-6 years.
Alkaline saliency expected to reach 20-25% of batteries in about 3 years, with zinc at 75%; company aims to exit with about 20% alkaline share.
Debt reduction to continue in FY27; no capex planned beyond routine capex; Plot B2 proceeds of about INR90 crore expected in FY27.
Tax: company expects to transition to Section 115BAA (22%) from FY27, subject to utilisation of carried-forward business losses.
A&P spend to stay at about 10% of sales.
capex_capacity: Jammu alkaline battery plant: investment about INR200 crore, peak capacity 360 million alkaline batteries per year, phased ramp-up; inaugurated 22 April 2026 by the J&K Lieutenant Governor.
Jammu also has lines for zinc batteries, flashlights and lighting products, enabling backward and forward integration.

Noida plant: exited, with Plot B1 leasehold transfer completed 30 March 2026 and Plot B2 pending; Noida plant closure is part of the manufacturing realignment begun in Q2 FY26 (November board meeting).
Jammu incentive (GST-linked) not yet approved; company is awaiting approval.
Depreciation impact of Jammu capitalisation not quantified; company will share details offline.
demand_pricing: Rural demand resilient through FY26; urban demand improved in the latter part of the year in value and everyday categories, but discretionary spending remains selective.
Zinc costs rose steeply and sustainedly in H2 FY26; calibrated price increases taken in carbon zinc and alkaline batteries.
INR ranged INR83 to INR91+ in FY26 and has moved to about INR94-95 recently; the company hedged FX and secured zinc positioning ahead of the market.
Flashlight market about 70% unbranded and China-dependent; BIS compliance expected to raise costs for unorganised importers in H2 CY26.
Management said H1 revenue is typically a few percentage points better than H2.
Urban revival may be at risk if West Asia-related disruption persists beyond Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How prepared is the business for INR94.5-95/USD and crude above $100, and what is the EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX hedging and zinc procurement positioning, plus pricing, delivered FY26. Management expects to hold margins around the 11.5% level in FY27, though headwinds are stronger than last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the alkaline plant cannibalise carbon zinc, and will carbon zinc prices be raised to narrow the gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects alkaline at 20-25% and zinc at 75% of batteries in about 3 years, with some cannibalisation. The price gap in India is currently narrow, and further zinc price increases are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 tax rate 22%, and why was there no tax on the Noida land sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Transition to 115BAA in FY27 is confirmed, subject to carried-forward business losses. The Noida gain was set off against about INR500 crore of business losses from the write-off of old ICD provisions; MAT credit not yet used.

qa_highlights.question: Is commercial production at Jammu starting in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial production has not started yet; it is expected in a few weeks and within the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target market share and export plan for Jammu?
qa_highlights.answer: Current alkaline share is about 16%, with a target of about 20% exit. Jammu output is for domestic sale for now, with white-label export possible later.

qa_highlights.question: Noida land sale proceeds versus the INR250 crore ballpark?
qa_highlights.answer: Plot B1 sold for about INR116 crore, with profit booked net of WDV and charges. Plot B2 is expected at about INR136 crore, with total about INR251 crore.

Jammu ramp-up and breakeven timing; depreciation impact not yet quantified.
Pending Jammu state incentive approval.

531508|2026-06.headline: Eveready Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR407.7 crore with EBITDA margin of 15.1% and PAT up 22.3%, driven by alkaline batteries and price actions.
531508|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR407.7 crore, up 9% YoY, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth. EBITDA was INR61.5 crore at a 15.1% margin and PAT was INR37 crore, up 22.3%. Management attributed margin protection to calibrated price increases and operational efficiencies, and stated there were no one-off gains. The Jammu alkaline plant began commercial production on 29 May 2026, while flashlights were soft on delayed monsoon and the lighting business reached breakeven.

segments.name: Batteries - Alkaline
segments.commentary: Key growth driver with close to 48% volume growth; premium alkaline market share reached 18%, with management targeting an exit share of 25-30% in two years. Alkaline is about 6-7% of company portfolio.

segments.name: Batteries - Carbon zinc
segments.commentary: Volume growth in line with industry (zinc market volumes roughly flat, -1% to +1%); company holds about 58% share of carbon zinc, described as broadly flattish. Legacy manufacturing costs reduced.

segments.name: Flashlights
segments.commentary: Revenue down 6.7% on delayed monsoon and lower conventional battery-operated volumes; rechargeable flashlights grew over 20%.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue up 13.7%; pricing stabilising after 18-20 months of erosion; company says segment broke even in Q1, with emergency LED bulbs and electrical accessories growing.

segments.name: Electrical accessories / wires
segments.commentary: Insulation tapes growing; wires and MCBs started about 6 months ago, with plans to more than double sales in FY27. Wires are sourced, not manufactured.

guidance_outlook: Management expects roughly 10% gross margin uplift on alkaline products from Jammu plant once fully stabilised (after about one year); operating margin not guided.
Alkaline market share target of 25-30% exit share in two years.
Debt expected to turn positive/like-to-like debt free in 4-5 quarters.
Lighting expected to grow in Q2 and Q3 FY27, with cost softening uncertain.
Management said another round of price or margin corrections may be needed to manage zinc inflation.
Long-term plan and M&A strategy to be presented in 2-3 quarters.
capex_capacity: Jammu alkaline plant commenced commercial production on 29 May 2026; company describes it as the only alkaline battery plant in India.
Jammu plant plant and machinery investment about INR90-95 crore; total Jammu investment INR200 crore-plus, yet to yield results.
Pre-operating expenses of Jammu plant capitalised; expenses after 29 May charged to P&L.
Jammu GST/incentive approval (NCSS scheme, 3x eligible plant and machinery refund over 10 years) still pending formal approval.
Noida plant closed and sold; one plot executed, second expected to close shortly. CCI matter: next hearing around late September 2026.
Solar power installed at Jammu and other plants; company moving toward leasing/rental model for assets.
demand_pricing: Zinc prices around $3,500/ton versus below $3,000 for most of last year; electrolytic manganese dioxide, electrodes, acetylene black and lighting components also inflated.
Alkaline market about INR550 crore (within a battery market of about INR4,100 crore at MRP); alkaline volume growth +19% to +23% over last 7-8 quarters, versus zinc flat.
Alkaline share of dry cell about 13-15%; Duracell is the largest alkaline competitor, Panasonic and Nippo are close followers in zinc.
Digital channels (quick commerce, e-commerce) showed strong growth.
Employee cost up only 2-3% YoY, reflecting the Noida closure.
Management flagged no immediate cannibalisation of zinc by alkaline; may emerge when alkaline exceeds about 20% of the battery market.

qa_highlights.question: Share gains in dry cell (58%) and whether Amazon Basics entry or BIS/EPR compliance is a risk.
qa_highlights.answer: 58% share refers to carbon zinc only. BIS on flashlights is on paper complete, with compliance to be driven across unbranded players over 2-3 quarters. EPR pricing and compliance are under discussion with MoEFCC and the Pollution Control Board, and no cost estimate was given.

qa_highlights.question: What operating margin will Jammu alkaline deliver versus imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 10% gross margin uplift on the product once stabilised, not operating margin. Alkaline is 6-7% of revenue, so the impact is modest for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an one-off in the margin, and how is zinc hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs; margin came from calibrated price actions. Zinc is monitored weekly and further price or margin corrections may be needed.

qa_highlights.question: Consultancy fees to a director and timing of the GST subsidy.
qa_highlights.answer: NRC and Board approved a whole-time director's compensation; quantum not disclosed. GST incentive has no formal approval yet, with discussions advancing.

qa_highlights.question: When can the company be debt free and what is the Jammu fixed cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt around INR165 crore; company expects to be like-to-like debt free in 4-5 quarters. Jammu costs are absorbed into product cost, not separately disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Size of CCI matter and potential cash outgo.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cannot estimate the outcome; next hearing is in late September.

risks_watch: Zinc and commodity inflation; possible further price hikes could affect volumes.
Unresolved EPR compliance cost and pricing framework.
CCI matter with a potential INR150 crore outgo flagged by an analyst; management could not estimate it.
Pending GST incentive approval for Jammu.
Monsoon-dependent flashlight demand and structural decline in conventional flashlights.
Lighting margins at breakeven and dependent on price stability.
Emerging cannibalisation of carbon zinc by alkaline once alkaline crosses about 20% of the market.

531548|2026-03.headline: Somany Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin rose to 11.4% and FY26 to 9.3%; management guides at least 150 bps more margin improvement in FY27 despite gas-price shock.
531548|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 sales grew about 6% and FY26 about 5%, with EBITDA margin up in both periods (11.4% in Q4, 9.3% for FY26). Capacity utilisation was broadly flat at about 79% for the year, rising to 82% in Q4, and Somany Max reached near breakeven versus a loss of about INR 9 crore in Q4 FY25. Gas prices jumped from about 9 March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation, and Morbi capacity was disrupted, which management sees as a share-gain opportunity for organised players. Working capital improved sharply, with receivable days at 40 (from 51) and working capital lower by 4 days to 9 days. Management passed through about 16-17% tile price hikes and about 8% bathware and sanitaryware hikes, and said input cost increases are being fully recovered in retail but only about 85-90% in projects.

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: GVT volumes up 3% while ceramic and PVT volumes fell 3%; average tile price increase of about 16-17% since March 2026. Company-wide utilisation around 79% for the year.

segments.name: Sanitaryware and bathware
segments.commentary: Sanitaryware grew 8% in FY26 to INR 320 crore; management targets double-digit growth in FY27. Bathware price hike of about 18% taken in February on brass costs, and a blended 8% hike in April. Only 25% of dealers currently stock sanitaryware.

segments.name: Adhesives
segments.commentary: Management expects healthy double-digit volume growth in FY27 for sanitaryware and adhesives combined; no separate adhesive figures were given.

segments.name: Outsourced / JV production
segments.commentary: Outsourced sales about 35-36% of volume after Acer and Amora moved from JV to outsourced status (about 30% excluding those). Total FY26 sales volume about 72 million sq m; capacity about 75 million sq m.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin to improve by at least 150 bps from the 9.3% FY26 base, to about 10.5-11% or better; management reiterated 10.8% or better when asked.
FY27 volume growth guided to decent single digits for tiles and double digits for sanitaryware and adhesives.
FY27 revenue growth of about 20-25% if current prices hold, per management, which would be driven by about 15% price hikes plus high single-digit volume growth; value outcome depends on gas prices.
Brand spend to rise slightly in absolute terms, while staying around 2% of sales as a percentage.
Capex limited to about INR 70-80 crore of routine capex and balancing equipment, mainly for the vintage plant and to add value at bathware plant.
South plant to move to a long-term gas contract from next month, expected to cut gas cost by at least INR 17-18 per SCM versus the current INR 78.
capex_capacity: Current gas price in Morbi is about INR 74 per SCM plus 6% (about INR 78) for May, sourced from GSPC; North plant is about INR 3-5 cheaper.
Morbi restarting after gas supply from 1 May: about 60-65% of Morbi running in mid-May, with management expecting about 85% by month-end; labour shortage is the constraint.
Company plants running at about 100% of operating capacity across India, excluding a couple of kilns shut for product-mix reasons.
INR 30 crore invested in a new press at Somany Max to improve utilisation.
Vintage plant balancing equipment being added to turn it profitable; bathware capacity being augmented.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand improved in January and February with single-digit growth; March was disrupted as exports stalled. Industry exports were about INR 17,000+ crore versus about INR 18,000 crore potential.
April was a slow but growing month: Morbi supply shortfall, higher prices (company about 15-17%, Morbi about 30-35%), and dealer destocking caused slower volumes.
Gas cost increase is about INR 5.5-6 per sq ft; other input costs (transport, labour, packaging) add about INR 1-1.5 per sq ft; total cost pressure about INR 6.5-7 per sq ft.
Management says the price hike covers the full cost in retail, while about 15% of business (projects) recovers about 85-90%.
Sanitaryware and bathware blended price hike of about 8% in April 2026.
Stock levels at Q4 end reduced by about 2.5 million sq m (about 15 days) over the year; old stock over 180 days cleared in March.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are the receivable days and negative working capital, and what is the outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects receivable days to stay near current levels, possibly up 1-2 days. Working capital gains came from lower outsourced-vendor stock and clearance of old stock in March. Sustainability is uncertain given the delayed response to price hikes in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a tipping point where gas costs make running plants unviable?
qa_highlights.answer: Tile prices are about 15-20% below two years ago and current hikes bring prices back to historic levels. Management does not see plant shutdown even with a further 10-15% rise, excluding a severe oil shock (about USD 200/bbl).

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth only about 2% in Q4 versus double digits for peers, and realisation lagging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume was focused on non-JV and outsourced material to clear inventory before April price increases. It said realisation was up INR 6 per sq m YoY, with the mix shifting toward cheaper outsourced product.

qa_highlights.question: Gas price differential between Morbi and North, and South plant pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Morbi is about INR 74 plus 6% (about INR 78) per SCM for May; the North plant is about INR 3-5 cheaper. South is INR 78 per SCM currently, but a long-term contract from next month should cut it by at least INR 17-18.

qa_highlights.question: Is the share buyback possible given the market leader's INR 300 crore buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for the next 6-8 months, due to an SEBI embargo tied to consolidation of wholly owned subsidiaries. Promoters bought shares before the trading window closed.

qa_highlights.question: Will Morbi's recovery affect outsourced volumes and FY27 supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outsourced OEM plants for large organised players should keep running. Four or five supplier plants had short-term material gaps in April, expected to normalise in May. Full material availability is expected by June.

risks_watch: Gas prices and any further geopolitical escalation; management said price cuts would follow if gas prices fall.
Morbi restart pace (85% target by end-May) and labour availability; a 10-15% Morbi capacity may not restart.
Demand response to 15-17% tile price hikes; management expects pent-up demand but April was slow.
Transport and fuel costs, which had not yet been quantified after diesel and petrol price hikes.
Sustainability of working capital release and debtor days, and the 4-day rise in receivables risk.
Somany Max path to positive EBITDA in FY27, and Acer and Amora now sitting in the outsourced bucket.

Answers on gas pricing and April volumes were less precise and some figures were corrected or restated during Q&A.
key_quotes: Our guidance is to improve EBITDA margin from here by at least 1.5% or more.
So we are to gain from this disruption because a lot of the capacity in Morbi shut down, and everybody is now buying from the same source of gas.
Tile still being the most cheapest material for the flooring and wall, like I mentioned, there is no alternative to a tile.

rows.why: Somany Max loss narrowed to INR 21 crore in FY26 (from INR 27 crore) and was near breakeven in Q4 versus INR 9 crore loss in Q4 FY25; INR 30 crore new press is being added to lift utilisation.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin guidance (at least 150 bps FY27 improvement) and industry structure from Morbi disruption, but cautious on April demand, gas costs, labour and Morbi restart; analysts pushed on working capital sustainability, Q4 volume growth of about 2%, and the gas-price differen

531548|2026-06.headline: Somany Q1 FY27: EBITDA margin up 3.6 pts YoY to 11.6% on standalone utilisation of 83% (vs 72%), with volume growth only ~3%.
531548|2026-06.overview: Management attributed the margin expansion to higher in-house capacity utilisation and a swing in JV performance from a loss of INR10 crore to a profit of INR3 crore YoY. Sales grew about 3% while value grew about 24%, with a few percent of sales lost in April when Morbi supply was shut for roughly 1.5 months. Price hikes of about 16-17% were passed through to the market, and gas costs rose 16-18% in the current period. Management guided to single-digit to mid-single-digit volume growth, maintained margins of 11%+, and announced a 9-plus million sq m South plant (about INR220 crore capex) due around end-Q3 FY28.

vs loss of INR10 crore in Q1 FY26
vs loss of INR7 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Tiles (own plants and JVs)
segments.commentary: Standalone utilisation rose to 83% from 72%, with two lines under maintenance in the quarter. JV profit of INR3 crore vs a INR10 crore loss a year ago.

segments.name: Bathware / sanitaryware
segments.commentary: Management said Bathware margins run about 1% better than normal tile margins, and tile margins have now caught up. Bathware is growing healthily, with more sanitaryware balancing equipment planned.

segments.name: Construction chemicals (building materials)
segments.commentary: Large capacity added in the South, and a very large North capacity went on stream in July 2026; impact seen partly in Q1 and mostly in Q2.

segments.name: Somany Max

EBITDA margin of 11%+ maintained for the year, with an aspiration to reach 12% and above; management said it is trying to improve margins in Q3 and Q4 as balancing equipment comes on stream.
Balancing equipment and debottlenecking (about 3-4 million sq m, some reported as 4-5 million) to be largely done by end-Q3 and fully in place in Q4 FY27; no new line in FY27.

Management said maximum revenue at current capacity and prices is about INR3,700 crore; debottlenecking could add about INR300 crore partly by year-end.
Gas prices rose 16-18% in the current period; management said the company has passed through increases to date, and July and August gas prices are marginally higher.
capex_capacity: South plant: 9-plus million sq m greenfield, about INR220 crore outlay, operational around end-Q3 / start-Q4 FY28.
Balancing equipment in own plants and JVs (Bahadurgarh, Gujarat, Morbi, South) to add about 3-4 million sq m (also cited as 4-5 million) by Q4 FY27; no new line in FY27.

Construction chemicals capacity added in South, and a very large North capacity commissioned in July 2026.

demand_pricing: Price hike of about 16-17% taken in Q1 FY27; management said margins come from efficiency, with pricing being a pass-through.
Morbi was shut for about 1.5 months, with a 20-day ramp-up to full output from May. Management said about 15-17% of Morbi capacity has not restarted and will not restart.
Morbi exports are down 50-60% from peak due to geopolitical issues and freight; this may persist until freight stabilises.
Channel inventory was built up in March ahead of the April shutdown, is now back to normal but lean, as dealers wait for gas-price cuts.
Retail project share is about 7-8% and government about 10-11%; management expects this to rise by 3-4 percentage points.
Management said July demand was affected by rain but sales were still pushed; it said demand was 'perfectly fine' overall.

Management said that in the Q1 volume growth shortfall versus the industry leader, the leader benefited from in-house Morbi production in polished vitrified tiles (PVT), which Somany is fully exposed to via outsourcing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion and will it sustain from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to standalone utilisation rising to 83% from 72% and JV profit of INR3 crore vs a loss of INR10 crore YoY. It said margins are driven by efficiency rather than pricing and expects them to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Gas pricing across Morbi, North and South?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended natural gas cost is about INR68/unit. South and Morbi are around mid-INR70s (South partly on spot), and North is about INR68-69. Management did not give a blended fuel cost incl. biofuel.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth outlook and why guidance is only mid-single-digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is currently mid-single-digit. It said the leader's higher growth came from in-house PVT production. It has been cautious after missed high-single-digit targets in the past.

qa_highlights.question: Is the price premium over Morbi narrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Morbi raised prices by roughly double Somany's 16-17%, narrowing the gap. Morbi units are now on GEL gas, and their accounting is being rectified, which narrows landed-cost differences.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 capex and funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR275 crore to end-FY27 including the INR220 crore South plant and balancing equipment, with 65-70% from internal accruals. JV loan is without corporate guarantee from Somany.

qa_highlights.question: Is 2%-3% volume growth affected by outsourcing from Morbi, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Morbi outsourcing is not needed beyond a point because of freight. Own plants are targeted at 100% utilisation, with capacity located in North, South and West.

risks_watch: Gas cost volatility: blended natural gas about INR68/unit, with the current increase 16-18% and July/August prices marginally higher; management says the price pass-through has worked so far, but a gas-price cut could bring a price reduction.

531569|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell YoY as March 2026 exports stalled on Middle East disruption; consolidated revenue INR 132.1 mn, EBITDA margin 15.74%.
531569|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue declined year-on-year because exports could not be executed in March 2026 after Iran-related conflict disrupted Middle East shipping and logistics. Input costs also rose in March, compressing gross margins. Consolidated revenue was INR 132.1 mn with EBITDA of INR 21.73 mn (15.74% margin) and PAT of INR 5.5 mn (3.97% margin). Management says alternative routes via Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Southeast Asia have restarted shipments and expects a broader export recovery in Q1 FY27. The Pune IV facility, commercial since December 2025, contributed INR 2.7 mn in Q4 versus INR 1.2 mn in Q3.

531595|2026-03.headline: Capri Global Q4 FY26 PAT hit record INR283 crore (+59% YoY) and FY26 PAT INR949 crore (~2x), with consolidated gross Stage 3 down to 0.9%.
531595|2026-03.overview: Capri Global posted its highest-ever quarterly profit of INR283 crore in Q4 FY26, up 59% YoY, with FY26 PAT of INR949 crore, almost double the prior year. Consolidated AUM reached INR36,623 crore (+60% YoY, +20% QoQ), led by gold loans at INR16,965 crore (+111% YoY, +33% QoQ). Asset quality improved, with consolidated gross Stage 3 at 0.9% (down 61 bps QoQ) and net Stage 3 at 0.5%. Management reiterated FY28 targets of INR55,000 crore AUM (revised FY28 AUM guidance cited as INR57,000 crore in Q&A, with FY27 at INR46,000 crore), ROA 4-4.5% and ROE 16-18%.

531595|2026-06.headline: Capri Global posted record Q1 FY27 PAT of INR353 crore (+102% YoY) on AUM of INR40,112 crore (+62% YoY) and cost-to-income of 44.2%.
531595|2026-06.overview: Capri Global reported record quarterly profit after tax of INR353 crore, up 102% YoY, with consolidated AUM of INR40,112 crore, up 62% YoY and 10% QoQ. Gold loans (48% of AUM) drove growth, with AUM of INR19,179 crore (+111% YoY, +13% QoQ), while cost-to-income improved to 44.2% from 49.4% in Q4 FY26. Asset quality weakened at the margin: gross Stage 2 ratio rose to 3.8% from 2.8%, mostly on gold loans, and gross Stage 3 rose to 1.1%, largely from one construction finance account. Management revised its FY28 AUM target to INR65,000 crore and reiterated medium-term ROE of 19-21% and ROA of 4.2-4.7%.

532054|2026-03.headline: KDDL standalone Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 87.6% YoY to INR36.4 crore at a 25.1% margin; FY26 standalone revenue INR506 crore, up 31.9%.

Watch components (ex-Ethos, ex-bracelets) grew ~20% to ~INR240 crore, Precision Engineering (Eigen) grew 35%+ to ~INR200 crore, and Ornapac grew ~37% to INR23 crore. segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR23 crore vs ~INR17 crore, up ~37%. Still loss-making during ramp-up; management expects profitability in H2 FY27.

532067|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue about INR142 crore and PAT nearly INR60 crore; management guides 15-20% growth for FY27 across the group.

qa_highlights.question: What is Coris's full-year FY26 revenue on a 12-month basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Coris did about INR50 crore for the full year; with Coris's accounting aligned to 31 March, the 15-month period to March 2026 gave INR57.65 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How does the margin look for FY27 and how is Q1/Q2 Coris loss treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide quarterly; it said full-year revenue and EBITDA should both grow 15-20%, with Coris losing money in Q1 and Q2 and benefiting from HAT order timing in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the M&A pipeline and cash deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Two or three opportunities are in advanced discussion with consultants in France, UK and US; European valuations are high, and the company will hold a reserve of INR50 crore with the balance for M&A over one to two years. Treasury is about 90% in FDs, government bonds and AAA corporate bonds, and about 5-7% in equity mutual funds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Coris contract status and the EBITDA trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Of a EUR6 million four-year contract (Congo, affected by Ebola), about EUR3.45 million has been executed and about EUR2.4 million remains; Coris is guided to slightly EBITDA positive in FY27, about 10% in FY27-28.

risks_watch: Coris earnings depend on the HAT order timing; the Congo contract is at risk from the Ebola outbreak.
FY26 domestic growth (~10%) lagged the chains' reported test volume growth of 10-11%; the company said it is high-base affected.
FY27 consolidated margin depends on Coris losses in H1 and the M&A outcome; the cash pile of about INR230 crore is not yet deployed.
Chinese competition in respiratory and enteric products, including export markets, and IVDR compliance timing for EU exports.
US FDA clearance timing for AMR products remains uncertain.
532067|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the 15-20% growth guidance and long-term margin profile, but evasive on quarterly phasing, M&A timing and the FDA timeline, repeatedly deferring to full-year figures. Several answers were also unclear on the numbers, with the chairman asking the analyst to check the slide during the Coris Q4 depreciation discussion.
key_quotes: So, growth of 15% to 20% is what is we are trying to achieve and let's look forward to it.
So, we will do only two earning calls every year.
Coris will become slightly EBITDA positive.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides group EBITDA growth of 15-20% in FY27 in line with revenue, and says margin profile is maintained; standalone EBITDA margin held at 55% in FY26, but Coris losses in H1 FY27 cap any expansion at consolidated level.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 50%, and any capacity increase would cost just INR4-5 crore, so no meaningful new plant or line is being added; the sample-to-answer rollout is an OEM demand-side install at two to three labs from Q3 FY27, not a company capacity build.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consolidated revenue guided to 15-20% growth in FY27, backed by Coris (about INR50-52 crore revenue vs about INR35.91 crore for seven months in FY26) and standalone growth of about 7.1% non-export, though domestic growth lagged at about 10% due to the FY25 high base.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 50% with capacity increases costing only INR4-5 crore, so no large capex is needed; the cash pile of about INR230 crore is more likely to go to M&A than to plants.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Coris HAT order timing in Q3-Q4 FY27 and the sample-to-answer OEM rollout could lift results above the 15-20% guide, but management declined to guide quarterly and the Coris Congo contract (about EUR2.4 million left) is at Ebola risk.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Coris is loss-making in Q1 and Q2 FY27, domestic growth (about 10% in FY26) lagged chains' test volume growth of 10-11%, and Chinese players are underpricing respiratory and enteric products.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sample-to-answer system is expected to start installations at two to three labs from Q3 FY27 after positive validation, and IVDR technical documentation review is progressing for key product families, but no specific launch dates or revenue sizes were given.

rows.label: US FDA clearance for selected AMR products
rows.why: The US could contribute about 20% of AMR revenue, about INR11-16 crore (USD1-1.5 million), but timing is uncertain and management gave no firm date.

rows.label: M&A deployment of about INR180-200 crore of cash
rows.why: Two or three targets are in advanced talks with consultants in France, UK and US, and about INR230 crore of treasury cash is held with a INR50 crore reserve; management targeted a deal by year-end but committed to no timing.

rows.label: Coris Congo EUR6 million contract execution
rows.why: About EUR3.45 million of the four-year contract is executed and about EUR2.4 million remains, but the Ebola outbreak in Congo puts the balance at risk.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 15-20% FY27 growth guidance and the 55% standalone margin, but evasive on quarterly phasing, M&A timing and the FDA timeline; analysts pressed on the consolidated EBITDA margin (about 40% vs 61.84% cited) and the Coris numbers, which were not reconciled on the call.

532134|2026-03.headline: Bank of Baroda Q4 FY26 net profit rose 11.2% YoY to a record Rs 5,616 crore; FY26 net profit Rs 20,021 crore, with FY27 loan growth guidance raised to 12-14%.
532134|2026-03.overview: Global business crossed Rs 30 lakh crore at Rs 30.78 lakh crore (+13.9% YoY), with global advances up 16.2% and total deposits up 12%. Q4 operating profit was Rs 9,069 crore (+11.5% YoY) and NII grew 8.7%, with NIM at 2.89% (+10 bps QoQ) helped partly by interest on income-tax refunds. Asset quality improved (GNPA 1.89%, net NPA 0.45%), but Q4 credit cost rose to 0.76% after a Rs 1,500 crore floating provision funded from IT refunds. Management raised FY27 loan and deposit growth guidance and set a Rs 6,000 crore AT-1/Tier 2 raise plan, while cautioning that cost of deposits will stay sticky in Q1 given tight liquidity and West Asia tensions.

financial_highlights.value: 0.76% (0.32% excluding Rs 1,500 crore floating provision); FY26 0.46% (0.34% excluding floating provision)

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Organic retail book grew 17.9% YoY and crossed Rs 3 lakh crore; auto loans +20.6%, mortgages +19.3%, home loans +14.6%, education +10.9%, personal loans +8.7%. RAM share of advances is 61%.

segments.name: Agriculture and MSME
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 20.7% and organic MSME 15.6%. MSME book is about Rs 1.6 lakh crore, of which 55-60% is working capital; ECLGS disbursement estimated at Rs 12,000 crore plus.

segments.name: Corporate and international
segments.commentary: Corporate loans grew 11.2% YoY. International advances grew 24.4%; US operations are about 37-38% of the international book. Management says Middle East exposure is about Rs 50,000-60,000 crore across multiple countries, with no asset-quality impact yet.

guidance_outlook: FY27 loan growth guidance raised to 12-14% from 11-13%.
FY27 deposit growth guidance raised to 10-12% from 9-11%.
FY27 NIM guidance 2.75-2.95%, which management says includes volatility from IT refund interest; management said it would not breach 2.75% over the four quarters.
ROA guidance kept at more than 1%; slippage ratio kept at 1-1.25%; full-year credit cost guided below 0.60%.
Normalised recoveries from written-off accounts guided at Rs 750-800 crore; management said Q4 recovery was higher than guidance.
Cost of deposits expected to stay sticky in Q1 FY27 given tight liquidity. Management sees scope to reprice MCLR-linked assets; MCLR is 36% and repo-linked 35% of the book.
Hiring of 4,000-5,000 headcount in FY27, against a plan of 6,000-7,000.
capex_capacity: Capital plan: Rs 6,000 crore of AT-1/Tier 2 in FY27, with no fixed timeline and execution depending on pricing. An enabling Rs 8,500 crore equity raise runs through FY28.
Tech spend (opex plus capex) was about Rs 4,500 crore; management says it is adequately covered, with extra spend possible if needed. Tech spend is about 10% of operating profit as a norm.

New subsidiaries: BOB Securities and Gilt Edge Ltd (primary dealer, operational from 1 April 2026, Rs 2,000 crore capital committed, Rs 500 crore availed); pension fund sponsorship approval received, with 6-9 months expected to launch.
Green infrastructure bond of Rs 10,000 crore raised, 3x subscribed; green deposits of Rs 1,899 crore.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth of 12% outpaced by the 16.2% advances growth, a gap management views as sustainable given excess SLR and bulk deposit usage.
Bulk deposits rose to 19% of total deposits in March from 17% a couple of quarters earlier; management says it will stay below 20%.
Domestic SLR is about 22.5-23%, roughly 4.5-5% above the statutory level; management targets 3-3.5% excess SLR.
Collection efficiency excluding agriculture is 98.9%, up from December. CRILC SMA-1 and 2 fell to 0.18% from 0.33% a year earlier.
Management said MSME stress (SMA-0 to SMA-2) was better in March than December, and auto loan stress remains very small.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 NIM improvement came from IT refund interest, and how much is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a number and said it is a recurring but volatile line item (about Rs 100 crore to interest income in Q4 per a later reply). It treats the 2.89% as core and the 2.75-2.95% range as covering refund volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 1,500 crore floating provision linked to ECL or West Asia?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a balance-sheet buffer funded by IT refunds, aimed at lifting PCR and keeping net NPA low. It cannot be used without regulatory approval and is separate from ECL. ECL impact is not yet quantified; management said it should be broadly in line with earlier estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Why was loan guidance raised after a 16.2% growth year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth has been strong since 31 March on a daily YoY basis, the deposit base is recovering, and it expects the geopolitical disruption may not last long. It raised guidance by 1 percentage point.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of deposits outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of deposits (4.78% total, 4.99% domestic) is expected to stay sticky for at least the next three months as liquidity remains tight; management does not expect further reductions and sees repricing mainly on the asset side.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to the Middle East and overseas book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Middle East exposure at about Rs 50,000-60,000 crore across multiple countries, some A-rated, with US about 37-38% of the international book. Trade is below 20% of overseas exposure, and no asset-quality impact has been seen yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for agriculture and the weak monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Agriculture GNPA fell year on year. Fresh slippages are normal and were offset by recoveries. Management does not expect a weak monsoon to materially affect the portfolio.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: a prolonged war or high oil prices could affect the overseas book, Middle East operations and MSME borrowers; management is watching this closely over the next couple of quarters.
Cost of deposits is sticky and asset repricing is still to be shown; NIM guidance of 2.75-2.95% relies partly on volatile IT refund interest.
ECL implementation: quantification is pending, with management indicating it will show up in the books from the first quarter of implementation.
Credit cost run rate is guided below 0.60%, but the Q4 level of 0.76% included the one-time floating provision.
Bulk deposit share, LCR (about 127%), and the timing and pricing of the Rs 6,000 crore AT-1/Tier 2 issuance.
532134|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, profitability and asset quality, with several guidance upgrades. Cautious and hedged on margin, deposit costs and West Asia exposure, repeatedly saying impacts are unquantified and depend on liquidity and the conflict's duration. Evasive on ECL quantum and bilateral accounts such as Vodafone Idea.
key_quotes: So, in terms of customer income, we have improved, the NIM has improved vis-a-vis the last quarter from 2.79% to 2.89% with the domestic NIM at 3.04%.
The credit cost for the full year is going to be less than 0.60%.
I'm not predicting any increase in deposit rate.
Our floating provision cannot be used without the regulatory approval and that can only be used on extraordinary scenarios.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM rose 10 bps QoQ to 2.89% in Q4 (partly IT refund interest), with management seeing repricing scope on MCLR-linked assets (36% of book), but cost of deposits stays sticky at 4.78% in Q1 and it guides only to a 2.75-2.95% range.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Global advances grew 16.2% and deposits 12% in FY26, with FY27 loan guidance 12-14% and deposit guidance 10-12%; retail organic book up 17.9% past Rs 3 lakh crore and agriculture advances up 20.7%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No physical capex discussed, but the Rs 6,000 crore AT-1/Tier 2 raise in FY27 (no fixed timeline, pricing dependent) and the enabling Rs 8,500 crore equity raise through FY28 signal capital actions; tech spend about Rs 4,500 crore is covered, with extra spend possible.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 loan growth guidance was already raised to 12-14% (from 11-13%) after 16.2% advances growth in FY26, and deposit guidance raised to 10-12%; management says growth has been strong since 31 March on a daily YoY basis.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: NIM guidance of 2.75-2.95% relies partly on volatile IT refund interest (about Rs 100 crore in Q4), cost of deposits is sticky at 4.78% through at least the next three months, and West Asia exposure of Rs 50,000-60,000 crore is unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pension fund sponsorship approval received with 6-9 months expected to launch, and BOB Securities and Gilt Edge Ltd (primary dealer) operational from 1 April 2026 with Rs 500 crore of Rs 2,000 crore capital availed.

rows.label: Hiring 4,000-5,000 in FY27 vs plan of 6,000-7,000
rows.why: Management guided 4,000-5,000 headcount additions in FY27, below the 6,000-7,000 plan, reflecting a slower hiring pace.

rows.label: ECL implementation impact on provisions
rows.why: ECL impact is not yet quantified and management says it will show up in the books from the first quarter of implementation, with the floating provision of Rs 1,500 crore sitting alongside it.

rows.label: Excess SLR and bulk deposit funding
rows.why: Domestic SLR is about 22.5-23% (4.5-5% above statutory), with management targeting 3-3.5% excess SLR; bulk deposits are 19% of total, which management says will stay below 20%.

tone.note: Management was confident on loan growth, record profit, asset quality and raised guidance, but cautious and hedged on margins, sticky deposit costs, West Asia exposure and ECL quantum; analysts pressed on IT refund contribution, the floating provision and the Middle East book.

532134|2026-06.headline: Bank of Baroda Q1 FY27 net profit fell to INR 1,278 crore after a USD 600 million NMC settlement; ex-item profit was INR 5,528 crore.
532134|2026-06.overview: Global business reached INR 30.5 lakh crore, up 15.4% YoY, with global advances up 17.4% and domestic deposits up 14.7%. Operating profit was INR 8,127 crore, roughly flat YoY, as NII grew 9.5% but treasury income fell to about INR 800-900 crore from over INR 2,000 crore a year earlier. The USD 600 million NMC out-of-court settlement, paid on 1 July 2026 and expensed in Q1, cut reported ROA to 0.25% (1.10% excluding the item). Asset quality improved YoY, with GNPA at 1.99%, credit cost at 0.29% and slippage at 0.91%, though sequentially GNPA and NNPA ticked up due to a lower write-off of INR 625 crore versus INR 2,200 crore a year earlier.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -29 bps YoY; Net NPA -10 bps YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Domestic CASA ratio / domestic CD ratio

segments.name: Advances
segments.commentary: Global advances +17.4% YoY (domestic +16.1%, international +23.3%). Organic retail +18.4%, agriculture +18.7%, organic MSME +20.3%, corporate +15.3%; auto +25.3%, mortgage +27.4%, home loan +14.7%, education +10.8%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Total deposits +13.8% YoY (domestic +14.7%, international +8.9%). Domestic CASA +10% and term deposits +17.8%; management says current account growth was 14.5%.

segments.name: Treasury and other income
segments.commentary: Treasury income about INR 800-900 crore versus over INR 2,000 crore in Q1 FY26, mainly on revaluation as G-sec yields rose to about 6.78% from about 6.10%. Recoveries from technical write-offs exceeded INR 1,000 crore, and PSLC sales of about INR 270 crore were added. Commission and fee income fell about 47% YoY.

segments.name: International book
segments.commentary: Overseas book is about 16-17% of global book and grew 15-20% over recent quarters; international NIM is about 1.4-1.5%.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth 12-14% (unchanged despite outperformance; management cites geopolitical caution).
Deposit growth 10-12%; CD ratio 84-86%.
NIM 2.75-2.95%; slippage ratio 1-1.25%; credit cost below 0.6%; ROE 15-16%.
Full-year ROA guidance deferred to Q2; management expects Q2-Q4 ROA above 1%, and said full-year ROA may not exceed 1%.

ECL transition impact about INR 12,000 crore (about 110 bps on CRAR), with INR 2,500 crore floating provision offsetting part; run-rate credit cost impact about 15-20 bps (earlier cited 20-22 bps on CRAR).
FCNR(B)/OFCB/ECB inflow target USD 4-5 billion; about USD 600-700 million raised so far; USD 1 billion expected via bonds; swap window open until 31 December.
capex_capacity: Capital plan: INR 8,500 crore equity over the medium term to March 2028; about INR 6,000 crore Tier 2 intended in FY27, subject to pricing and timing.
Branches: about 8,400 total; about 260 added last year. Headcount hiring plan of about 7,000 in FY27 after about 6,000 planned last year.
IT budget (OPEX plus capex) above INR 4,000 crore.
Average LCR about 127%; management targets around 120%.
Investment duration increased QoQ and YoY; yields on the book moved from a peak of about 7.13-7.14% to about 6.75-6.80%.
demand_pricing: Corporate book shows a YTD decline. Management says it let go of some low-priced non-MCLR assets and is moving them to MCLR or near-MCLR, helping asset yields.

Bulk deposits and CD together were about INR 2.31 lakh crore, of which bulk deposits were INR 2.11 lakh crore. Bulk deposit rates eased after the FCNR(B) scheme, so incremental bulk deposit cost is now below March levels, per management.
FCNR(B) Rupee deposit rate of about 6.4-6.5% is the landed cost of funds. Loans against FCNR(B) are offered to NRIs, and overseas branches price these loans at their own cost of funds.
Domestic NIM at 2.93% described as top quartile. Global NIM is also described as top quartile.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the bank settle the NMC case, and what changed from the annual report stance of defending it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the defence position is unchanged, but the decision reflected the stage of trial and negotiation, legal advice, and time and cost. The settlement was USD 600 million, the terms are confidential, and it was described as far below the oral claim quantum. Recovery against principal individuals continues in India and abroad.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no specific provision earlier, and what is the ECL transition impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a specific provision is not allowed on litigation under legal advice. The ECL transition impact is about INR 12,000 crore (110 bps CRAR), offset by the INR 2,500 crore floating provision, with the remainder to be amortised. Credit cost impact is about 15-20 bps; CRAR impact per year is about 20-22 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why not raise the credit growth guidance given strong performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited geopolitical headwinds and uncertainty over deposit growth. It said guidance could be upsized if deposit growth becomes more certain.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in treasury and other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury income fell to about INR 800-900 crore from over INR 2,000 crore, mainly due to revaluation as yields moved. This was offset partly by about INR 1,000 crore of TWO recoveries and PSLC sales of about INR 270 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the NIM and the FCNR(B) inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed the 2.75-2.95% NIM guidance, citing asset repricing and lower incremental bulk deposit costs. FCNR(B) inflows are targeted at USD 4-5 billion, with about USD 1 billion expected via bonds, subject to pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Is there stress in the book from global headwinds, and what do the asset quality indicators show?
qa_highlights.answer: No; CRILC SMA-1 and 2 fell to 0.07% from 0.40% a year earlier, and collection efficiency excluding agriculture was 99.2%. Management said ECLGS supports MSMEs and that slippage and recoveries were better YoY.

risks_watch: NMC settlement: the terms are confidential and the case is sub-judice against other defendants; management says no further claims on the bank in the two courts.
ROA: full-year guidance deferred to Q2; management expects Q2-Q4 ROA above 1%, but the Q1 reported figure was 0.25%.
ECL transition: about INR 12,000 crore impact and a 15-20 bps run-rate credit cost increase. Management said pricing pass-through is subject to RBI spread-change rules.
Margin pressure: asset growth of 16-17% is running ahead of NII, with the NIM at 2.77% against 2.8%+ last quarter.
Sequential rise in GNPA and NNPA due to a lower write-off (INR 625 crore) and a lower denominator. Management said write-offs were kept conservative to protect PCR.
Funding and capital: the INR 8,500 crore equity raise (by March 2028) and about INR 6,000 crore Tier 2 are pending; the FCNR(B) and dollar bond timing depend on pricing.
Non-interest income: commission and fee income fell about 47% YoY; management says pricing is under review.
532134|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet growth, asset quality and capital, but defensive on the NMC settlement, which management declined to detail beyond its commercial rationale. Cautious on guidance: credit growth is held at 12-14% and full-year ROA is deferred, citing geopolitics. Some answers were vague (ECL run-rate, pricing pass-through), and the CEO pushed back on the view that the quarter was weak.
key_quotes: The liability of the Bank in these proceedings is limited to the sum of USD 600 million, which was paid on 1st July 2026.
Without the impact of this exceptional item, net profit for the quarter would have been INR 5,528 crores.
The Bank continues to hold the floating provision of INR 2,500 crores.
So, in terms of the Bank's ability to grow, I think, with a large franchisee of almost 8,400 branches

rows.why: Domestic NIM 2.93% within 2.75-2.95% guidance and incremental bulk deposit cost below March levels, but global NIM fell to 2.77% from 2.8%+ and asset growth of 16-17% runs ahead of NII; ECL and pricing pass-through remain uncertain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 260 branches were added last year (about 8,400 total) and about 7,000 hires are planned in FY27 versus about 6,000 last year, but no new capacity numbers beyond branches were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Global advances up 17.4% YoY and deposits up 13.8%, yet credit growth guidance is held at 12-14% and deposit growth at 10-12%, implying growth ahead of guidance continues if deposits firm up.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capital plan of INR 8,500 crore equity to March 2028 and about INR 6,000 crore Tier 2 intended in FY27 are the stated plan; CRAR 16.30% after an ECL impact of about 110 bps, and IT budget above INR 4,000 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said credit growth guidance could be upsized if deposit growth becomes more certain, and full-year ROA guidance is due in Q2 with Q2-Q4 ROA expected above 1%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Full-year ROA may not exceed 1% after the 0.25% reported Q1 ROA, and ECL run-rate credit cost impact of 15-20 bps could push credit cost toward the sub-0.6% ceiling.

rows.label: FCNR(B)/ECB inflows toward USD 4-5 billion
rows.why: About USD 600-700 million raised so far against a USD 4-5 billion target, with USD 1 billion expected via bonds and the swap window open until 31 December, subject to pricing.

rows.label: NMC settlement paid and expensed in Q1
rows.why: USD 600 million settlement cut reported ROA to 0.25% from 1.10% ex-item and reported net profit to INR 1,278 crore against INR 5,528 crore ex-item, so no further hit is expected from this item.

rows.label: Non-MCLR assets migrated to MCLR
rows.why: Management is moving low-priced non-MCLR assets to MCLR or near-MCLR, supporting asset yields as bulk deposit costs ease below March levels.

tone.note: Management was confident on balance sheet growth, asset quality (GNPA 1.99%, credit cost 0.29%) and capital, but defensive on the NMC settlement and cautious on guidance, holding credit growth at 12-14% and deferring full-year ROA; analysts pushed on the ECL run-rate, pricing pass-through and the NM

532143|2026-03.headline: SKM Egg Products FY26 sales rose 58% to ₹767 crore and PAT crossed ₹100 crore for the first time (₹102 crore).
532143|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 results: sales up 58% YoY to ₹767 crore, operating profit about ₹163 crore, PBT ₹136 crore and PAT ₹102 crore, the first year above ₹100 crore PAT. Q4 FY26 sales were ₹197 crore, with PBT ₹41 crore and PAT ₹32 crore against ₹9.7 crore and ₹6.22 crore a year earlier. Management said powder capacity is now running at full utilisation, so FY27 volume growth will be modest. The company is funding a ₹400 crore layer-shed expansion (about 20 lakh birds, completion targeted 2028-29) and is bringing the associate SKM Universal into the listed entity.

financial_highlights.change: up from ₹33 crore; first year above ₹100 crore
vs ₹180 crore in the prior-year quarter as stated on the call
vs ₹9.7 crore / ₹6.22 crore a year earlier
rose Q1 to Q3; Q4 dipped on product mix

segments.name: Egg powder (export)
segments.commentary: About 7,000 tonnes of powder today with a stated target of 10,000 tonnes over roughly five years; powder capacity was 7,320 tonnes as of 2023. Management said FY27 powder volume growth will be small because capacity is fully used.

segments.name: Shellac (export and domestic)
segments.commentary: Export business is about ₹100 crore and domestic about ₹40 crore; management expects this to keep growing and to be a source of FY27 growth.

segments.name: Branded / value-added egg products
segments.commentary: Products include egg in tetra-pack, egg liquid, egg white cube and Egg Pro protein drink. Management reformulated Egg Pro for launch in June, and an R&D division is planned within six months. Revenue from these products has been small so far.

guidance_outlook: Management said the ₹1,000 crore revenue target is for 2030, not FY27.
FY27 powder top-line growth will be modest because the company is at full capacity; shellac and domestic growth expected to add to it.
Q1 FY27 realisation expected to continue near the Q4 level (~₹722/kg powder terms), with some international market changes but no major impact expected.
The ₹400 crore layer-shed capex is a cost-saving, bottom-line investment (not a top-line one) and is expected to be completed by FY28-29, taking the flock from about 20 lakh to 40 lakh birds.
Management said it expects about ₹0.20 per egg of production-cost savings from the new system, and a gross margin of about ₹0.50 per egg.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 sales volumes and realisation per kg, and what is the outlook for FY27–28, including the ₹1,000 crore target and the SKM Universal consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no exact volume or consideration figures on the call. It said capacity is full, realisation rose through FY26 with a Q4 dip on mix (~₹722/kg powder), and the ₹1,000 crore goal is for 2030. For SKM Universal, the valuation is about ₹37 crore for the whole company; the group already holds 26%, so the 74% stake costs about ₹27.75 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the country-wise revenue split and competitive position, and what is driving elevated egg prices in Japan?
qa_highlights.answer: The country split was declined as it is not public. Competitors are European producers in Japan and Russia. Management said it earns about 5% more than competitors. Price strength was attributed to bird flu culls, which take about two years to repopulate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity, the 400 crore capex timeline, and the value-added product plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Flock is moving toward 40 lakh birds by 2028-29. The capex is a cost-saving investment, not a revenue driver. Management is developing value-added products (Egg Pro relaunch, egg white cube) and an R&D unit. Shellac export and domestic are also growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Indian producers not consistently profitable outside bird flu cycles, and how are contracts priced and hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bird-flu disruptions are sporadic and under control, with vaccination under discussion with the government. Contracts are mostly 3–6 months, priced on cost and competition, and the forex hedge is currently only about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected ROC on the new EC-shed project and what drives FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exact ROC figures would follow later. It said the project cuts production cost by about ₹0.20 per egg. FY27 growth is expected to be small in powder and larger in shellac and domestic sales.

qa_highlights.question: How does the USD–EUR rate affect other expenses, and will the investor presentation be shared?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe is a small share of business and most pricing is in USD. Russia is invoiced in rupees and rubles, and Japan from H2. The presentation will be uploaded to the website.

532143|2026-06.headline: SKM Egg Products' Q1 FY27 realisation rose to about Rs 770/kg from Rs 722 last quarter, while management flagged feed-cost pressure lasting at least two more quarters.
532143|2026-06.overview: Management said the company is running near full capacity, so volume growth is capped and results depend on international egg product prices, exchange rates and feed costs. Realisation was stated at about Rs 770 per unit against Rs 722 last quarter, mainly helped by the rupee, while margins were hit by a substantial rise in soya-based feed costs. Management said the company is moving into domestic branded eggs, with a business plan due by end-March, and is adding easy-shed capacity with completion targeted for November-December 2028. Capex approval for further expansion is expected at the next board meeting, with a target of October. The call was largely Q&A; no formal presentation was given, and several answers were vague on numbers.

segments.name: Egg powder (export)
segments.commentary: Realisation about Rs 770 per unit this quarter; management guided that the quarterly average will likely stay above Rs 700, with a range of Rs 720-750 cited. Russia shipments run about 150 tons per month.

segments.name: Branded eggs (domestic, new)
segments.commentary: Structure set up after the company took over a brand company; business plan due by end-March. Management said margins are lower than egg products and gave no brand EBITDA or revenue figure beyond the Rs 40-50 crore turnover expected this year.

segments.name: Easy sheds / egg production
segments.commentary: About 20 lakh birds planned; first four sheds completed earlier, all to be complete by November-December 2028. Management said the cost advantage is at least 5% of overall production cost, from higher productivity and feed efficiency.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth limited by capacity for the rest of FY27; the company is running at full capacity.
Feed-cost pressure expected to persist for at least two more quarters, per management.
International egg white prices seen as stable, with possible improvement of 2-3/4 for egg white; inventory positions still high.
Japan office approval delayed one to two months for resubmission; new business expected in the second half of the year.
Next board meeting in October expected to approve a further expansion plan (capex timing, capacity numbers not given).
capex_capacity: Easy sheds: about 20 lakh birds; completion by November-December 2028.
Backward integration and plant expansion referenced; management has not disclosed capacity numbers.
Waste-to-biogas and organic fertiliser: fermentation gas used in the boiler; liquid and solid organic fertiliser to reach commercial sale by September.
Plant at full capacity; next expansion plan to be announced at the October board meeting.
Phased capex to come in FY28 and FY29; capacity by end FY27 or FY28 not disclosed on the call.
demand_pricing: Global egg product prices are set by Europe (egg white) and the US, South America and China (yolk); India and Ukraine are also cited as supply countries.
International prices described as stable; some signs of higher egg white demand but high inventories still with processors.
Pricing is set by competition and market prices, not by the company's cost; management said feed-cost increases cannot be passed on directly.
Russia war reported as not affecting exports; Iran-related shipping disruption led to about 6-7 containers being returned from Dubai and re-airlifted.
Management said Europe's severe summer could support demand toward the end of the financial year.

qa_highlights.question: How are international egg powder prices determined, and which countries set them?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe sets egg white prices and the US, South America and China influence yolk prices; the company said cost structures and historical supply decide prices, which differ by product.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE on the easy-shed and biogas capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate return estimate was given. Management said the biogas gas is burned in the boiler and by-products sold as organic fertiliser, and that the investment is needed for efficiency and sustainability.

qa_highlights.question: What are the realisation and margin drivers this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation was about Rs 770 vs Rs 722 earlier, helped by the exchange rate. The main margin hit was a substantial rise in soya feed cost, which management expects to persist for at least two more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution and margin of branded products?
qa_highlights.answer: Branded eggs were not part of the business historically. Management gave no number and said margins are lower than egg products but volume scale is easier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Japan office status and the Russia export position?
qa_highlights.answer: Japan approval delayed by one to two months; direct contracts already in place. Russia at about 150 tons per month. A second distributor is being sought.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost savings from easy sheds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no figure beyond a minimum 5% reduction in overall production cost, from higher productivity and better feed conversion.

risks_watch: Feed-cost (soya) pressure will keep margins under pressure for at least two quarters and cannot be passed on directly to customers.
Full capacity caps volume growth until new capacity is commissioned (easy sheds targeted by end-2028).
Branded-egg venture has no disclosed margin, capex or revenue split beyond the Rs 40-50 crore turnover expected this year.
Exchange-rate dependence: much of the realisation gain was attributed to the rupee.
Shipping disruption (Iran-related) led to returned containers; management said the stock will be sold in July-August.

532143|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 turnover ~363 crore vs 380 crore, PAT ~40 crore flat; Q2 PAT fell to ~16 crore as feed raw material costs rose.
532143|2026-09.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as broadly flat year on year: turnover about 363 crore versus 380 crore, EBITDA about 67-44 crore (transcript reads "6744 crores", unclear) and PAT about 40 crore in both periods. Q2 turnover rose to about 184 crore from 179 crore in Q1, but EBITDA fell to about 28 crore from 38 crore as feed raw material costs increased. Q2 PBT was about 22 crore (32 crore in Q1) and PAT about 16 crore (24 crore in Q1). Management guided to a 100 crore-plus profit for the full year but declined to give quarterly guidance, and the company is in a heavy capex phase funded largely by term debt.

segments.name: Egg powder / egg products
segments.commentary: Powder sales were 1,625 MT in Q2 versus 1,831 MT in Q1, and 3,457 MT in H1 versus 4,289 MT in the prior-year half. Average realisation was cited at about 700 rupees per unit, with management expecting 700-plus in H2 and volumes slightly better.

segments.name: Domestic shell eggs / branded eggs
segments.commentary: Management said it currently sells about 1.5 lakh eggs a day in the branded egg segment and targets 5 lakh eggs a day in two to three years. Business model, segment (premium vs mass) and pricing are still under internal discussion, with a decision expected in about three months.

segments.name: SKM Universal (wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Board approved merger of SKM Universal into the listed company; it will cease to exist by April next year. Management said scale-up plans begin in FY28, and a 17.5 crore goodwill-like item in Q2 was described as a share purchase cost from a sister company.

guidance_outlook: Full-year PAT of 100 crore-plus reiterated, described as a ballpark figure; no quarterly guidance given, citing SEBI limits and export volatility.
Next six months expected to continue the past six months with a small margin improvement; more aggressive growth expected from next financial year.
Average realisations not expected to correct significantly over the next six months; Japan pricing reduced due to US oversupply, with pressure elsewhere limited.
Real sales increment from the expanded capacity expected from FY28-FY29; no top-line or bottom-line numbers given.
Dividend payout to be maintained at about 25% even during the high-investment and debt phase.
capex_capacity: EC (layer) farm phase two: 2.4 million birds target by September 28; first rearing house expected complete in about two weeks, chicks to be placed from November 15; project running about one week behind schedule.
Board approved term loan of nearly 300 crore (200 crore State Bank, 100 crore Access Bank); documents to be signed the following week.
Powder capacity expansion from 7,000 to 10,000+ tons at about 180 crore (30 crore margin, about 150 crore term loan at 8.25%), with capacity commissioning around H2 FY28 and 3-5 years to fill.
Management described total debt for the investment phase as about 450 crore.
Cash of about 167 crore held; management said about 100 crore is kept as a minimum for seasonality.
demand_pricing: US oversupply of eggs is reducing prices in Japan; management said pressure elsewhere has been limited and international prices are set by global competitors (Europe, Ukraine, South America, Mexico), not by Indian costs.

Feed raw material (soya and other ingredients) costs rose sharply in Q2; the company cannot fix prices in contracts and has no pass-through mechanism. Management could not confirm pass-through to customers.
Management plans to import soya for about six months of requirement, expected to be about 10% cheaper than local prices; implementation expected in a week or two.
South Korea: two customers have approved samples; bigger trial shipment is under way, with a first order targeted for October-December quarter.
Freight costs rose due to the US-Iran conflict and the Ukraine-Russia war; management said the rupee depreciation offsets part of this and demand has not been affected.

qa_highlights.question: What are realisations outlook for the next six months, and will domestic sales drive growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US oversupply has hit Japan pricing only; average realisation is about 700 rupees and not expected to correct much. Grading equipment arrives by April, and a relaunch strategy will follow, with the business model still under discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Will profit stay around 100 crore for the year, and can raw material inflation be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is very confident of repeating 100-plus crore this year. It said international prices are set by global competition, not Indian cost, so pass-through is uncertain; soya imports and backward integration are the offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Will quarterly profits exceed 16 crore in the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly projections, saying it did not think SEBI permits it, and reiterated only the 100 crore-plus ballpark for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the expansion receive interest subvention, and what capex is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: The 3% interest subvention applies only to farm investment, not egg processing. Powder expansion is about 180 crore with 150 crore term loan at 8.25%; benefits from the farms come gradually and fully by September 28.

qa_highlights.question: Why hold about 167 crore cash while borrowing 300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company keeps about 100 crore for seasonality and that its cost of funds is about 5.25% after 3% interest subvention; it targets returns above 10% on surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will branded domestic eggs become a substantial part of turnover within two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects it to become an important revenue stream within two to five years, but segment choice (premium, mid, or mass) is still being decided and should be firmed up in about three months.

risks_watch: Feed cost inflation (soya and other ingredients) compressing EBITDA; Q2 EBITDA fell to about 28 crore from 38 crore.
Japanese price pressure from US oversupply and softening international egg-powder prices.
EC farm commissioning slippage (already about one week behind) and the 2.4 million bird target by September 28.
Debt rising to about 450 crore for the investment phase, with finance costs and dividend policy (25% payout) to watch.
Branded domestic egg strategy and business model still undecided; decision expected in about three months.
Freight cost increases from geopolitical events; South Korea first order targeted October-December.
