532149|2026-06.headline: Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 36.23% YoY to Rs 3,068 crore; Global NIM eased to 2.52% and FY27 guidance was kept unchanged.
532149|2026-06.overview: Bank of India reported Q1 FY27 net profit of Rs 3,068 crore, up 36.23% YoY, with operating profit up 25.99% to Rs 5,051 crore and NII up 12.61% to Rs 6,833 crore. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with Gross NPA at 1.81% and Net NPA at 0.51%, and slippage ratio at 0.24%. Global business grew 16.57% YoY to Rs 17.55 lakh crore, with advances up 18.64%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance for advances growth of 15-16% and deposit growth of 13-14%, and raised a dollar-funding target of $4.2 billion through FCNR(B), OFCB/MTN and ECB routes by December 2026.

segments.commentary: Global gross advances Rs 7.98 lakh crore (+18.64% YoY); domestic advances Rs 6.74 lakh crore (+19.20%). RAM advances Rs 3.93 lakh crore (+19.75%), 58.30% of advances.

segments.commentary: International business touched about Rs 2.56 lakh crore; around 32% of international loan book is trade finance, which management plans to reduce.

segments.commentary: Bank of India mutual fund AUM about Rs 16,000-17,000 crore; no near-term plan for public issue.

532149|2026-09.headline: Bank of India Q2 FY27: H1 net profit about Rs 6,000 crore, Global NIM 2.47%, Gross NPA 1.60%; ECL front-loading planned from Q3, about 0.5% CRAR impact per year.

Operating profit rose 33.18% to Rs 5,089 crore and net profit rose 25.32% to Rs 3,202 crore for Sept'26 (the Q2 figure as stated on the call). Asset quality improved, with Gross NPA at 1.60% and Net NPA at 0.42%, and credit cost fell to 0.12% from 0.15% in June'26. Global NIM eased 5 bps YoY to 2.47%, which management attributed mainly to FCNR-linked leverage. Management guided FY27 global advances growth of 15-16% and global deposit growth of 16-17%, and said ECL provisioning will begin from Q3 after Board approval.

financial_highlights.change: +Rs 20,539 crore YoY; ratio down from prior quarters
down 5 bps from 2.52% (management cited Sept'25 at 2.41%)

segments.name: Corporate and pipeline
segments.commentary: Corporate pipeline about Rs 65,000 crore as of 30 Sept; total pipeline across corporate, RAM, digital, pool/co-lending and supply chain about Rs 86,000-87,000 crore. Largest sector pipelines are renewable energy (over Rs 12,000 crore), power (over Rs 9,000 crore) and roads (over Rs 5,000 crore).

segments.name: RAM
segments.commentary: RAM advances up 18.68% YoY to Rs 4.13 lakh crore, 58.63% of gross advances, with RAM pipeline about Rs 20,000 crore.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about Rs 61,000 crore, mostly agriculture with some MSME and retail; gold loan NPA about 0.13%, LTV capped at 75%.

segments.name: Overseas book
segments.commentary: Overseas advances up 35.21% YoY to Rs 1.51 lakh crore against overseas deposits up 11.52% to Rs 1.37 lakh crore; FCNR raise of USD 2.2 billion was deployed into the international loan book.

segments.name: Supply chain / trade
segments.commentary: Supply chain book just over Rs 1,000 crore, with a Rs 1,500 crore first-year target; trade and MSME-linked assets grew about 10% in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 global advances growth guided at 15-16% and global deposit growth at 16-17%.

NIM expected to gain about 6-7 bps from the 25 bps repo hike, with deposit repricing staggered because about 60% of term deposits mature in 1 to 18 months.
Recovery in written-off accounts expected to sustain the run rate of about Rs 900-1,000 crore a quarter; non-interest income expected to hold above Rs 2,500 crore a quarter.
capex_capacity: Technology budget for opex and capex (core IT, digital, cybersecurity) said to be unchanged for FY27; Big Four consultants engaged on IT, digital and cybersecurity transformation.
AI policy approved by the Board; current AI use is predictive (Data Lake project), with analytics-led leads above Rs 21,000 crore.
Centralised supply chain branch in Mumbai handles pool, co-lending, trades and supply chain; 69 zones each asked to onboard one new supply chain vendor per month.
ECL: consultant onboarded; computation covers PD, LGD and SICR; Board note to be presented, with clarity expected by Q3.
demand_pricing: Domestic deposit and advances growth remained strong YoY, with management saying no impact from the macro headwinds is foreseen on FY27 business growth.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the ECL provisioning need, how much is already provided, and what is the road ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the broad total will not be shared until the Board note; the CRAR impact is about 0.5% per year over 4 years, covered by profits (H1 profit above Rs 6,000 crore, run rate of about Rs 12,000 crore for FY27). No ECL provision has been made yet; front-loading expected from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank still meet its growth targets given global and drought headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no impact on FY27 business growth at present, citing a pipeline of about 10% of the loan book, GST collections above Rs 2 lakh crore a month and e-way bills of Rs 13-14 crore a month.

qa_highlights.question: How much can NIM improve from the rate hike, and how will CASA be raised?

qa_highlights.question: What drove non-interest income, and why is other income down?

qa_highlights.question: Is there stress in the gold loan book after NBFC concerns?

qa_highlights.question: What is the government stake and any capital raise plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter holding is 73.8%, within the 75% SEBI limit. No government indication to reduce stake further and no capital raise plan.

risks_watch: ECL transition from 1 April 2027: quantum of front-loading and CRAR impact, pending Board approval and the Q3 update.

532156|2026-03.headline: Vaibhav Global FY26: PBT up 41% YoY, record FCF of INR272 crore, EBITDA margin 10.8%; FY27 guidance 9-11% revenue growth and 50-100 bps margin expansion.
532156|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR935 crore (+10% YoY) with EBITDA of INR96 crore (about 10.3%) and PBT of INR64 crore (+41% YoY). For FY26, revenue was INR3,691 crore, EBITDA margin rose 140 bps to 10.8%, and free cash flow hit a record INR272 crore. In-house brands crossed 50% of B2C sales about a year ahead of plan, and Germany reached full-year EBITDA breakeven. Management guided FY27 to 9-11% revenue growth and a 50-100 bps EBITDA margin improvement, but gave no constant-currency guidance. U.S. and U.K. growth stayed weak in Q4, and the Mindful Souls write-off of about INR25 crore was a notable one-off.

financial_highlights.value: INR6 per share (incl. final INR1.5 recommended)

segments.name: U.S.

segments.name: Germany
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 7%; Germany achieved full-year FY26 EBITDA breakeven and is expected to contribute to group profit from FY27.

segments.commentary: Lifestyle products are ~35% of total sales (medium-term target 50%). Lab-grown diamonds are ~11% of retail revenue at ASP around USD 250 (about 18 months old category).

FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 50-100 bps; gross margin and employee-cost efficiencies named as main sources, with shipping leverage unlikely this year.

Tax rate steady at around 22% for upcoming years.

Elevated precious metal prices and cautious discretionary spend were cited as headwinds across core markets; tariff uncertainty persists.

qa_highlights.question: How can EBITDA margin rise back toward the 13-15% levels seen in FY22 when revenue is much larger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Germany's breakeven and digital/paid media investments weighed on margin; margin rose from 7% (FY23) to 11% (FY26). Leverage expected in HR, SG&A and shipping; peak 15% seen as achievable over time but no precise timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why not enter India, and will the company consider a buyback given the share price decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Agrawal said TV shopping never took off in India, so entry would be digital-only, to be considered after digital maturity in the Western markets. No buyback response was given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Lifestyle 50% target versus in-house jewellery mix: are these contradictory?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Panwad clarified that in-house brands are 50% of B2C, of which 85% is jewellery and 15% lifestyle; the 35% lifestyle share and 50% medium-term target are for total group sales, including external and umbrella brands.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins flat over three years despite digital mix shift, lab-grown and higher ASPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B sales growth (lower gross margin, no content cost) dilutes gross margin; Q4 gross margin rose ~180 bps and FY26 ~40 bps. Tariffs and metal spikes were a substantial headwind, and paid media channel margins are rising.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the 50-100 bps margin improvement come from, and what constant-currency growth to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin first, then employee cost efficiency; shipping leverage unlikely this year and SG&A not expected to leverage. No constant-currency guidance given; INR guidance used given macro and business transition.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a INR25 crore Mindful Souls write-off and what drove other expenses up ~16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Impairment reflects conservative testing as double-digit growth did not materialise; payback extended from 5 to 7 years. Other expenses rose on U.K. warehouse set-up, travel and AI technology spend, which management called temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in ROE and the ROU asset increase?
qa_highlights.answer: ROE was driven by PAT growth including a one-time MAT credit; normalised ROE still improves to ~15%. ROU increase is from a new U.K. premises lease signed around February 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Trends for U.S. growth and visibility from AI initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Agrawal cited AI across ad creatives, landing pages, conversion analytics and supply-chain forecasting, started about a year ago and accelerating recently. He expects U.S. and U.K. to reach double-digit growth in mid-to-long term but gave no timeline.

532174|2026-03.headline: ICICI Bank Q4 FY26 PBT ex-treasury rose 10.1% YoY to ₹18,209 crore, with provisions falling to just ₹96 crore.
532174|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 profit before tax excluding treasury grew 10.1% YoY to ₹18,209 crore and profit after tax grew 8.5% to ₹13,702 crore, helped by provisions of only ₹96 crore versus ₹891 crore in Q3. Core operating profit grew only 5.1% YoY as operating expenses rose 12.0%, so the bottom line leaned on low credit costs and recoveries from written-off accounts. Loan growth accelerated to 15.8% YoY, led by rural (+25.6%), business banking (+24.4%) and mortgages (+13.2%), while deposits grew 11.4%. Management declined to guide on loan growth and said NIM should stay range-bound in FY27, while flagging West Asia conflict uncertainty without yet seeing portfolio stress.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit rates rise, given recent falls?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate direction depends on macro conditions and it is difficult to make a long-term call; the bank focuses on CASA and primary-banking relationships.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the mortgage pickup and does the deposit-loan gap persist?

qa_highlights.question: Was there any provision release or write-back this quarter?

532174|2026-06.headline: ICICI Bank Q1 FY27: PBT excluding treasury rose 20.9% YoY to ₹18,975 crore; NIM 4.36%, loans up 19.6% YoY.
532174|2026-06.overview: ICICI Bank posted strong Q1 FY27 profit growth, with PBT excluding treasury up 20.9% YoY to ₹18,975 crore and PAT up 15.9% to ₹14,805 crore. Net interest margin expanded to 4.36% from 4.32% in Q4, helped by about 8 bps from income tax refund interest; excluding that, NIM was 4.28%. Loan growth accelerated to 19.6% YoY, led by a sequential pickup in domestic corporate (up 6.9% QoQ) and business banking, while asset quality was stable with net NPA at 0.35%. Management guided NIM to be range-bound in FY27 but flagged possible dilution from the FCNR(B) mobilisation push, and gave no FCNR amounts raised so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4.36% NIM sustainable and what levers exist, and what drove the slippage rise and West Asia stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax refund interest added about 8 bps; FY27 NIM expected range-bound absent rate moves, with FCNR dilution risk. Management said the quarter-on-quarter slippage rise is seasonal (KCC-related); Q1 FY27 gross additions of ₹5,552 crore compared with ₹6,245 crore a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: How much has been mobilised under FCNR(B), at what leverage, and will rates go above 6%?
qa_highlights.answer: No amount or leverage disclosed; management said rates will be calibrated, funding will come from partner banks, bond issuance and unleveraged inflows, and no need to raise rates above 6% currently. Details expected with Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% loan growth sustainable and where is the corporate demand coming from?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth reflects system momentum from policy measures, that there are no segment targets, and that corporate demand reflects working capital needs and bond/equity market moderation. Average loan growth will be somewhat lower than the period-end rate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the agri (KCC) provision write-back and the ECL transition?
qa_highlights.answer: Remediation of the agri portfolio is under validation before any provision write-back; no timeline given. ECL from April 2027 expected to have no net worth impact, with Stage 2 provisioning raising ongoing costs partly offset by Stage 3 changes; quantum not estimated.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-off recovery in Q1, and what is the normalised credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: One NCLT-driven recovery on an asset previously sold to NARCL came through this quarter. Reported credit cost 32 bps; normalised about 50 bps excluding chunky recoveries.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving fee income growth and card/personal loan trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee growth reflects broad business momentum plus a low base; sequential fee increase about ₹500 crore. Personal loans grew 12% YoY and 4% QoQ; cards growth is weak due to lower revolver rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LCR and NRI share of deposits, and surplus SLR?
qa_highlights.answer: LCR about 124% vs 128% a year ago. Surplus SLR and NRI share of deposits not disclosed; management expects NRI share to rise as FCNR(B) flows pick up.

532174|2026-09.headline: ICICI Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose 20.1% YoY to ₹14,843 crore, but NIM fell to 4.18% on FCNR(B) mix, with management guiding to a Q3 trough.
532174|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 profit before tax excluding treasury grew 23.4% YoY to ₹19,954 crore and PAT grew 20.1% to ₹14,843 crore, with standalone RoE of 16.6%. Net interest margin fell to 4.18% from 4.36% in Q1 (4.28% ex-tax-refund interest), which management attributed to FCNR(B) inflows, lower CASA mix and a larger overseas book. Total loans grew 30% YoY and deposits 27.1%, both flattered by about $10 billion of FCNR(B)-linked leverage; ex-leverage loans grew 24.1%. Asset quality stayed clean, with net NPA at 0.30% and the provision coverage ratio at 75%.

segments.commentary: Overseas loans were 7.8% of the book. FCNR(B) leverage loans sit in overseas branches, which earn about 1% margin versus 4%-plus domestic, and this mix shift is a key driver of margin compression.

Frankly, I would say that we have done better than what we originally thought we would do when this scheme started.

532175|2026-03.headline: Cyient DET Q4 FY26 revenue $163.5M, down 2.4% QoQ in constant currency; INR720 crore buyback at INR1,125/share announced.
532175|2026-03.overview: DET revenue fell 2.4% QoQ and 1.5% YoY in constant currency to $163.5M, as some client budget deployments shifted and West Asia energy deals slipped into later quarters. Normalized DET EBIT margin held at 12.4% and gross margin rose 114 bps QoQ to 38.9%. Management announced a buyback of up to 6.4M shares (5.76%) at INR1,125 per share for up to INR720 crore, and a planned fundraise at Cyient Semiconductor. The company also paused Project Astro, an acquisition, and took a INR71 crore exceptional diligence charge.

EBIT margin target of about 15% by Q4 FY27 (management equates this to roughly 17-17.5% EBITDA); margin levers are price hikes, automation/AI, and admin cost cuts.

qa_highlights.question: How much DET revenue is exposed to West Asia, and what headwind over the next few quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct exposure is not significant; exposure is project-based via Tier 1 EPC and energy firms, and the slipped deals were in the Middle East pipeline. No exact figure given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Project Astro asset and vertical?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishna declined to give specifics, citing NDAs; described it only as a very big transformative acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: How much dilution for the semiconductor fundraise and how do buyback and raise reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: First raise about 10-12% dilution, small; buyback is for Cyient, raise is to establish independent value for Cyient Semiconductor and avoid penalizing Cyient shareholders with its losses.

qa_highlights.question: Will strategic units keep degrowing in Q1, and will delayed programs return?
qa_highlights.answer: Connectivity delays are already in execution but capacity-limited, so work shifts rather than being lost. Target is roughly flat for Q1; energy/West Asia timing uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 outlook for semiconductor and margin path to 15% EBIT?
qa_highlights.answer: Semiconductor FY27 revenue about $100M with negative margins; 15% EBIT by Q4 FY27 target maintained, with price hikes, automation and admin cost cuts as levers, though geopolitics add volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Why has EBITDA margin fallen from about 18% in FY24, and when will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified the 16% peak was EBIT in Q4 FY24; the target is 15% EBIT by Q4 FY27, which equals roughly 17-17.5% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Which part of the business is most at risk from AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees AI threat as minimal overall; software development is a small portion where 20-30% productivity gains are seen; data and life cycle services seen as opportunities.

AI-driven pricing pressure in software development; 20-30% productivity gains could compress revenue on some work.
Group EBIT margin down 254 bps to 9.5%; margin path depends on pricing, cost actions and currency.
Leadership transition: new CFO Shrinivas Kulkarni and COO Prabhakar Atla from April 1, 2026.

key_quotes: I want also to categorically communicate that these were not structural to the business demand or our value proposition in the market.
We won't dilute more than maybe 10 -12% of the equity to start with.

It will be among the largest buybacks in the tech sector, and that's because our Board is very confident that while we have a lot of investment opportunities, we also have a lot of avenues for cash generation.

532175|2026-06.headline: Cyient Q1 FY27: DET revenue $162.5M, down 0.5% QoQ in constant currency, while DET EBIT margin rose to 13.2% and the 15% target slipped to H1 FY28.
532175|2026-06.overview: DET revenue was flat-to-down in constant currency (-0.5% QoQ, -0.9% YoY) but rose 2.7% QoQ and 10.6% YoY in rupee terms. Normalized DET EBIT margin expanded to 13.2% (+79 bps QoQ, +114 bps YoY) on cost optimisation and a stronger USD. Management pushed out its 15% EBIT target from Q4 FY27 to around H1 FY28 because revenue ramp-up is lagging, and it said mid-single-digit FY27 growth is now hard to achieve. Group revenue was $219M (+4.5% QoQ, +9.1% YoY in constant currency), with Kinetic Technologies consolidated for the first time.

segments.name: DET (Digital Engineering & Technology)
segments.commentary: Revenue $162.5M, -0.5% QoQ cc, with normalized EBIT margin of 13.2% (+79 bps QoQ). Transportation & mobility grew 3% QoQ and 14.8% YoY cc, while strategic units fell 8.2% QoQ on energy weakness.

segments.name: Cyient DLM
segments.commentary: Management said the quarter closed with its highest-ever order book and book-to-bill above 1.5, with double-digit EBITDA margins for four consecutive quarters. No DLM financial figures were given on the call.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: Combined revenue $17.9M including Kinetic ($10.4M). Organic business $7.5M (+5% QoQ). Management expects breakeven only in FY28, with about $3M per quarter of Kinetic-related amortisation to cover.

guidance_outlook: 15% DET EBIT target now expected about H1 FY28 rather than Q4 FY27, because revenue ramp-up is behind plan while cost levers are on track.
No formal revenue guidance; management said mid-single-digit growth for FY27 will be challenged and it is 'hopeful' of meaningful growth returning in H2 FY27.
Full-year DET effective tax rate expected at 27-28%.
Semiconductor breakeven expected in FY28; high-voltage/high-power ASSP development to consume cash for at least the next four to five quarters.
TAO Digital Solutions closing expected by August 2026 (late Q2); TAO revenue expected at roughly $40-50M, with consolidation from about late Q2.
Investor Day scheduled for 25 August 2026 in Mumbai.
capex_capacity: DET capex was higher in Q1 due to a cyclical IT system refresh and project ramp-up.
Management chose not to cut investments, including in the high-power semiconductor ASSP program, which it says is funded organically and absorbs most of the cash flow.
Semiconductor: seven new GaN-powered chips launched on Navitas technology; custom ASIC pipeline above $100M.
Share buyback completed: 6.4M shares at Rs 1,125 (Rs 720 Cr, about 5.76% of paid-up capital), settled after the quarter ended.
Financing: $30M raised through a mix of debt and equity closed under the $500M post-money round announced 25 May 2026.
demand_pricing: Order intake was up 5.3% YoY; five large deals won across Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27, and a large-deal pipeline of over $300M created or qualified (nine deals in Q1).
Existing-business renewals were weak because of project completions, delayed restarts of discretionary projects and customer hesitancy, which management described as timing rather than structural.

Energy: the prior large single project has completed; management expects one to two more quarters before growth rebounds, with cross-selling into North America under way and nuclear engineering wins expected in one to two quarters.
Telecom/connectivity: fibre build-out capex is seen as visible, but Q1 was affected by delayed program starts and fiscal-year seasonality.
Aerospace: no impact yet on business-as-usual work, but flying-hour concerns from the West Asia conflict have stopped some discretionary projects.
Management did not disclose or quantify pricing changes; it cited customer rate increases as one lever for margin.

financial_highlights.change: +5% QoQ; fifth consecutive quarter of >5% organic growth

qa_highlights.question: Is Strategic Units at the bottom after two quarters of decline, or is there more impact from delayed discretionary spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Energy is the one market still soft; management expects one or two more quarters before growth rebounds and aims to narrow the gap or make it flat next quarter. Other strategic-unit verticals are delivering adequate results.

qa_highlights.question: Is Transportation & Mobility growth driven by a single project or a broader sector trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Not one project. Aerospace, rail and automotive each grew QoQ and at double digits YoY, so growth is broad-based.

qa_highlights.question: How will semiconductor breakeven come through, including PAT, given Kinetic acquisition debt, and what is growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven expected only in FY28. High-voltage ASSP development will consume cash for at least four to five more quarters, and about $3M per quarter of Kinetic-related amortisation must be covered. Growth expected to stay strong, with custom ASIC pipeline above $100M.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the energy vertical lost momentum versus peers that are winning deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier growth was built on one very large project, now completed. Management cited three fixes: a rebuilt go-to-market team, prioritised offerings, and a broader service portfolio, with a multi-year digitalisation deal with a large energy OEM as an example.

qa_highlights.question: Will DET revenue growth turn positive from Q2 and accelerate through FY27? Also, when will the 15% EBIT margin be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth will build slowly over the quarters. On margin, cost levers are on track but absorption from growth will come late. Management expects 15% to be reached around H1 FY28, a couple of quarters into next year, and wage-hike decisions will be taken at the start of H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for FY27, including TAO once consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: There was no formal guidance; the aim was mid-single-digit growth, which is now challenged. Management is hopeful of meaningful growth in H2 FY27 but gave no landing figure. TAO is expected to close in late Q2 with revenue of about $40-50M.

qa_highlights.question: Why was existing-business renewal weak despite strong order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: Project-based work ended (mostly planned), discretionary restarts were delayed, and customers were hesitant to commit. Management called this timing rather than structural.

risks_watch: Energy vertical recovery: management expects one or two more quarters before growth rebounds; strategic units fell 8.2% QoQ.
DET 15% EBIT target slipped to around H1 FY28, with absorption from revenue growth arriving late and wage-hike decisions pending at start of H2.
FY27 mid-single-digit growth is now hard to achieve; revenue growth in H2 FY27 is the key test.

TAO closing by August 2026 and TAO revenue of about $40-50M; TAO financials not yet confirmed by management before closing.
Debt rising with TAO and Kinetic acquisitions; management cited sub-3% cost for Kinetic debt and SOFR-based debt for TAO.
DET effective tax rate of 27-28% for FY27 versus 29.2% in Q1; Q1 DET FCF down 49% QoQ.
Possible DLM demerger: management said no plan for now, with continued structure for the foreseeable future.
key_quotes: We are still working towards a 15% EBIT, but we now believe that this may take a little longer than the Q4 F Y27 we originally aimed for.
We remain firmly on track on the cost side and it is the revenue ramp up where we are running a little behind and that is where our attention is now.

Now, of course, that will be challenged or given just the way the mathematics works, if you have not started the year with a growth, I think the ask rate for the rest of the year does become very hard.

But having said that it has nothing to do with any structural issues or market issues it has more to do with some of the timing and both from a project perspective as well as customer willingness to commit to new projects.

532175|2026-09.headline: Cyient Q2 FY27: DET revenue $174.2M (+7.5% QoQ, +6.3% YoY cc) and EBIT margin 14.2%, highest in 10 quarters; organic growth only 1.6% QoQ.
532175|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed DET revenue of $174.2M including one month of TAO Digital (about $9.6M), with organic DET revenue of $164.5M up 1.6% QoQ and 0.4% YoY in constant currency. Record Q2 order intake of $158.4M (up nearly 21% YoY) excludes a €50M-per-year frame agreement with a consumer goods major. EBIT margin rose to 14.2%, aided by cost optimisation and billing days, and DET free cash flow reached Rs.214 Cr. Management flagged a wage hike in Q3 and Q4, a deferred semiconductor breakeven (still FY28), and softer near-term semiconductor growth on supply constraints.

segments.name: Networks & Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Flattish at -0.3% QoQ cc and +1% YoY, reflecting completion of project engagements and weakness in utilities; portfolio reshaping announcements expected soon.

segments.name: Strategic Markets
segments.commentary: Declined 1.5% QoQ in constant currency; management says energy is at the bottom and should grow, and the strategic markets mix is roughly 65% energy/process, 22% HLS and the rest mining & minerals.

segments.name: DLM
segments.commentary: Revenue grew more than 26% YoY in INR; order book at a record high with book-to-bill above 1.6x; H1 revenue more than 30% above H1 last year.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue guidance; management expressed confidence in H2 FY27 growth, which excludes TAO Digital.

qa_highlights.question: What share of DET revenue is sticky annuity and what is the target?

qa_highlights.question: Why is the €50M framework agreement excluded from order intake, and when will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a framework agreement without signed commitment; SOWs will be booked into order intake when signed. Ramp takes one to two years, with some ramp-up in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TAO Digital run-rate and growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired at about $80M run-rate, now close to $100M; next 12 months could be $100-110M, a rough estimate pending Q3 results.

qa_highlights.question: Will TAO margins be similar to DET?
qa_highlights.answer: At EBIT level after intangibles, interest and earn-out effects, margins are very close to Cyient's; at EBITDA level they are materially higher.

qa_highlights.question: How will wage hikes affect margins in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-phase hikes over Q3 and Q4 with roughly equal impact; cost optimisation gives visibility to hold margins at current levels and grow through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Semiconductor breakeven timeline and near-term growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven still targeted for FY28, possibly deferred a quarter or two; slowdown is supply-driven rather than demand-driven, with high-voltage chip revenue expected during FY28.

risks_watch: Organic DET growth only 1.6% QoQ and 0.4% YoY cc; H2 confidence depends on the frame agreement and pending deals.
Commercial aviation headwind from oil prices and the Middle East war; scenario analysis shows aerospace and automotive growth exposed to a downturn.
Semiconductor supply constraints, rising wafer and memory costs; EBIT losses continue due to product R&D; breakeven could slip.
Wage hikes in Q3 and Q4 and FX movements could pressure margins despite cost optimisation.
Declining client and account counts; top 5 and top 10 accounts ramped down in Q2.
Interest costs from the $120M acquisition debt and an earn-out liability; mining and minerals portfolio still being reworked.
532175|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on margins, order intake and H2 growth, but cautious on Semiconductor near-term growth and evasive on specific numbers (no guidance, deferred annuity and TAO specifics). Management stresses that the Q2 rebound was faster than expected.

We recorded highest ever Q2 order intake of $158.4 million, up nearly 21% year-over-year, with positive momentum across both new businesses in existing and new customers from an order intake perspective.
The breakeven timeline remains intact. We will breakeven somewhere in FY 2028.
We are back with a renewed leadership team.

532178|2026-03.headline: Engineers India FY26 standalone turnover rose 27% to Rs.3,849 crore and PAT 37% to Rs.638 crore; order book hit a record Rs.15,109 crore.
532178|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: standalone turnover Rs.3,849 crore (+27% YoY), PAT Rs.638 crore (+37%), operating margin 16.22% (vs 14.76%), and EPS Rs.11.36 (vs Rs.8.28). Q4 turnover was Rs.899 crore with PBT Rs.195 crore and PAT Rs.152 crore. Order inflow was Rs.7,979 crore versus Rs.8,214 crore a year earlier, while the order book reached Rs.15,109 crore (Rs.11,717 crore a year earlier). Management flagged a slowdown in Middle East awards due to the regional conflict, while domestic and Africa activity was steady, and guided FY27 consultancy margins of 20-25% and LSTK margins of 5-7%.

segments.name: Consultancy & engineering
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover Rs.1,782 crore (vs Rs.1,678 crore); Q4 turnover Rs.489 crore with a reported Q4 margin near 29%, which management attributed to a Rs.221 crore change order, not a one-off write-back. Guided segment margin 20-25%.

segments.name: Turnkey (LSTK)
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover Rs.2,067 crore (vs Rs.1,349 crore); Q4 turnover Rs.410 crore. Guided segment margin 5-7%. Dangote refinery (USD 360 million) and fertilizer (USD 70 million, four lines) contracts are being executed, started around January 2026.

segments.name: Subsidiary CEIL
segments.commentary: Profit rose to Rs.24.71 crore in FY26 from Rs.20.62 crore. Associate (refinery-linked) profit was about Rs.40 crore in the latest quarter after a shutdown-affected earlier period; management expects 100% plant capacity this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow to stay around Rs.8,000 crore (consultancy plus LSTK), with an aim to exceed it; management said FY27 inflow is hard to predict beyond one or two quarters.
FY27 revenue growth guided at a minimum of 10-15%, based on two months of the year elapsed.
Consultancy segment margin to be sustained at 20-25%; LSTK segment margin at 5-7%.
Consultancy revenue growth seen conservatively at 15-20% a year over the next two to three years.
Middle East: management expects a delay of a couple of months in big-ticket awards; Africa and the new Saudi Aramco agreements (5+3 years) are the growth routes.
Final dividend of Rs.2.5 per share proposed; with the interim Rs.2.5, total FY26 dividend is Rs.5 per share (100% of face value Rs.5).
capex_capacity: Dangote refinery and fertilizer projects are about four years in duration; site activity expected to start around end-2026 or early 2027.
Andhra (BPCL) project: feasibility underway; licensor selection next, with project activities targeted in FY27.
IOCL Paradip phase-2 balance order (about Rs.8-10 billion) expected to be awarded by end of FY27, after the investment decision.
Panipat (P25) project is in advanced construction and expected to commission soon.
Company is setting up a CBG plant in Maharashtra on its own investment and is the OT consultant for an MRPL sustainable aviation fuel plant.
demand_pricing: Order book is at a record Rs.15,109 crore, but FY26 inflow was slightly lower than FY25 at Rs.7,979 crore.
Middle East is about 30% of overseas business secured, and roughly 10-15% of the current order book. Big-ticket Middle East awards are slower, with client decisions delayed by security concerns.
Africa is the main overseas focus after the Dangote awards; management sees investment shifting to Africa as an alternative hub.
Infrastructure is about 25% of FY26 order inflow (clients include ONGC, NTPC, Government of Rajasthan, IIMs/IITs and data centres).
Coal gasification: government raised viability gap funding; a consultancy opportunity of about Rs.300-400 crore was indicated. Project sizes of Rs.10,000-40,000 crore were cited.
Public-sector tenders are competitive or negotiated; hit rate on bids is about 20-25%. Nomination only for critical projects.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for FY27 consultancy inflow in domestic and international markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to sustain inflow at roughly the current level of about Rs.8,000 crore total; Middle East slowdown is the key risk, with domestic projects not being delayed or cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East share of the order book and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East is about 30% of overseas business secured and 10-15% of the current order book; a Saudi Aramco long-term agreement (5+3 years) was signed, with an out-of-kingdom agreement pending.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any one-off or change order behind Q4 consultancy margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no write-offs; a Rs.221 crore change order was received in FY26 and the expenditure already incurred, and the Q4 margins are described as normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue slippage Q4 vs Q3 and cost pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue slippage; the prior quarter included a change order over Rs.200 crore, which made it high-profit. Management did not report commodity cost impacts.

qa_highlights.question: Expected growth in FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Minimum 10-15% growth expected in FY27 execution; FY27 and FY28 revenue guidance was deferred to next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East and Africa opportunity size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.1,000-2,000 crore of projects is achievable over time, with an inflection expected around FY27-FY29.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict delaying big-ticket awards and revamp-led spending; monitor Saudi and out-of-kingdom agreement signing.
Consultancy order inflow, with FY26 slightly below FY25 and the Rs.8,000 crore FY27 target dependent on public-sector tenders.
Sustainability of 20%+ consultancy margins; Q4 margin benefited from a Rs.221 crore change order.
Dangote and IOCL Paradip conversion timing; large LSTK jobs carry 5-7% margins.
Associate plant operating at full capacity this year after a prior shutdown.
Disclosure readability: an analyst flagged that the figures uploaded to the exchanges are hard to read.
532178|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the domestic book and FY26 results, but cautious and hedged on the Middle East and on FY27 inflow, repeatedly saying 'let us hope' and 'too early' to answer questions on timelines and sizes.
key_quotes: Company order book position has reached its all-time high and stands at Rs.15,109 crores as on 31st March 2026, as compared to Rs.11,717 crores as on 31st March 2025.
We are continuously maintaining our consultancy margin in the range of 20% to 25% percent and in the LSTK business around 5% to 7%.
There is no nomination cases are coming from the public sector unless there is a very critical project or there is nobody in the industry who can do it.
But we have not seen in the domestic market anywhere any project being delayed or anything being done.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs.11,717 crore a year earlier

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at minimum 10-15% (midpoint 12.5%) against FY26 turnover of Rs.3,849 crore (+27%), backed by a record Rs.15,109 crore order book, though FY27 order inflow is held flat at about Rs.8,000 crore vs Rs.7,979 crore.

The CBG plant in Maharashtra is company-funded, with no size or date given.

rows.label: Africa and Saudi Aramco agreements as growth routes
rows.why: Management sees Rs.1,000-2,000 crore of Middle East and Africa projects achievable over time, with an inflection around FY27-FY29, and the Saudi Aramco 5+3 year agreement is signed while an out-of-kingdom agreement is pending.

rows.label: Dangote refinery and fertilizer execution
rows.when: site activity from end-2026 or early 2027
rows.why: Dangote refinery (USD 360 million) and fertilizer (USD 70 million, four lines) contracts are already being executed since around January 2026, with a roughly four-year duration and LSTK margins of 5-7%.

rows.label: Coal gasification consultancy opportunity
rows.why: Government raised viability gap funding and a consultancy opportunity of about Rs.300-400 crore was indicated, with project sizes of Rs.10,000-40,000 crore, but timing is not given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the domestic book and FY26 results but hedged on Middle East awards and FY27 inflow, repeatedly saying 'let us hope' and 'too early'; analysts pushed on the Rs.221 crore change order behind the Q4 consultancy margin and on FY27 revenue and inflow outlook.

532178|2026-06.headline: Engineers India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 55% to INR109 crores, while turnover fell 7% to INR801 crores on Turnkey decline.
532178|2026-06.overview: Standalone PBT rose about 55% YoY to INR145 crores and PAT to INR109 crores, helped by Consultancy growth of about 22% to INR499 crores. Turnkey turnover fell to INR302 crores from INR449 crores as major projects tapered. Order book stood at INR14,424 crores at 30 June 2026, but Q1 order inflow was only INR514 crores. Management kept the INR8,000 crore FY27 order inflow target and the FY27 operating margin guidance of 16%, and said the Middle East new-mega-project pipeline has slowed.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR104 crores, 11.72% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR14,424 crores (Consultancy INR10,498 crores; Turnkey INR3,926 crores)

segments.name: Consultancy & Engineering
segments.commentary: Turnover INR499 crores, up ~22% YoY; segment profit margin rose to ~24% from 17% in Q1 FY26, with management targeting 24-25%.

segments.name: Turnkey (LSTK)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR302 crores, down from INR449 crores as major projects tapered; segment margin ~7.5% in Q1 FY27. New Turnkey orders are in early execution, with turnover expected to rise in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: CEIL subsidiary
segments.commentary: Profit INR6.88 crores vs INR2.69 crores a year earlier.

segments.name: Joint ventures / associates
segments.commentary: Contributed INR42.51 crores to consolidated profit vs a loss of INR7.37 crores in Q1 FY26. RFCL contributed about INR42 crores of revenue-linked profit; management expects some dividend from RFCL this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow target of INR8,000 crores maintained; management said it will try to cross it. Current inflow is about INR2,750 crores (about INR1,100 crores overseas, about INR1,500 crores domestic, of which ~INR1,500 crores domestic is LSTK and the rest consultancy).
FY27 consultancy revenue targeted at more than 50%, possibly around 55%, implying consultancy turnover of INR2,300-2,400 crores.
Total FY27 turnover growth target of at least 10% on last year's INR3,850-4,200 crore base; management said guidance could improve.
FY27 operating margin target held at 16%, same as FY26; upside possible if pending change orders are settled.
FY28 revenue target of INR5,000 crores maintained, with an intent to improve it.
Dividend payout of around 100% for the current financial year referenced.
capex_capacity: Company is setting up a CBG plant with its own investment (non-hydrocarbon).
RFCL plant expected to run about 330 days a year; a 30-35 day regular shutdown in December will carry technical work without hitting profitability.
No specific capex amounts or commissioning dates were given for other projects.
demand_pricing: Middle East: new mega projects on hold or slow; existing jobs continuing. Secured about INR500 crores of Middle East business in Q1, including PMC work of INR400 crores under long-term agreements. Aramco contract in place but no major inquiry yet.
Overseas share of current inflow is about INR1,100 crores out of INR2,750 crores.
Nuclear: environmental studies for 3 private projects and 1 government project; engaged with NPCIL on engineering consultancy; SMR work secured last year.
Coal gasification: government VGF support of INR34,000 crores revived feasibility inquiries; an NTPC gas-to-SNG project is ongoing; results expected in a couple of months.
Domestic pipeline: BPCL Andhra execution tender may come by year-end; IOCL Paradip Phase 2 awaits OMC approval; ONGC petrochemical project only at feasibility stage.
Infrastructure about 45% of business in the current year, mostly LSTK/OBE, with a recent data-centre assignment from PowerTel.
Competition described as high in all segments, with most work won through competitive bidding.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crore order inflow target still achievable, and how much would be consultancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is unchanged, with about INR2,750 crores in hand now and about two quarters left. Consultancy is about INR1,100 crores of this, with the rest mainly LSTK domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be write-backs or change orders this year, including HPCL Barmer?
qa_highlights.answer: No exceptional change order is in the current quarter and no provision write-backs are expected; provisions reverse only after the defect liability period ends.

qa_highlights.question: How should consultancy growth and margins be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Consultancy growth target is at least 10%+ overall, with consultancy above 50% of turnover; segment profit is targeted at 24-25%. Operating margin target is 16%, with possible upside from change orders.

qa_highlights.question: Have Middle East clients put projects on hold due to the conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no existing project is stopped; new mega projects are on hold or slow, and routine jobs continue.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue be recognised on the Dangote Nigeria order?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on cost-progress basis, with turnover booked as cost progress is achieved over about 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan to distribute surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans to distribute the full reserves now, as other investment plans are under consideration, and pointed to about 100% dividend this year.

risks_watch: Turnkey turnover fell 33% YoY; management expects recovery in Q3-Q4 but this depends on execution of new projects still in early phase.
Q1 order inflow of INR514 crores is far below the run rate needed for INR8,000 crores; the target depends on a few lumpy domestic and overseas wins.
Middle East (about 12-15% exposure per analyst estimate) faces slow new mega-project awards; Saudi/Aramco work still at initial discussion stage.
Q1 operating margin of ~14% is below the 16% full-year target, so the guidance depends on later quarters and change-order settlements.
Coal gasification and nuclear inquiries remain at feasibility or EOI stage; timing and value of awards unclear.
Management did not confirm the Turnkey-to-consultancy mix beyond ranges given, and gave conflicting statements on the consultancy share (50-60%, around 55%).

key_quotes: Company order book position stands at INR14,424 crores as on 30th June 2026, which comprises consultancy segment of INR10,498 crores and Turnkey segment constitute of INR3,926 crores.

Definitely, it is the strategy of the company to keep consultancy business on higher side since we are having margin -- strong margin in the consultancy segment.

rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launches were discussed.

532209|2026-03.headline: J&K Bank posts FY26 net profit of INR2,363 crores, a fourth straight record, with Q4 profit near INR800 crores (up 36% QoQ); FY27 NIM guided at ~3.5%.
532209|2026-03.overview: FY26 delivered a record annual net profit of INR2,363 crores and a record quarterly profit of nearly INR800 crores, up 36% QoQ. Business grew 13.6%, with advances up 16.8% and deposits up 11.3%, both above guidance. NIM for FY26 was 3.60%, a marginal miss against guidance, attributed to 125 bps of RBI rate cuts in 2025 and deposit competition. Operating expenses fell about 4%, and GNPA/NNPA stood at 2.50%/0.64%. FY27 guidance is conservative: credit growth 12%, deposits 10%, NIM about 3.5%, RoA maintained, RoE about 16%, GNPA below 2.25%.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR734 crores in Q4 FY25; includes INR153 crore one-off reversal

financial_highlights.value: INR180 crore impairment on EDB amalgamation into J&K Gramin Bank

segments.name: Jammu, Kashmir & Ladakh (J&K)
segments.commentary: Loan growth 9.5% in FY26 versus 28.8% in Rest of India; J&K & Ladakh share of loan book is 63% versus 37% for Rest of India as on 31 March 2026. Bank holds about 60% market share but only 37% branch share.

segments.name: Rest of India
segments.commentary: Loan growth 28.8% in FY26 under the recalibrated strategy; Personal loans grew above 13%, with housing and education loans growing double digits.

segments.name: Corporate and Agriculture
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 38.5% and Agriculture 27.6% in FY26. Financial market book (mainly AAA-rated NBFCs) rose sharply to about INR20,000 crores, with co-lending still immaterial.

segments.name: Retail, Agriculture & MSME (RAM)
segments.commentary: RAM remains more than two-thirds of the loan book. Car loans grew 17.5% and were the best-performing personal loan segment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 credit growth guidance 12%, deposit growth 10%, CASA 45%.
FY27 NIM guided at around 3.5%; management said it could be revised upward next quarter once retail yields recover.
RoA to be maintained around the current 1.37%; RoE around 16%; GNPA below 2.25%.
Employee cost expected at around INR500 crores per quarter for the next two quarters; full-year FY27 employee cost seen around INR2,500 crores or lower.
Credit cost guided at 0.1% to 0.2%, excluding ECL impact.
Business target of above INR5 lakh crores in three years from the current ~INR2.9 lakh crores; management said it would grow above system if system grows 16%.
capex_capacity: Capital raise of up to INR1,250 crores planned in FY27 at an opportune time, with Board and shareholder approval already obtained; RBI ECL framework effective 1 April 2027.
Management estimated five-year ECL provisioning of around INR1,600 to INR1,700 crores on RBI's base requirements.
Co-lending target of around INR1,000 crores for FY27, with Board approval up to INR5,000 crores; co-lending started only in Q4 FY26.
Zonal ARBs introduced as specialised recovery units.
End-to-end digitised loan journeys in place for all loans; TAT for corporate, mid-corporate and SME loans reduced substantially in Q4.
demand_pricing: Yield on advances fell due to 125 bps of RBI rate cuts in 2025 and higher-rated corporate lending at competitive rates; FY27 focus is on retail, which management expects to lift yields.
Deposit competition in J&K is intensifying, mainly in Srinagar and Jammu, while the bank holds about 80-85% share in smaller districts.
Management says the bank recovered some lost accounts in FY26; April 2026 business figures were the best of any April, per management.
Management said it has not found any sticky sector; no MFI exposure; all NBFC exposures are AAA-rated, mainly housing, public sector and gold loans.
SMA-2 rose to 0.71% in March 2026 from 0.35% a year earlier, but was down from 2.92% in December 2025.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall sharply, and what is the run rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Pension obligations are shifting to NPS and retirements have reduced headcount. Q4 employee cost was INR509 crores including a INR153 crore discount-rate reversal. Management expects about INR500 crores per quarter for the next two quarters and about INR2,500 crores for the full year, with some hiring of specialists.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall, and what was the Gramin Bank item?
qa_highlights.answer: A one-time INR180 crore impairment on the investment in J&K Gramin Bank, taken in other income after the NABARD-directed amalgamation of Ellaquai Dehati Bank (EDB). Management said it was a policy decision and occurred in the full year, not in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank grow faster than the system?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is conservative. Management said it would aim to grow above 16% if system growth reached 16%.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM improve, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects NIM to improve because deposit repricing benefits are yet to accrue. Retail income from J&K will take one to one-and-a-half quarters to regenerate. Management may revise NIM guidance upward next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost outlook beyond the next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost guided at 0.1% to 0.2% maximum for FY27, excluding ECL. Management said it cannot foresee credit cost above 1% over the next three to four years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated five-year ECL provisioning of INR1,600 to INR1,700 crores, using RBI base requirements, and said the actual number will depend on the bank's board-approved model.

risks_watch: ECL transition from 1 April 2027 with about INR1,600 to 1,700 crores of five-year provisioning and a capital raise of INR1,250 crores.

532209|2026-06.headline: J&K Bank Q1 FY27 net profit fell to INR424 crore on margin compression to 3.28% and higher standard-asset provisions, despite 25.44% advances growth.

Operating profit was INR703 crore (+5% YoY), but net profit of INR424 crore was below last year, driven by standard-asset provisions raised on strong credit growth and lower technical write-off recoveries. NIM compressed to 3.28% as cost of deposits stayed high (4.74%) while yield on advances was 8.56%. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged for now, to be reassessed after Q2, but indicated credit growth of 18-20% against the 12% guidance.

segments.name: J&K and Ladakh
segments.commentary: Home-market share of banking business at 61.13% (31 March 2026); deposit market share improved in 19 of 22 districts during FY26.

Chairman-level view: actual credit growth 'will not be less than' 18-20% in FY27; J&K growth ~12-13%, ROI growth ~25%.

NIM expected to return to around 3.5% 'by end of Q3, definitely'; retail yields to be at least 200 bps above corporate book.
Management expects FY27 profit to exceed FY26 profit of about INR2,367 crore.

Operating expenses expected flat at worst; Q1 employee cost to be the base for the year, with some recruitment planned.

532209|2026-09.headline: J&K Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose about 29% QoQ to INR546 crore; management raised FY27 credit growth guidance to 14%+ and sees ROA of about 1.20%.
532209|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 net profit was INR546 crore, up about 29% QoQ with double-digit YoY growth, after a weak Q1. Operating profit rose 27% YoY to INR789 crore, helped by operating expenses up only 2% QoQ and cost-to-income falling to 56.57%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.23% and NNPA at 0.51%, and H1 gross slippages were INR234 crore versus INR550 crore a year earlier. Management revised FY27 guidance after the mid-term review: credit growth 14%+, deposit growth 12%+, CASA 42%+, ROA about 1.20% and GNPA below 2%. Key open items are the ECL transition impact, which management will quantify in December, and NIM, which management declined to quantify.

Gross slippage amount roughly halved YoY

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Auto loans grew over 25% YoY; Rest of India housing grew double digits YoY. Retail yield about 10%. Management says 60% of FY27 growth target will come from retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost outlook, and what is the ongoing cost after ECL?

532210|2026-03.headline: City Union Bank Q4 FY26: advances up 26% YoY to INR66,698 crore and PAT up 25% to INR360 crore, with gross NPA at 1.91%.
532210|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the bank's strongest quarter in recent years, with total business growing about 24% YoY and advances up 26% to INR66,698 crore. Asset quality kept improving: gross NPA fell to 1.91% from 3.09% a year earlier, and total SMA fell to 2.47% from 3.68% in Q3. Q4 PAT rose 25% to INR360 crore, the highest single quarter, and FY26 PAT rose 18% to INR1,326 crore with ROA at 1.56%. The call also marked the handover of MD and CEO from Dr. N. Kamakodi to R. Vijay Anandh effective 1 May 2026.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loans are about 30% of the book and growing faster than overall loans; management says the 30% level is near the upper limit, with 1-2% flexibility. Per-gram lending was capped around INR10,000-10,500 even at peak gold prices.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Core focus segment, with management citing rising capacity utilisation and CC limit usage as demand drivers. FY27 plan keeps MSME at 55-60% of the mix. Only 3-4% of MSME loans are under CGTMSE cover.

segments.name: Secured retail
segments.commentary: Housing and loans against property are growing and are an additional growth driver. FY27 plan uses secured retail to fill the remaining share of the mix after MSME and gold.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth planned at 2-3% above industry credit growth, with MSME at 55-60%, gold loans and secured retail as additional enhancers.
FY27 NIM expected to stay in a narrow 5-10 bps band around the FY26 level of 3.74%.
FY27 operating expenses expected to rise 15-18% YoY, with about 75 branches to be opened in FY27 (about 50 in April, 25 by year-end).
ROA to exit FY27 at least 10 bps higher, at about 1.65-1.67%, supported by retail income and lower cost-to-income.
CD ratio to be kept at 85-87%. Third-party business to be 1-2% of the book. Fee income to be 55-60% of other income.

Credit cost expected to fall about 50% from the 15-year average of about 0.60% over the next 15 years; individual years may vary. Management said the ECL circular lets banks adjust the opening balance, so the ECL impact on P&L is expected to be limited.

About 75 branches to be opened in FY27, with about 50 in April 2026 (70 opened in the first month per the CEO-designate); branches typically reach breakeven in year one.
Distribution capacity was lifted by the Newgen LOS and digital process set, which the management credits for secured MSME and retail growth.
demand_pricing: Advances grew by over INR5,800 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR13,600 crore for the full year; double-digit growth has run for eight consecutive quarters.
Deposit growth was matched to credit growth, with CASA at 28% of deposits and the average CD ratio at 85% for FY26. Some CDs were replaced by retail term deposits.
Yield on advances was 9.80% in Q4 (9.73% in Q3) and 9.75% for FY26 (9.79% in FY25). The cost of deposits was 5.60% in Q4 (5.57% in Q3).
Management said rate passthrough was completed around December 2025, and incremental yields are holding up, with non-agri gold loans at double-digit yields.
Management is watching the US-Iran conflict and oil prices; no visible impact on asset quality so far. Management expects a 1-2% extra slippage rate in a downturn, mainly on new business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for steady-state credit costs after the ECL norms?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the 15-year average credit cost is about 0.60%, and FY25 and FY26 were 0.09% and 0.04%. He expects at least a 50% reduction over the long run, with AI-based underwriting cited as the reason.

qa_highlights.question: Will underwriting filters tighten given fuel prices and demand risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it watches SMA trends and branch and customer feedback. It would add some caution to filters but has no plan to change them now, as underwriting is set for multiple business cycles.

risks_watch: Gold price correction on the INR30%+ gold book and whether LTV cushions hold.
Impact of the US-Iran conflict and oil prices on MSME demand and slippages; management expects an extra 1-2% slippage in a downturn.
Rising deposit costs as the bank fine-tunes rates to fund faster credit growth; the CD ratio is at 85% and CASA at 28%.
Opex growth of 15-18% in FY27 from branch expansion, against the ROA target of 1.65-1.67%.
Leadership transition: MD and CEO handover on 1 May 2026, plus the retirement of two independent directors in February 2026. The retiring MD's future non-executive board role depends on RBI approval.
532210|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and asset quality, with management saying it met all earlier guidance. More cautious on macro risks, particularly the US-Iran conflict and fuel prices. Evasive on the ECL steady-state credit cost, deferring that question to the CEO-designate.
key_quotes: By and large, almost all the expectations whatever we shared with you in the earlier con-calls for the financial year 2026 were met in the same spirit whatever we had shared with you.
The gross NPA has come below 2 % mark after 11 years.
I think we should exit this year with at least 10 bps more in ROA, so we should be there between 1.65% to 1.67%.

financial_highlights.change: down from 3.09% YoY and 2.17% in Q3
Q4 vs 3.89% in Q3; FY26 up 14 bps from 3.60%

financial_highlights.value: INR1,856 crore in Q4; INR6,870 crore in FY26

financial_highlights.change: up from 78% and 60% a year earlier
recoveries INR231 crore (INR153 crore from live NPAs, INR78 crore from technical write-offs)
down from 3.68% in Q3 and 5.60% in Q2

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM is guided to stay within a narrow 5-10 bps band around FY26's 3.74%, and cost of deposits rose to 5.60% in Q4 from 5.57% in Q3 as rates were fine-tuned to fund credit growth.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network reached 1,000 after the Kumbakonam opening on 4 May 2026, with about 75 more branches planned in FY27 (about 50 in April, 25 by year-end), a 7.9% addition to the network.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management plans advances growth 2-3% above industry credit growth, following 26% YoY in Q4 and INR13,600 crore added in FY26, with MSME at 55-60% of the mix and gold and secured retail as enhancers.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Advances grew 26% YoY to INR66,698 crore against FY27 guidance of only 2-3% above industry credit growth, and gross NPA fell to 1.91%, so the guide looks conservative if growth holds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Opex is guided up 15-18% in FY27 against an ROA exit target of 1.65-1.67%, and management flags a 1-2% extra slippage rate in a downturn tied to the US-Iran conflict and oil prices.

rows.label: Credit cost to fall about 50% from the 15-year average of about 0.60%
rows.when: over the next 15 years, individual years may vary
rows.why: FY25 and FY26 credit costs were 0.09% and 0.04%, and management cites AI-based underwriting, but the long-run timing is uncertain and the CEO deferred on steady-state ECL questions.

rows.label: Gold loan price correction risk
rows.why: Gold is about 30% of the book with per-gram lending capped near INR10,000-10,500 versus a peak of INR15,000-16,000, and a 10-15% fall would be cushioned by LTV headroom.

rows.label: CEO handover to R. Vijay Anandh
rows.why: Leadership changed on 1 May 2026, and the retiring MD's future non-executive board role depends on RBI approval.
