532286|2026-03.headline: Jindal Steel Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,647 crores (INR 10,093/t) on ASP up INR 4,743/t QoQ, with FY27 sales guided at 10.5–11 Mt.
532286|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery: consolidated gross revenue rose 28% QoQ to INR 19,399 crores and adjusted EBITDA reached INR 2,647 crores, helped by a rise in HRC and TMT rebar prices and Angul volume ramp-up. Sales volume grew 15% QoQ to 2.62 Mt as the Angul expansion took steelmaking capacity to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa. A one-time impairment of INR 1,433 crores (standalone) and INR 834 crores (consolidated) was booked on the Australian WCL asset after the shaft was closed. Management said the major capex programme is essentially complete and the focus shifts to asset sweating and deleveraging.

segments.name: Steel (India, Angul/Raigarh/Patratu)
segments.commentary: FY26 production 9.25 Mt (+14% YoY) and sales 8.68 Mt (+9% YoY). Q4 production 2.65 Mt (+6% QoQ, +26% YoY) and sales 2.62 Mt (+15% QoQ, +23% YoY). Flat/long mix was 52:48 in Q4 and 49:51 for FY26.

segments.name: Raw materials / overseas mines
segments.commentary: Iron ore sourcing about 60% outside purchases and 40% captive, with pricing described as stable. Mozambique is EBITDA positive, South Africa operating but not EBITDA positive, and Australia is closed with minimal cash burn.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: 1,050 MW Shree Bhoomi power plant commissioned (two 525 MW modules); ramp-up to complete within H1 FY27. Surplus power to be sold but described as not material to financials.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 11–11.5 Mt and sales at 10.5–11 Mt.
Q1 FY27 coking coal prices expected to rise by USD 20–25/t sequentially; iron ore movement of plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month.
Slurry pipeline (Barbil–Angul) to be commissioned in Q1 FY27; savings of about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps up.
Port facility to be commissioned; DRI-2 (2 Mtpa) expected towards end of FY27; PP2 also remaining.
Capex guidance of INR 7,500–10,000 crores for expansion and sustenance capex; remaining programme capex INR 11,545 crores.
Leverage expected to normalise by Q2 FY27; value-added flat mix expected to move from about 50% toward 70%.
Start-up costs of INR 125 crores in Q4 are said to be finished and not recurring.
capex_capacity: Steelmaking capacity raised to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa after BOF2 and BOF3 (3 Mt each) at Angul; iron-making capacity increased by 6.6 Mt through BF2 (4.6 Mt, operational) and DRI2 (2 Mt, under construction).
Cold rolling complex of 1.2 Mtpa commissioned at Angul to support value-added product mix.
Coal pipe conveyor from Utkal C thermal coal mine to Angul is operational; slurry pipeline from Barbil to Angul close to completion.
Total planned capex programme INR 47,043 crores: INR 25,924 crores spent up to FY25 and INR 9,574 crores in FY26, leaving INR 11,545 crores.
Thakurani-A1 iron ore block declared preferred bidder; Saradhapur Jalatap East coal block awarded at end of last year.
Rail rake programme of about 79 rakes: 72 acquired, remainder expected within 2–3 months.
demand_pricing: Management expects India steel demand growth of about 9–9.5% and cites FY26 finished steel consumption of 164.2 Mt (+8% YoY) and Q4 consumption of 44.6 Mt (+10% QoQ).

Realisations lag because the order book mixes spot and contract sales; contracts priced at earlier levels still support Q1 realisations. Management said the market is holding firm despite a slight dip in recent weeks.
Management declined to give a Q1/Q2 realisation upside estimate, saying the market is hard to predict.
Flat sales focus is on infrastructure first, then building and construction, downstream products and automobiles. HSM grades developed for niche products are ramping in the current quarter.
Management said the Q4 sales run rate reflects seasonality, so no large sequential volume pickup is expected.
Safeguard duty on flat steel imports reduced to 11.5% from 12% effective 21 Apr 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will steel and realisation gains continue into Q1, and have contracts been reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts on earlier prices continue and ASP rose strongly in Q4 because of the spot/contract lag; the market is holding firm, though slightly softer recently.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company shift to asset sweating rather than further capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the capex programme is essentially complete and the focus is on sweating assets, with INR 7,500–10,000 crores allocated to expansion and sustenance capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why is value-added share falling and what is the target mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the priority during ramp-up is utilisation, with mix optimisation starting in H1 FY27 and stabilising in H2. Flat mix is about 50:50 today and is expected to reach about 70% flat over time.

qa_highlights.question: What were the start-up costs this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Q4 start-up costs at INR 125 crores, most of which were booked in Q3, and said these will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the slurry pipeline savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slurry savings are about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps. Full utilisation is not expected this year, but per-tonne savings do not depend on utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further write-downs on overseas assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no further write-downs are expected, based on an independent valuation. Australia has minimal cash outflow, and Mozambique is EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: What are the raw material cost moves into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Coking coal is expected to rise USD 20–25/t QoQ in Q1. Iron ore is expected to move by about plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month and is hard to predict.

risks_watch: Value-added product share fell to about 61% from 66% QoQ, and management says mix will move back toward normal levels only over time.
Coking coal cost increase of USD 20–25/t in Q1 FY27 could compress margins if steel prices soften; a dip in steel prices was acknowledged.
FY26 EBITDA per tonne fell to INR 10,482 from INR 11,712 in FY25 even as volume rose.
DRI-2 is due towards end FY27 and PP2 is also pending; slurry pipeline commissioning is due in Q1 FY27.
Leverage (1.66x net debt/EBITDA) is expected to normalise only by Q2 FY27.
Management gave no EBITDA margin or revenue guidance for FY27, only volume guidance.
Overseas mine EC capacity increase is pending with no date given.
532286|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on volumes, demand and the end of the capex cycle, with management repeatedly calling the market healthy. Evasive on pricing, margins, revenue and the timing of DRI-2 and raw material moves, and it referred several questions to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: Our focus is on sweating the assets and getting returns out of them.
I think you are going to see a little bit of movement in the first two quarters of this year and then a stabilization in the second half of the year.
It is a cost. Cost cannot be reversed.

Per-tonne down from INR 11,712 in FY25
Net debt was INR 8,876 crores in FY22

rows.why: Net debt INR 16,019 crore at 1.66x net debt/EBITDA and D/E 0.43x; management guided normalisation by Q2 FY27 as capex winds down.

rows.why: Barbil–Angul slurry pipeline to save about INR 700/t of iron ore (INR 750–1,000/t of steel) as it ramps, with savings not dependent on utilisation.

rows.why: Order book mixes spot and contract sales; contracts priced at earlier levels still support Q1 realisations, but market dipped slightly in recent weeks.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, demand (9–9.5% growth) and the end of the capex cycle, but cautious and evasive on realisations, margins, coking coal and iron ore moves, and DRI-2 timing; analysts pushed on pricing, write-downs and mix.

532286|2026-06.headline: Jindal Steel Q1FY27 consolidated adjusted EBITDA INR 2,667 crore, INR 11,937/ton, with ASP up INR 7,500/ton despite 15% sequential volume drop.
532286|2026-06.overview: Q1FY27 revenue fell about 8% QoQ on a plant maintenance shutdown (BOF refractory change), with sales volume down 15% sequentially. ASP rose about INR 7,500/ton on stronger steel prices and richer mix, and value-added share rose from 61% to 66%. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,667 crore (INR 11,937/ton, up INR 1,843/ton), while PAT was INR 844 crore and finance cost rose to INR 548 crore as Q4FY26 expansion assets entered the P&L. Management guided to net debt/EBITDA below 1.5x in Q2FY27 (Q1: 1.71x) and a sequential cost recovery from the shutdown reversing, with the slurry pipeline targeted for commissioning around August.

segments.name: Flat products
segments.commentary: NSR moved about INR 7,000/ton QoQ higher per management. HRC prices were firm through the quarter, though management cited HRC down about INR 800/ton versus Q1 average in recent pricing.

segments.name: Long products
segments.commentary: NSR moved about INR 4,500/ton QoQ higher per Sandeep Modi. TMT rebar prices fell about INR 8,000 per index in recent weeks on monsoon seasonality, while rails, rounds, specialty angles and quench-and-tempered plates held prices.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume guidance of 10.5-11 million tons maintained; management expects to recover about 300,000 tons of hot metal lost in Q1.
Q2FY27 cost structure expected to improve on no shutdown, operating leverage (about INR 2,000/ton in Q1) not repeating, and coking coal up a further $12-15/ton.
Slurry pipeline (18 MTPA design) expected to commission in first half of August, subject to monsoon; about INR 700/ton iron ore cost benefit from Q2 per management.
Cost reduction campaign targeting at least INR 1,000/ton, mainly electricity, fuel, coke, oxygen and yield (98% to 98.5%).
Angul blast furnace hot metal to ramp from 11,000 t/d to 12,000 t/d in September and 13,000 t/d by December.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 1.5x in Q2FY27.
FY27 capex about INR 8,500 crore; about INR 2,000 crore spent in Q1. Ongoing capex envelope of INR 7,000-10,000 crore per year on value-added products.
capex_capacity: Cumulative expansion spend INR 37,457 crore of announced INR 47,043 crore; FY27 plan about INR 8,500 crore, about INR 2,000 crore spent in Q1.
Crude steel capacity installed 15.6 MTPA; FY27 output expected at about 11-11.5 MT, with 12.5 MT possible via blast furnace readjustment.
Angul: two blast furnaces (BF1 at 10,000 t/d rated, running about 11,000 t/d; BF2 rated 13,000 t/d), one DRI plant (5,000 t/d), EAF and BOF 1/2/3 (BOF 2 commissioned Sep-25, BOF 3 Mar-26).
Raigarh: two blast furnaces at 6,800 t/d combined (100% utilised), 10 DRI plants, three EAFs; Raigarh hot metal cited as 3.6 MT.
Slurry pipeline: 18 MTPA capacity, 60% Fe and 35-40% water; pellet plants of 6 MT existing plus 6 MT under addition, plus a 5 MT sinter plant, to absorb about 17-18 MT/year.
Plate capacity about 2 MT/year going to 2.5 MT; hot strip mill (commissioned FY24) rated 5-5.5 MT of HRC.
demand_pricing: Indian crude steel production down about 6% QoQ to 42 MT and finished steel consumption down about 7% to about 41.5 MT in Q1 on monsoon seasonality.
Management expects construction recovery from end-August after monsoon; HRC firm, TMT weak.
Imports of HRC via advance licences cited as a pressure on commodity flats; management says value-added grades are insulated.
Coking coal: $15/ton further increase expected; blend optimisation and coke imports from Indonesia cited as offsets.
Iron ore prices set largely by NMDC and OMC, which management treats as uncontrollable.
Share of high-EBITDA products targeted to rise; product EBITDA ranges from about INR 7,000 to INR 25,000/ton per management.

qa_highlights.question: What are the new management's key priorities and expansion plans at Angul?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities: utilise 15.6 MT capacity and shift mix to value-added grades; growth funded from earnings at INR 7,000-10,000 crore capex per year, with no commodity capacity additions and no new borrowing to expand.

qa_highlights.question: Current NSR movement and Q2 price outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Flats about INR 7,000/ton higher QoQ and longs about INR 4,500/ton higher QoQ; recent HRC about INR 800/ton lower and TMT about INR 8,000 lower, expected to recover post-monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 volume fall and what is the FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Shutdown was needed to replace BOF refractory after heat life of 9,000-10,000; about 300,000 tons of hot metal lost; FY27 volume guidance of 10.5-11 MT maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of QoQ cost increase of about INR 5,500/ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore about INR 500/ton, Middle East conflict impact $12-13/ton, coking coal about $23/ton, and operating leverage from the shutdown about INR 2,000/ton.

qa_highlights.question: Quantified cost savings over next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least INR 1,000/ton cost reduction; slurry pipeline about INR 700/ton; Vishal Chandak pointed to 18-20% ROCE targets to back-calculate project EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA/ton not rising with value-added share?
qa_highlights.answer: Product-wise EBITDA is not disclosed; about 50% of portfolio is high-EBITDA, with aim to convert 1.5-2 MT of low-EBITDA volume to value-added.

qa_highlights.question: Concerns about frequent senior management changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said eight new board-level faces were brought in, including CFO, CHRO and VP HR; about 1,800-2,000 upper-middle managers are stable.

risks_watch: Long product (TMT) price correction and monsoon-driven demand weakness; timing of post-monsoon recovery.
Coking coal and Middle East-related input cost pressure, with $12-15/ton further coking coal increase expected in Q2.
Slurry pipeline commissioning slippage beyond August due to monsoon or trials.
Blast furnace ramp to 12,000 t/d in September and 13,000 t/d by December; Q1 rain-related electrical grid failure cited.
Net debt/EBITDA reaching below 1.5x in Q2FY27 from 1.71x.
Rising finance and depreciation costs from newly capitalised assets.
Jharkhand MoU (2.5-2.7 MT blast furnace) conditional on iron ore block allocation; no investment committed.
Senior management turnover, with eight new senior appointments.

Several answers were deflected or qualified (for example, on cost savings quantification and slurry timing), and management repeatedly stressed uncontrollable input costs.

rows.why: Q1 volume fell about 15% QoQ on the BOF refractory shutdown, about 300,000 t of hot metal is to be recovered, and operating leverage of about INR 2,000/ton does not repeat in Q2.

532286|2026-09.headline: Jindal Steel posted record Q2 FY27 gross revenue of INR 19,448 crore (+44% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR 2,504 crore (+34% YoY) on 2.38 MT sales.
532286|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly gross revenue of INR 19,448 crore and record sales volume of 2.38 million tons, with domestic sales about 92% of volume. Adjusted EBITDA rose 34% YoY to INR 2,504 crore, but adjusted EBITDA per ton of INR 10,529 was sequentially lower on higher raw material, power, fuel and freight costs. Net debt fell to INR 14,786 crore and net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 1.51x from 1.71x. Management guided to 11 MT gross steel output in FY27 with H2 net steel of about 6 MT, and said the switch from propane to coal-gas syngas protected productivity during the West Asia supply disruption.

financial_highlights.change: down INR 1,141 crore from INR 15,927 crore in Q1

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,228 crore in Q2; INR 3,187 crore in H1

financial_highlights.change: apples-to-apples basis; management says over 65% when excluding low-priced TMT

segments.name: Flat products (HRC and plates)
segments.commentary: Plates production exceeds 220,000 tons per month across both locations; management targets a 65:35 flat-to-long mix, up from about 60:40 currently. Hot-rolled coil output is being shifted to value-added grades such as high and medium carbon.

segments.name: TMT / long products
segments.commentary: TMT output was cut to about 120,000 tons per month from 220,000 tons earlier, with volume redirected to plates and HRC. TMT now goes mainly to major projects.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports run at about 100,000 tons per month, mainly HRC, plates, with some rails and structurals.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Pellet output is about 33,000 tons per day (Barbil 18,000-20,000 and Angul 14,000), all consumed in-house. A new pellet plant is targeted for commercial production by June 2027.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: JSOL (100% subsidiary) turnover and EBITDA are rising as major projects commission; Mozambique coal EBITDA improved YoY on better coal prices.

guidance_outlook: Net steel production target of about 6 MT in H2 FY27 (about 3 MT per quarter, planned at 0.96 MT per month); gross steel about 11 MT for FY27.
Record production expected in Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), with Q4 to exceed Q3.
FY27 sales volume guidance lower end of about 10.5 MT; management says 9-9.5 lakh saleable tons per month is needed and that they are comfortable.
Coking coal cost increase of USD 20-25/ton expected for Q3; a possible further USD 20/ton from diesel and oil if the West Asia conflict prolongs.
Slurry pipeline (192 km, Barbil to Angul) commissioned; commercial supply from about 2-3 days from 23 Oct, saving about INR 700/ton on freight at 20,000 tons per day.
Blast furnace at Angul (about 10,000 tons per day) to ramp to 10,500 in about 7 days, 11,000 in November and 12,000 in December.
Coal gasifier expansion (3 more gasifiers, 35,000 NM3/hr each) and DRI-2 (2 MT) targeted for commissioning by June 2027.
Utkal B2 coal mine clearance expected in FY27; Roida iron ore mine restart expected by about December 2026 to January 2027.
Annual growth capex guided at INR 7,500-10,000 crore; net debt-to-EBITDA to stay below 1.5x through the cycle.
capex_capacity: Blast furnace at Angul ramping to about 10,000 tons per day, targeting 12,000 tons per day by December 2026.
Slurry pipeline: 192 km, commissioned, first iron slurry dispatched, continuous operation planned.
Captive coal mines: about 15 MT total capacity across Raigarh and Angul; captive coal meets about 50-55% of requirement, targeted at 65-70%. Gare Palma about 4 MT.
Kasia iron ore mine at 22,000 tons per day, ramping to 30,000 tons per day.
Coal gasification: 3 additional gasifiers (105,000 NM3/hr combined), over 95% indigenous content, commissioning by June 2027.
Total capex plan of about INR 47,000 crore with INR 8,000-9,000 crore remaining, including DRI-2 and performance-linked payments.
demand_pricing: Average HRC moved from INR 51,000 to INR 60,000/ton during Q2; TMT from INR 52,000 to INR 59,000/ton; structurals INR 60,000-65,000; rails above INR 70,000.
Spot prices around INR 60,000/ton for HRC and TMT as of late October.
Coking coal cost rose about USD 12-15/ton in Q2, within prior guidance; management says prices are stable now.
Propane to coal-gas switch saves about INR 70/kg in reheating furnaces (propane about INR 100/kg vs syngas about INR 30/kg). Management says the company will not revert to propane.
Q2 is seasonally weak for TMT; Q3 expected to be stronger on festive-season construction demand.
Europe steel deficit of about 28 MT cited; EU CBAM and quota remain open issues for exports.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4.8 MT H1 production run-rate achievable and will flat mix stay at 70:30 in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of about 3 MT per quarter; mix target is 65:35 flat to long, not 70:30, to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How much freight saving does the slurry pipeline give, and any extra cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 700/ton on freight with no additional cost; around 500 of 700 daily iron ore trucks to be removed.

qa_highlights.question: Coking coal and West Asia cost impact for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Coking coal up USD 20-25/ton expected in Q3 by Sandeep Modi; West Asia impact on fuel about USD 4-5/ton, steady. Another USD 20/ton possible if conflict prolongs.

qa_highlights.question: Water availability from Brahmani for Angul at higher volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Only 31 MLD being used against 59.1 MLD sanctioned; usage to fall at least 15% next year as Barbil slurry supplies water.

qa_highlights.question: Power sales and their EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said power sales are miniscule relative to the INR 1 lakh crore revenue ambition; no figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Pellet plant and merchant pellet sales?
qa_highlights.answer: No merchant pellet sales now; all 33,000 tons/day consumed in-house. New pellet plant commercial production by June 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation and spot price detail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined exact spot prices, citing policy; gave approximate ranges as above.

risks_watch: Coking coal and diesel cost pressure from the West Asia and Russia-Ukraine supply disruptions; management flagged possible USD 20-25/ton in Q3.
Execution on the Angul blast furnace ramp, Roida mine right-of-way, and Utkal B2 approvals.
Possible delays to DRI-2 and coal gasifiers, which management says could slip from June 2027 due to imported equipment.
Other expenses rose about 13% QoQ on freight and power/fuel; management expects normalisation in Q3.
Water availability at Angul given the Brahmani river reservoir level, though management says consumption will be lower.
EU quota and CBAM outcomes that determine export access.
532286|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and expansive on production ramp-up, cost savings and balance sheet, with management repeatedly describing the company as cash surplus. Evasive on exact ASP, spot prices, power sales and subsidiary-level numbers, which it declined to quantify on the call.
key_quotes: So, we are quite confident that we'll be in a position to achieve these 3 million tons per quarter.
And INR 700 per ton will be saving on freight and no additional expenses.
So, we don't want to invest money unless we reach to our 100% capacity utilization.
So, the steel scenario is very good. I think it is now around 10% Y-o-Y basis, there's a growth.

rows.why: Angul blast furnace ramping from about 10,000 to 12,000 tpd by December 2026 (about 20% debottlenecking), with DRI-2 (2 MT) and 3 gasifiers targeted for June 2027, though management flagged possible slippage from imported equipment.

tone.note: Management was confident on the blast furnace ramp, slurry freight savings and the balance sheet, but cautious on coking coal cost headwinds and evasive on exact ASP, spot prices, power sales and subsidiary numbers; analysts pushed on the H1 run-rate, flat mix and water availability at Angul.

532300|2026-03.headline: Wockhardt FY26 revenue INR3,373 crore, EBITDA about INR630 crore (~51% growth); Zaynich US FDA approval is the key catalyst, with peak sales guided at $1.5-2 billion globally.
532300|2026-03.overview: Management hosted an investor meet on 4 June 2026 (disclosed 11 June) after the US FDA approval of Zaynich (cefepime-zidebactam), described as the first Indian-discovered research product approved by the FDA. FY26 revenue was INR3,373 crore, EBITDA about INR630 crore (margin about 18.6%, up from about 5.4% three years earlier) and profit before tax INR238 crore. Management framed the next phase as scaling growth: US launch of Zaynich via an operationally light model, India and emerging-market launches, and biosimilar diabetes expansion. Most numbers were given verbally; no quarterly figures or formal guidance were disclosed in the presentation.

segments.name: Pharma core (India, UK, Ireland)
segments.commentary: About 75% of business; UK is top-five with 18% covered-market share and focuses on specialty injectables. India driven by diabetes, orthopedics, pain and regenerative medicine (Emrok, Miqnaf).

segments.name: Biosimilars / biotech (diabetes)
segments.commentary: Grew 27% in FY26; human insulin output scaled 2x and glargine 1.5x. Two products commercialised, five in pipeline (aspart, RN 30/70, degludec, degludec aspart, semaglutide); registered in 30 emerging markets.

segments.name: Novel antibiotics (Zaynich, Emrok, Miqnaf, Odrate)
segments.commentary: Specialty (biosimilars plus novel antibiotics) is 23% of business. Zaynich has US FDA and CDSCO India approvals; US launch planned with leadership hired and a commercial operating partner; European approval expected by end of calendar 2026.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: 28% of turnover, growing 35%, supported by partnerships in Brazil, Thailand, Algeria and Malaysia. Plans to launch Zaynich in seven to eight high-carbapenem-resistance markets within 18 to 24 months.

guidance_outlook: Zaynich global peak sales of $1.5-2 billion per year, with US roughly 40% of global revenue; country-wise split not given.
Revenue ramp expected to be slow initially (hockey-stick pattern), with breakeven in 12 to 18 months in the Zaynich business; first 12-18 months may see a slight loss, per the Chairman.
Zaynich US price expected at roughly $1,200-1,500 per day, with India pricing about 75-80% below US; Europe and US pricing described as price-neutral versus existing antibiotics.
Long-term target of about 20-25% share of resistant cases globally; India possibly higher.
Biosimilar business expected to double in 24-36 months; capacity to double in 12-15 months; five pipeline products to launch about two years out.
Capex of INR200-300 crore over next three years, primarily for biologicals capacity; R&D spend to stay at similar percentage of sales.
Foviscu DCGI filing expected in two to three months; approval timing not predictable. Odrate is about four years away and Phase 2 waiver not expected.
capex_capacity: Planned capex of INR200-300 crore over the next three years, mainly for biologicals capacity.
Biosimilar capacity to double within 12-15 months.

Zaynich manufacturing: US supply from an FDA-approved European site; India supply from Indian facility; emerging markets to be supplied from either India or Europe depending on timelines (Europe could save six to nine months).
Company has 11 manufacturing facilities and two R&D centres in-house.
Management said US, Europe and emerging markets filings are submitted or in progress, with European approval expected by end of 2026.
demand_pricing: US cUTI is the largest of about 1.2 million US gram-negative hospital infections (about 600,000 cUTI cases); management cited about 20-25% readmission rate for cUTI.
India: about 600,000-700,000 gram-negative infection patients, with 35-45% estimated carbapenem resistance (ICMR surveillance caveated by regional variation).
Phase 3 vs meropenem: composite cure rate 96.8%, about 20% higher than meropenem per management.
Management said new anti-infectives in the US market total about $1 billion; the company does not plan to create new demand but to take share, with price neutrality.
Competition: cefiderocol (Fetroja) cited as the closest competitor; management claimed Zaynich has a better efficacy and safety profile, without numerical head-to-head data.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue from Zaynich over the next 6 to 24 months, and capex and commercial costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman expects slow initial revenue growth, a hockey-stick curve after 12-18 months, INR200-300 crore capex over three years, and no capex for sales build-out, only revenue cost. Breakeven expected in 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Does Zaynich qualify for the 10% PLI and what is the China strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Government funding recognised but immaterial versus R&D spend. China: Chinese patients in trial were insufficient; a small China study is ongoing and a partner may be sought.

qa_highlights.question: Will Zaynich be made in Europe for the US and in India for emerging markets?
qa_highlights.answer: US supply from an FDA-inspected European site as a de-risking step; India supply from India; emerging markets from India or Europe depending on timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Wockhardt exit US generics and will it re-enter?
qa_highlights.answer: US generics were about 5% of the portfolio and loss-making, amid the 2012-13 FDA import alert. Management said it is re-entering with innovative products sourced from European manufacturers, with India production for India.

qa_highlights.question: Patent life and exclusivity for Zaynich, Emrok and Miqnaf?
qa_highlights.answer: Zaynich patent runs to 2038 in India with further filings planned; Miqnaf patent to early 2033 in India. QIDP status gives five extra years in US; minimum 10-year market exclusivity in US and Western markets.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and patient targets for FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: US price about $1,200-1,500 per day, typically $10,000-15,000 per course; India priced about 75-80% below US. Long-term share of 20-25% of resistant cases, with no FY28-29 patient numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Peak sales of Zaynich?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $1.5-2 billion per year globally at peak, not cumulative, with US around 40% of global revenue.

risks_watch: Commercial execution: a new US sales model for antibiotics with a commercial operating partner, 6,000 US hospitals to segment, and a first-time anti-infective launch for the company.
Losses or breakeven in the first 12-18 months from US launch costs; Chairman's comments on profitability were clarified as Zaynich-only.
Regulatory timing: European approval expected by end-2026, emerging market filings to follow; DCGI approval for Foviscu not predictable.
Label scope: US approval is for cUTI; HAP/VAP and other indications need a further trial, so off-label use is a question.
Zaynich Phase 2 waiver for the aztreonam combination (Odrate) not expected; Odrate timing about four years.
Hospital segment profitability and ROCE targets were not answered (hospitals deemed out of scope; ROCE question deflected).
532300|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on Zaynich and the R&D pipeline, with forward-looking claims (peak sales, market share) given without detailed assumptions. Evasive or deflective on ROCE, hospitals, Foviscu timing and China specifics, and on country-wise revenue split.
key_quotes: Wockhardt, as you know, in the last few days, is now the first Indian company to have an Indian research product approved with the US FDA, Zaynich.
So, it is in your financial terms you say investment, I mean, asset-light and capital-heavy.
We will stick to only antibiotic research for next 10 years.
Peak sales per year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management guided biosimilar capacity to double within 12-15 months, with human insulin output already scaled 2x and glargine 1.5x, backed by INR200-300 crore capex over three years.

rows.why: Biosimilar and biotech grew 27% in FY26 and emerging markets (28% of turnover) are growing 35%, with Zaynich US launch planned, though Zaynich revenue ramp is expected to be slow initially (hockey-stick after 12-18 months).

rows.why: Capex of INR200-300 crore over three years, mainly biologicals, is already firmly planned; utilisation was not disclosed, so further capex beyond this is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue or margin guidance for FY27 was given, and the Zaynich peak sales of $1.5-2 billion are long-dated, so an upgrade depends on early US launch traction that has not yet been reported.

rows.why: Execution risk is high: first-time anti-infective launch in the US via a commercial partner, a 6,000-hospital segmentation task, Foviscu DCGI timing not predictable, and an expected Zaynich loss in the first 12-18 months.

rows.when: Zaynich US launch now; European approval by end-2026; five b
rows.why: Zaynich has US FDA and CDSCO approvals with leadership hired and a commercial partner in place; European approval is expected by end of calendar 2026, and emerging-market launches in seven to eight markets are planned within 18-24 months.

rows.label: Zaynich emerging-market launches in 7-8 high-CRE markets
rows.why: Management plans launches in seven to eight high carbapenem-resistance markets, with emerging markets already 28% of turnover growing 35% and partnerships in Brazil, Thailand, Algeria and Malaysia.

rows.label: Biosimilar business doubling
rows.why: Management expects the biosimilar business to double in 24-36 months after growing 27% in FY26, with 2 products commercialised and 5 in the pipeline registered in 30 emerging markets.

rows.label: Foviscu DCGI approval
rows.when: filing in 2-3 months; approval timing unpredictable
rows.why: Filing is expected in two to three months, but management would not predict approval timing, so this is a binary timing risk.

tone.note: Management was confident on Zaynich peak sales of $1.5-2 billion, the biosimilar doubling and the 20-25% resistant-case share, but was evasive on ROCE, hospitals, Foviscu timing, China and the country-wise revenue split, while analysts pressed on Zaynich revenue, losses and capex.

532305|2026-06.headline: Ind-Swift Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 2.85x YoY to ₹33.32 crore, a 17.91% margin, with management guiding to 20%+ from Q3.
532305|2026-06.overview: Operating income grew 21.16% YoY to ₹186.08 crore and operating EBITDA reached ₹33.32 crore (17.91% margin, up 1258 bps). PAT excluding exceptional items was ₹24.68 crore (13.26% margin vs 4.99%). Management attributed the step-up to exit of litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business after the merger, and to a higher own-brand export mix. CDMO contracts with Viatris, Manx and Arrotex were commercialised in the quarter but contributed only about ₹5-6 crore so far, with ramp-up expected from Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 export sales of about ₹750 crore and ₹1200 crore revenue by FY29, and declined to revise targets at this stage.

segments.name: Export own-brands
segments.commentary: 57.20% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 48% in Q1 FY26; management cites this mix shift as a key margin driver. Export gross margin was stated at about 55%.

segments.name: Export contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.64% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 29% a year earlier. Viatris, Manx and Arrotex partnerships commercialised in the quarter, with about ₹5-6 crore booked from Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) so far.

segments.name: Domestic segments
segments.commentary: Branded generics 6.41%, ethical 6.14% and domestic contract manufacturing 3.61% of Q1 FY27 sales, all lower than a year ago. Management describes these as a stable cash-generation base; domestic sales are seasonal.

segments.name: Product portfolio
segments.commentary: Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin was about ₹25 crore in Q1 FY27 per management, partnered with Tiffen-Becker. FY26 revenue: Atorvastatin ₹85.50 crore, Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin ₹80.78 crore, Fexofenadine ₹74.32 crore, Quetiapine ₹19.75 crore, Famciclovir ₹18.64 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 export sales target of about ₹750 crore, with roughly 45% from CDMO (per management).

FY29 revenue target of ₹1200 crore; management said it is not revising this yet and will revisit by year-end. Mentioned FY27 expectation of about ₹900 crore and a longer-term aspiration of ₹1500 crore revenue and ~₹200 crore net profit by FY30.
EBITDA margin of 18% described as sustainable; management expects to move above 20% from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally targeted), potentially 21-22% with sequential sales growth.
Viatris CDMO volumes expected to double in Q2 versus Q1; Arrotex Macrogol push expected in Q2, and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules to contribute in Q3-Q4.
Medium-term growth of 20-25% CAGR referenced, with EBITDA margins above 18% (management answered 'yes').
Dossiers to reach 400+ additions, taking the total from 2,100 to about 2,500 by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: About ₹250 crore of cash to be deployed in capex over roughly 2 to 2.5 years across a new warehouse, capacity enhancement at the existing facility, and the Jammu facility (EU-GMP/PIC/S audit under way).
Samba facility upgrade to EU-GMP and PIC/S standards in progress as planned.
Capacity utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules about 70% in Q1 per management; management expects 90% utilisation of planned FY29 capacity over time.
Capex for a potential new CDMO customer deal estimated at ₹50-75 crore, with revenue of ₹150+ crore expected.
R&D working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29; capex to follow only after filings are completed. New R&D land bought in Panchkula area.
demand_pricing: CDMO economics: Viatris paid about USD 2 million for development work, to be reimbursed through orders.
Selection criteria for new products include a minimum 50-55% gross margin and customer confidence in R&D delivery. Candidate molecules include Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin and Empagliflozin.
Tiffen-Becker arrangement: transfer-priced supply with about 43% of the customer's margin shared with Ind-Swift.
Management expects no dearth of capacity for the planned growth; new partnerships under discussion with 3-4 existing overseas customers, not expected to contribute this year.

qa_highlights.question: What was the CDMO contribution in Q1 and what growth to expect from the Viatris partnership over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Gagan Aggarwal said Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) booked only about ₹5-6 crore in Q1, with growth reflecting in Q2 and Q3. He said about ₹100-130 crore is expected from these two products, not the full ₹200 crore in year one, and that it would build over about two years.

qa_highlights.question: What are export margins for CDMO and own-brands, and how will the ₹250 crore cash and Synthimed stake be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Export gross margin is about 55%. The ₹250 crore cash will be deployed as capex over about 2.5 years (warehouse, existing capacity, Jammu). No plans to divest the Synthimed stake this year; Synthimed budgeted EBITDA is about ₹750 crore and Q1 results are on track.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18% EBITDA margin sustainable, and could it rise further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 18% is fully sustainable and could reach 21-22% if sales grow quarter on quarter. It denied calling Q1 a turnaround, citing litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business for about 1.5 years that are now over.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY29 revenue guidance of ₹1200 crore not being raised, and when does growth come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not revise at this stage and will revisit by year-end. Growth is H2-weighted via Arrotex Macrogol in Q2 and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules in Q3-Q4. FY27 expectation is about ₹900 crore, with export sales of about ₹750 crore, roughly 45% from CDMO.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the API business sold and what R&D capability was retained?
qa_highlights.answer: The API business was sold to Synthimed in FY24 for net about ₹2000-2100 crore, used to repay group debt of about ₹1250-1300 crore. Retained R&D in Panchkula handles regulatory compliance, tech transfer and global filings, with new land bought for a further R&D facility.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and will there be a capacity shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Ibuprofen and granules ran at about 70% in Q1 on pilot batches. Management expects 90% utilisation of the FY29 plan over time and sees no capacity dearth. Capex for new molecules will follow only after filings are complete.

risks_watch: CDMO ramp-up timing: Viatris volumes are guided to double in Q2 from a ₹5-6 crore base, and Arrotex Macrogol and Ibuprofen and granules contributions depend on Q2-Q4 execution.
Margin trajectory: management targets above 20% EBITDA margin from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally), against 17.91% in Q1; a shortfall would challenge the 21-22% view.
Capacity and capex: ₹250 crore capex over about 2-2.5 years, Jammu and Samba EU-GMP/PIC/S audits in progress, and the new CDMO deal needs ₹50-75 crore capex; delays could cap FY28-29 revenue.
Revenue guidance: FY27 about ₹900 crore and FY29 ₹1200 crore; management says it will revisit by year-end, so the next quarter's run-rate matters.
Synthimed stake: ~7.8% holding, no divestment planned this year, tag-along right on any PE exit; monetisation timing is open.
Customer concentration and unnamed partners: two new overseas CDMO deals and 3-4 existing customers are under discussion but not named; 'the war' is cited as slowing signings.
Several questions were deferred (market size, Q1 capacity utilisation, new registrations, packaging differentiation), so follow-ups via IR are pending.
key_quotes: Yes, yes, 18% is fully sustainable and we plan if the sales we are able to increase quarter-on-quarter they might go up to 21 to 22%.
Sir, not at this stage. Maybe after if we are able to achieve our, overachieve our results this financial year, we may revise this.
So that ₹250 crores will be deployed in capex over a period of 2.5 years approx.
We don't want to spend a single penny in R&D before we sign off any agreement with our customers.
532305|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and the export mix, stating 18% EBITDA margin is fully sustainable and describing the quarter as an excellent start. Cautious on guidance, declining to revise the ₹1200 crore FY29 target and avoiding firm commitments on the 20% margin timing, the new partnerships and the CDMO revenue split. Evasive on several detailed questions, including market size, Q1 capacity utilisation, partner names and new registrations, which were deferred to follow-up.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin 17.91% (up from 5.33%) with own-brand exports at 57.20% of sales vs 48%, export gross margin ~55%, and management guiding above 20% from Q3 FY27 and 21-22% if sales grow sequentially; not yet proven and Q1 margin was helped by exit of litigation and other costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About ₹250 cr capex over 2-2.5 years for new warehouse, existing-facility capacity enhancement and Jammu, plus a ₹50-75 cr capex for a potential new CDMO deal, but the capacity additions are not dated to a specific quarter and utilisation is only ~70%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to ~₹900 cr and export sales ~₹750 cr (~45% CDMO), with Viatris volumes guided to double in Q2 from a ₹5-6 cr base and Arrotex Macrogol in Q2, but Q1 CDMO contribution was small and FY27 implies a step-up from ₹186 cr in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex already raised to ~₹250 cr and a ₹50-75 cr CDMO-specific capex is pending a new customer deal, but Ibuprofen/granules utilisation is ~70% and management said no capacity dearth, so a fresh board-level capex is conditional on signing new deals.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to revise FY29 ₹1200 cr target and will revisit only by year-end; the CDMO revenue split and partner signings are still unconfirmed, with only ₹5-6 cr CDMO booked in Q1.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: CDMO ramp is back-end loaded (Ibuprofen/Clarithromycin in Q3-Q4, ~₹100-130 cr from Viatris over two years vs ₹200 cr year-one expectation) and 'the war' is cited as slowing new signings, so FY27 ₹900 cr could slip if Q2-Q3 run-rate lags.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Arrotex Macrogol push in Q2, Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules in Q3-Q4, and 5-6 R&D molecules for FY27-29 (Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin, Empagliflozin candidates) with dossiers rising from 2,100 to ~2,500 by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Viatris CDMO volume doubling in Q2
rows.why: Viatris volumes guided to double in Q2 from ₹5-6 cr booked in Q1, with Viatris CDMO expected to contribute ~₹100-130 cr over about two years.

rows.label: New overseas CDMO partnerships
rows.when: not expected to contribute this year
rows.why: Two new overseas CDMO deals and partnerships with 3-4 existing customers are under discussion, unnamed, and management said they are not expected to contribute this year.

rows.label: Synthimed stake monetisation
rows.why: Stake ~7.8%; management said no divestment planned this year, though tag-along right exists on any PE exit and Synthimed budgeted EBITDA ~₹750 cr.
